title: fix(import): refuse a STEP item with no unit context in a degree file
body:
## What changed

- `crates/kernel/src/step_units_guard.rs` gets `UnlistedAngles`. It finds the first stated plane angle unit that is not the radian. It also finds the items that a representation with a context lists, and the pieces of those solids.
- `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs` (`read_guarded`) uses it after the topology read:
  - A built solid with no unit context is refused when the file states a non-radian angle unit.
  - For an item that failed to read, the unit reason replaces the read message. The wrong angle unit is the first cause of the failure.
- A file that states only the radian, or no angle unit, keeps such an item.
- The refusal names the item and the angle unit, for example: `no representation gives it a unit context, so its angles would be read in radians, but the file states plane angle unit #13, which is not the radian`.

## Cause

The pinned reader gives a solid item that no representation lists the default units: 1 mm per length unit and 1 radian per angle unit. Nothing checked the angle default. In a degree file, the reader read the angles of that item in radians, without a warning.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/kernel/tests/step_short_units.rs`:

- `unlisted_item_in_a_degree_file_is_refused_by_name`: the degree cone fixture with the solid #16 not listed. Red before the fix: the item was refused for an edge gap (`face #40: an edge lies 8.32 mm off the face's surface`), not for its unit.
- `unlisted_item_that_reads_cleanly_is_refused_by_name`: the same cone with a semi-angle that reads cleanly in radians. Without the fix it imports as a wrong solid (volume 3196.7 mm^3, no warning).
- `unlisted_item_in_a_radian_file_is_kept`: control. A millimetre and radian cube with no context imports as a 1 mm cube.

Mutation results:

- Solid filter disabled: `unlisted_item_that_reads_cleanly_is_refused_by_name` is red (the wrong cone imports). Restored: green.
- Failure message mapping removed: `unlisted_item_in_a_degree_file_is_refused_by_name` is red. Restored: green.
- Radian rule removed (each angle unit counts as non-radian): `unlisted_item_in_a_radian_file_is_kept` is red. Restored: green.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (10 steps, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- A file with an unlisted surface model (a sheet) in a degree file. The same filter covers it, because the reader gives sheets in `read.solids`.
- The length unit of an item with no context. PR #2927 (issue #2919) owns that rule.
- The heavy lanes. This change does not touch a heavy test.

## Overlaps

- PR #2927 touches the same function, `read_guarded` in `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs`, but different lines (it edits the solid build loop). This PR adds lines before the failure loop. PR #2927 has `needs-rework` and `conflicts`, so this PR does not stack on it. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: STEP import refuses, by name, a solid item with no unit context when the file states a plane angle unit that is not the radian, so its angles are no longer read in radians without a warning.

Fixes #3079

title: fix(sim): judge a reduced-accuracy model at its own chord error, up to 0.02 mm
body:
## What changed

- **The law** (`crates/sim/src/verify/excess.rs`). `excess_floor` reads a model's chord error `c` in three ranges:
  - `c` up to `DEV_TOL` (0.01 mm): the whole excess is taken (#864, no change).
  - `c` from 0.01 mm to `WIDE_CHORD_LIMIT` (0.02 mm): only the promised chord (0.005 mm) is taken. The program verdict is then read at the model's own chord error.
  - `c` over 0.02 mm: the whole excess is taken, so nothing is left. The operation is refused by name.
- `WIDE_CHORD_LIMIT` is a constant. No file, facet budget or vouch can raise it.
- A tolerance is never made larger than the law's own tolerance.
- **Collision bands** grow by the whole excess (`verify::band_growth`). The widening is never given to a band.
- **Strict readers** keep #864's law (`verify::strict_floor`, `fidelity_law::tightened_strict`):
  - the turning margin, the lathe axial-hole tolerance and `revolve::gouge_tol_on`;
  - the rotary field allowances;
  - the probe stylus slack.

  The program gate reads the strict law for these kinds (`fidelity_law::widens`).
- **Header note.** `ProgramId` has `notes`. The engine writes each note through the script's `onComment`, after `onOpen`. `document_program_id` fills the notes from `fidelity_note::program_notes`. Example: `Reduced accuracy: model brick was checked to 0.019 mm, not 0.010 mm`.
- **Notes in plain words.** The model summary, the MCP `facts` note and the #2994 import note (`step::loosened_consequence`) say the same fact.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2996-wide-verdict.md`. It gives the rule for each direction, each reader, what the user loses, and what was dropped.

## Cause

The #864 law took the whole excess from each tolerance. At a chord of 0.02 mm the excess is 0.015 mm. That is more than `DEV_TOL`, so no tolerance was left. Each finishing operation on such a model was refused at the post.

## Tests

New pins:
- `crates/app/tests/model_fidelity_wide.rs`:
  - `a_model_just_under_the_limit_posts_an_exact_finish_with_a_header_note` (0.019 mm).
  - `a_model_just_over_the_limit_is_refused_by_name` (0.021 mm).
  - `a_real_gouge_deeper_than_the_verdict_tolerance_still_blocks_a_widened_model` (0.02 mm under the face).
  - `the_edge_gap_step_file_opened_at_reduced_accuracy_posts_a_face_with_the_note` (the #2994 fixture `edge_gap_018_stated_010.step`).
  - `a_full_fidelity_model_and_a_mild_one_say_nothing_new`.
- `crates/sim/tests/model_excess.rs`: `past_dev_tol_up_to_the_limit_only_the_promised_chord_is_taken`, `a_cut_deeper_than_the_widened_tolerance_into_a_convex_wall_is_still_convicted`.
- `crates/app/tests/coarse_laws.rs`: a rotary op on a 0.019 mm model is still refused by name.

Mutation checks (each restored after):
1. `excess_floor` takes the whole excess again: 2 app pins and 2 sim pins go red.
2. `band_growth` reads the widened tolerance: `past_dev_tol_...` and `full_fidelity_grows_nothing` go red.
3. The engine writes no notes: the header pin goes red.
4. Every kind widens: the rotary pin goes red.

Pins changed on purpose (the old formula for a chord past `DEV_TOL`): `model_fidelity` (TIGHT), `fidelity_copies`, `coarse_probe_plasma` (plasma kerf), `import_step_edge_gap` (note text), and the sim `model_excess`, `coarse_collision` and `boundary_arc_walls`. The `coarse_collision` loops now use an excess past the limit. An excess of 0.01 mm is now judged, and those cases convict.

Full-fidelity pins: unchanged and green.

Gate:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the head before the main merge: 254 steps, 2 red. Both were pins of the old formula, fixed in 5eef00704.
- On the final head, the gate ran steps 1-128 (post, kernel, sim, motion) green. At step 129 (app build), the gate's sccache wrapper hung on `ring`'s `curve25519.c` two times. I stopped it.
- I then ran the same binaries with plain cargo (`env -u RUSTC_WRAPPER`): all 601 `camcraft-app` lib and test binaries, and the 6 ui binaries that the gate selects. All green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) did not run. The change reaches them. This PR is not ready until they run.
- No UI run. The model page shows the new sentence through `model_fidelity::summary`.
- The bundled posts write the header note in their own `onComment` form. Only the default mill post is pinned.
- Turning, rotary and probe kinds on a widened model are still refused. To judge them needs a separate collision allowance in those laws.
- `model_fidelity.rs` is now 433 lines (it was 414 on main).

## Overlaps

Each of these touches the same file, in a different function. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3037: `post/engine.rs` and `post/js_host.rs` (output budget, next to `ProgramId`).
- #2893: `post/engine.rs` (fine-bore cycle arm).
- #2836, #2714: `operation/probe_op.rs` (`stylus_cutter`).

Changelog: A model opened at reduced accuracy (a chord error up to 0.02 mm) is now judged at its own accuracy, not refused: a finishing operation posts, and the program header and the model page name the tolerance that the checks used. Collision checks still allow for the whole deviation.

Effort: max (no escalation).

Fixes #2996

title: fix(sim): judge the first traverse of the rotary, multi-axis and cross-drill kinds
body:
Stacked on #2997. GitHub cannot base a PR on a fork branch, so the diff below also shows the commits of #2997 (branch `mkinney:issue/2987-table-tilted-first-traverse`, merged here at 05c9e56f2). Merge #2997 first. Then this PR takes `git merge origin/main` and only its own commits stay.

## What changed

After a tool change the post sends Z, then X/Y at that height, then the block with the rotary words (`fanuc.cps` `xyFirst`, `traverseZ`, `onRapid`). The Z of that traverse is the higher of the clearance height and the start. The #2901 law did not judge the rotary, multi-axis and cross-drill kinds. Now each kind has a law or a named refusal:

- **Rotary kinds** (Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset): the new law `sim::verify::first_traverse_low_swept`.
  - The rotary words come after the X/Y traverse, so the law reads the work swept through a full turn about the fitted axis. It reads the stock and part points, and the steel that turns with the work (a chuck), at its corners.
  - It reads the fixed steel (table, tailstock) at its machine-frame top.
  - It reads the start at its machine height over the axis line, lifted to the clearance height.
  - The mounted machine selects the law. A machine whose work tilts gets the swept law. A machine whose head tilts gets the tip law. An unstated or mixed machine gets both laws.
  - When no axis can be fitted, generation is refused by name.
- **Multi-axis kinds** (5-Axis Contour, 5-Axis Parallel, Swarf, Advanced Swarf, Multi-Axis Rough, 5-Axis Flow, Multi-Axis Contour): the #2901 law on the tip in the part frame, at the post's traverse height.
- **Cross drill on a mill**: generation refuses it by name before any move ("cross holes are live-tooling work"). A test pins this refusal.
- **Cross drill on a lathe or a mill-turn**: this law does not judge it. The decision file records the limit. Refs #3077, which owns the gap.
- **Verdict**: the same blocking `Warning::FirstTraverseLow`. The post gate, the UI, MCP and the warned moves do not change.
- **Cache**: the op stamp of these kinds gets one more word (`first-traverse-2965`). Such a cache reads Stale once. The salt stays at v4, so no other stamp moves.

Dropped options: a reading at the start angle only (the rotary words come after the traverse); a sweep for the multi-axis kinds (no axis line is stated for them); a blanket refusal; a new `Warning` variant; a salt bump to v5 for all kinds. The decision file has the reasons: `docs/decisions/2965-first-traverse-rotary.md`.

## Examples (stamp-only regeneration, accepted by the maintainer)

- `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` (Journal) and `examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj` (Swarf1) were regenerated. Only the operation `stamp` field of each file changes (`git diff --word-diff`).
- Every `.nc` file and every golden is byte-identical.
- The `WRITE_GOLDEN` run also rewrote the last digit of 7 A words in `first-continuous-4axis-part.nc`. That change was discarded, and the suite passes with the committed program. #3063 owns that drift.

## Tests

- New, `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_rotary.rs`:
  - `a_rotary_kind_reads_its_square_bar_swept_about_the_axis`
  - `a_5_axis_kind_reads_a_far_clamp_over_its_clearance_plane`
  - `a_cross_drill_on_a_mill_is_refused_before_any_traverse`
- New `camcraft-sim` unit tests in `verify::first_traverse::tests`:
  - `a_turned_bar_is_read_at_its_corner_radius_not_its_upright_top`
  - `a_radial_start_reads_its_radius_over_the_axis_line`
  - `a_chuck_turns_with_the_work_and_a_tailstock_stands_still`
  - `the_swept_top_follows_the_axis_tilt_and_refuses_no_input`

## Quick gate (on 49e5d66e7 and 10cfd0cd2, with -j 18, before the merge of 05c9e56f2)

- `camcraft-sim` lib first_traverse: 8/8 pass.
- `camcraft-app`:
  - first_traverse_rotary 3/3, rotary_verify 9/9, setup_align_multiaxis 10/10.
  - first_traverse 4/4, first_traverse_table 5/5, operations 120 pass (6 ignored).
  - continuous_4axis_part 10/10.
  - post_not_judged, rotary_fixtures, center_cut_multiaxis, coarse_laws, cross_drill_neighbours, drilling_cross_stock, drilling_cross_box, stale_rapid_law, deburr_cache_stamp, wire_stamp: all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The merge of 05c9e56f2 (#2997's table fix) was clean. The stack gate of the coordinator covers this merged head.
- Heavy lanes not run, covered by the cut gate.

## Not exercised

- A machine with two rotaries: the rotary kinds read the sweep about the one fitted axis only.
- A multi-axis pose that leans the tool down from its tip.
- The tool radius under the tip (the same as #2901).

Refs #3077

Changelog: The first traverse after a tool change is now judged for the rotary, multi-axis and cross-drill operations; a clearance height inside the swept stock or under a fixture holds the post by name.

title: fix(app): a 3+2 first-traverse refusal names the heights the user set
body:
## What changed

- `Warning::FirstTraverseLow` (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`) gets the field `tilted: bool` with `#[serde(default)]`. A cache saved before this change still loads, and reads as upright.
- `operation::first_traverse::judge` (`crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs`) puts a 3+2 verdict into the frame in which the user sets the heights. Generate shifts each height by `h - origin.z` into the tilted frame. The new `in_user_frame` adds `origin.z` back to the two heights and sets `tilted` when the frame is not upright. The sim law does not change.
- A tilted verdict has a new text. It names the heights that the user set, says that they are measured along the tilted tool axis, and gives the raise. It has no `Z` value and no `X/Y`. The text of an upright verdict does not change.
- Guide: a troubleshooting entry for the new text (`site/content/guide/reference/troubleshooting.md`), and one paragraph in `site/content/guide/multi-axis/indexed.md` that says what the warning gives after a regenerate.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2991-tilted-first-traverse-message.md`.

## Readings

`examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj`, `Indexed Face1` (B 20 deg, tilt origin Z 20, Fixed clearance height 30). The operation cache was removed in a scratch copy, so `camcraft-cli process` generated it again:

- Before: `the first rapid (move 0) comes from an unknown X/Y at the clearance height Z10.000, under the stock top at Z11.114 - raise the clearance height above Z11.114`
- After: `the first rapid (move 0) comes from an unknown position at the clearance height 30.000 mm, under the stock top at 31.114 mm (both measured along the tilted tool axis) - raise the clearance height by at least 1.114 mm`

A clearance height of 31.114 or more passes the law (the local value is then 11.114 or more).

## Pinning tests

- `first_traverse::a_3_2_plane_reads_the_stock_top_along_its_tool_axis` (app): the verdict gives the typed clearance (25, not the local 5), the corner in the same frame (25.209), `tilted: true`, the new text without `Z` or `X/Y`, and the post refusal with the raise. It fails without the change in `judge` (`tilted` stays false).
- `verify::first_traverse::tests::a_tilted_verdict_names_the_raise_not_a_z_value` (sim): the full tilted text and a serde round trip.
- `verify::first_traverse::tests::a_verdict_saved_before_tilted_reads_as_upright` (sim): a cache JSON without `tilted` loads as upright, with the old text.
- `docs_troubleshooting` (app): the new troubleshooting heading matches the source text.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 109 steps, 0 failed (sim, motion and app suites, with `first_traverse`, `clearance_in_stock`, `wcs_start` and `stale_rapid_law`).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test docs_troubleshooting`: pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: the diff reaches 234 heavy steps (199 app, 34 motion). On head 9eee9c59d: 234 steps, 0 failed, wall time 58 min. The 16 known-fail steps (#1950, #2845 and others) are red as expected. `motion heavy: pocket3d_hsm` passes.

## Not exercised

- A saved cache keeps its old text until the operation is generated again. The verdict and the held post do not change. I did not change the op stamp salt, because that moves each stamp (`deburr_cache_stamp`, `wire_stamp`, the example projects) for a text change. For the same reason I did not regenerate `examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj`. The decision file records the two choices.
- No GUI check of the Warnings pane. The pane shows the `Display` text that the tests pin.

Changelog: The first-traverse refusal of a tilted (3+2) operation names the clearance height that the user set, says that the heights are measured along the tilted tool axis, and says how much to raise the clearance height.

Branch made from `upstream/main` at 2ec4ad7e0.

Fixes #2991

title: fix(turning): refuse a helical modelled thread by name
body:
## What changed

- New detector `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::axis_helix::helix`. It finds a helical surface (a modelled screw thread) from the facet normal lines. It gives the axis, the pitch and the hand.
- Threading now refuses a model with a helical thread. The message names the helical thread, its pitch and its hand. It tells the user to model the thread as revolved V grooves.
- The refusal is in the kernel (`turning::helical_refusal`, called by `thread_planned_in`). It is also in the app Threading arm, before the slice of the job region.
- `axis.rs`: the facet-datum loop and the normal moment move into two helpers (`data_of`, `moment`). The axis fit does not change.

## Cause

Threading reads a modelled thread as a revolved V section. A helical thread has no such section. Two earlier steps refused the issue's part with messages that named other causes:

- STEP route: the slice of the job region said `the mesh is open ... dangling chord ends`.
- Native route: the axis fit did not accept the helical flanks and said `every axis fits this model equally`. When the axis fit passes, the kernel said `nothing to thread ... threading cuts a MODELED thread`, and that does not tell the user that the thread is helical.

## How the detector works

About a candidate axis `(o, u)`, each inclined facet gives the screw parameter `h = (n x u) . (o - p) / (n . u)`. The normal lines of a helical surface belong to a linear line complex (Pottmann & Wallner, Computational Line Geometry). A revolve gives `h = 0`. The two flanks of a helical thread give one common nonzero `h`. The gates are:

- The agreeing area is at least half of the inclined area and at least 2% of the part.
- The agreeing facets go all the way round the axis (the coarseness skip of `axis.rs`).

The pitch is the area-weighted mean of the agreeing band. The two triangles of one twisted quad read `h` low and high (1.356 and 1.665 for a 1.5 pitch), so the median would be about 10% low.

## Tests

The QA files of the issue were not on this machine. The pins use a procedural shaft of the same shape: an M16x1.5 helical V, a Ø24 body and a Ø30 head, 70 long.

- `camcraft-motion` `turning_thread_helical`:
  - `a_helical_thread_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_left_hand_helical_thread_says_left_hand`
  - `a_coarse_helical_thread_is_refused_by_name` (48 segments)
  - `an_open_helical_mesh_is_refused_by_name` (facets removed)
  - `a_revolved_v_thread_and_a_smooth_bar_are_not_helical` (the pitch is found to 2%)
- `camcraft-app` `turning_thread_helical`:
  - `a_helical_thread_is_refused_by_name_before_the_slice` (an open mesh, as the STEP route)

Mutation results:

- The upstream kernel (`thread.rs`, `turning/mod.rs`) makes the four motion refusal pins fail with `nothing to thread - no valley 0.920 down ... threading cuts a MODELED thread` or `no material crosses the station interval`. My code makes them pass.
- The upstream `generate.rs` (no app guard) makes the app pin fail with `M16: the source model cannot be sliced: the mesh is open at z = 2.1875: 12 dangling chord ends`. This is the message in the issue. My code makes it pass.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (160 steps, 0 failed). This includes all the `turning_thread*` suites, and they keep their revolved-V fixtures. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. After the gate run, I changed only lints (`is_multiple_of`, a collapsed `if let`). Then I ran the two pin files again (green) and clippy again (clean).

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The issue's real STEP and `.sc` models (`/home/mikekinney/qa/runs/20261120-q03-turn-shaft/`). The files were not on this machine. A reviewer on skull can run `open_project` and `generate {name:"M16Modeled"}` / `generate {name:"M16Native"}` and expect the `HELICAL` refusal.
- A reader for helical threads (a phase from the helix) is not part of this PR. It is new algorithm work and changes posted G-code.
- This PR does not repair the STEP tessellation gaps of helical faces. That is an importer defect. Threading now refuses before the slice.
- No heavy lane ran.

## Overlaps

- Open PRs that change `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` in other functions: #3059, #3058, #2997, #2920, #2890, #2836, #2831, #2822, #2716, #2714. None changes the Threading arm. Touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/axis.rs` grows from 411 to 422 lines. The cause is the two extracted helpers. The file was already above 400 lines before this PR.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/3023-helical-thread-refusal.md`.

Effort: high

Changelog: Threading refuses a model with a helical modelled thread with a message that names the helical thread, its pitch and its hand, in place of a slice or axis-fit error.

Fixes #3023

title: fix(ui): an undersize-hole warning no longer hides a shank avoid hit
body:
## What changed

- `fold_warnings_located` (`crates/ui/src/operations.rs`) groups `Warning::DrillUndersize` under key `223`. Before, it used `216`. That is the key of `Warning::AvoidHit` with `FixturePart::Shank` (the avoid range is `216..=220`).
- A group prints only the line of its first warning. When the undersize hole came first, the pane folded the blocking "Do not touch" shank hit into the advisory line as "repeated on 1 more move". The pane did not show the shank hit.
- `223` and not `222`: open PR #2836 moves `UndercutLift` to `222`. The two PRs do not collide when the two merge.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3040-drill-undersize-fold-key.md`.

## Pinning test

`operations::warning_fold_tests::a_drill_undersize_never_hides_an_avoid_hit` folds one `DrillUndersize` and one `AvoidHit` for each of the five `FixturePart` values. It asserts six lines, each with its own move.

With the old key the test fails, and the output shows the defect:

```
"warning: undersize hole at move 3: ... - repeated on 1 more move (to 10)",
"warning: holder at move 11 violates protected 'Do not touch' item #1 (0.500 mm short of clearance)",
...
```

The shank hit at move 10 has no line of its own.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 3 steps, 0 failed (`ui build`, `ui suites: lib`, `ui suites: operations`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run`: the diff reaches no heavy lane.

## Not exercised

- No GUI check of the Warnings pane. The fold is a pure function, and the test calls it directly. The pane text does not change for a program with only one of the two warnings.
- `crates/ui/src/operations.rs` was 635 lines before this PR, above the 400-line rule. This PR adds 21 lines (the new test is in the `warning_fold_tests` module, as the issue asks). It does not split the file.

Changelog: The Warnings pane shows a protected "Do not touch" shank hit on its own line when the same program also has an undersize-hole warning.

Branch made from `upstream/main` at 08697d3c4.

Fixes #3040

title: feat(2d): import SVG drawings as 2D sketch profiles
body:
## What changed

- A new SVG reader, `camcraft_geometry::svg`, reads an SVG file into the same `dxf::Document` as the DXF reader. The sketch chaining, nesting, `SketchData`, the `Sketch` entity and the project file are shared and do not change.
  - Elements: `path` (M L H V C S Q T A Z, absolute and relative), `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `rect` (with rx/ry), `circle`, `ellipse`.
  - Groups: `g` with `transform` (matrix, translate, scale, rotate, skewX, skewY). A `use` of an element in the same file is drawn.
  - Curves: an arc or circle that maps to a circle stays an analytic arc. Beziers and true ellipses become lines within 0.005 mm.
  - Units: `width` and `height` in mm, cm, in, pt, pc or px (96 px to the inch), with the `viewBox` and `preserveAspectRatio`.
  - Y is flipped about the page height, so the drawing looks as it does in the editor.
  - A top-level `g` is a layer (`inkscape:label`, else `id`).
  - Text, images, nested `svg`, `style`, clip paths, masks, hidden content and `use` of other files are skipped and counted by kind.
- A new undoable command, `ImportSvg` (`commands/import_svg.rs`). It wraps `ImportDxf`, so apply and invert are the same code.
- A new MCP tool, `import_svg` (`mcp/svg_tools.rs`), and a new script verb, `cam.importSvg`. They take the options of `import_dxf`.
- The user guide (units and coordinates) and the MCP tool table list SVG.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1880-svg-import.md`.

## Refusals (by name, never a panic)

- A file that states no physical size, until the caller gives the unit of one drawing unit. The size is never guessed. A unitless `width` counts as no physical size.
- A caller unit for a file that states its size (two sizes would disagree).
- Malformed XML, malformed path data, an unknown transform or a singular one.
- A zero or negative document size or viewBox. A negative shape size.
- A degenerate arc (a zero radius).
- Percent or font-relative lengths in shapes.
- A file over the import budget (bytes, elements, segments), nesting deeper than 256, and `use` chains deeper than 16 (a reference loop).
- A compressed `.svgz` file, and a file that is not UTF-8.

## Tests

- `crates/geometry/tests/svg.rs` (9 tests): a rectangle with a hole in mm (nesting, Y flip), in and pt and px and cm documents, no physical size, absolute and relative path forms, Beziers and arcs, nested group transforms and a sheared ellipse, a rounded rect with polyline and skipped content, merged short segments, compact path syntax.
- `crates/geometry/tests/svg_refusals.rs` (5 tests): malformed documents and paths, zero or negative sizes, the import budget, and a deterministic smoke fuzz (truncations and 1000 byte mutations).
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_svg.rs` (2 tests): `import_svg` end to end (units, layers, chains, skipped notes, bounds, move, undo and redo, a 2D Contour on the profile, save and reopen, the script verb), and the command's refusals and undo step.
- Red before the fix: the pins did not compile on unchanged code (`unresolved import camcraft_geometry::svg`).
- Mutation checks. Each guard was removed, the pin went red, and then the guard was restored:
  - Y flip: red (4 tests).
  - Arcs stay analytic: red (4 tests).
  - Caller unit on a sized file is refused: red.
  - A unitless size is no physical size: red.
  - Zero-radius arc refusal: red.
  - `use` depth guard: red (stack overflow).
  - Short-segment merge: red.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean (exit 0).
- Touched suites, all green:
  - geometry: `svg` 9, `svg_refusals` 5, `dxf`, `dxf_refusals`, `sketch_data`, `sketch_chains`, and the lib tests.
  - app: `mcp_svg` 2, `mcp_dxf` 2, `sketch_profile` 8, `sketch_project` 14, `scripting` 20 (it checks `cam.d.ts`), `mcp` 23, and the lib tests (290).
- The gate did not complete. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` falls back to the batch tier, because the diff touches `crates/geometry/src/lib.rs`. On this machine the shared sccache server stopped responding: each compile through it hung, including the jobs of other sessions. The gate sets the sccache wrapper itself, so it hung at the `post` build twice. Clippy and the suites above ran with the wrapper unset. The batch tier still needs a run: the post-merge gate, or a reviewer's `pr-test.yml` run.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- A posted G-code golden for a 2D Contour on an SVG profile. On `main`, a 2D Contour on a profile is accepted but does not generate yet: that is #1864 (PR #2716). Follow-up: #3042.
- The row for `import_svg` in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. The edit was blocked as a sensitive file in this session. A maintainer session can add it. Then that PR needs `Process change: yes`.
- No UI change: the app has no DXF profile import dialog yet, so there is no file dialog to extend.
- Nested `<svg>` viewports, CSS stylesheets, text to outlines and embedded images are out of scope (the issue says so). They are counted as skipped.

## Overlaps

- #2773 (draft, needs-rework) changes the stock check in `ImportDxf::build`. This PR does not change `build`. `ImportSvg` has its own copy of that 10-line check, so it does not get the #2773 change. If #2773 merges first, `ImportSvg` must get the same change.
- #2924 adds rows to `commands/mod.rs` and `script/mod.rs`, and changes `mcp/sketch_tools.rs`. This PR adds other rows to the two `mod.rs` files and puts its MCP tool in a new file. The files are the same and the functions are different. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2678 adds lines to `commands/mod.rs`. The lines are different.

Changelog: Import SVG drawings (paths, shapes, group transforms, mm/cm/in/pt/pc/px sizes) as 2D profiles on the stock, with the `import_svg` MCP tool and `cam.importSvg`; an SVG with no physical size is refused until you state its unit.

Effort: high

Fixes #1880

title: fix(ui): clip pick outlines before screen projection
body:
## What changed

Clip each pick-outline segment before screen projection.
Keep each visible edge portion and preserve outline adjacency.
Selected, viewport-hover and row-hover highlights share this path.

## Cause

The old code projected points separately.
It dropped points behind the eye and lost visible edge portions.
Points before the near plane could project far outside the viewport.
The baseline is upstream/main `08697d3c4`.

## Tests

Pins:

- `pick_highlight_mesh::tests::highlight_near_clip_keeps_every_rectangle_edge_without_a_bridge`
- `pick_highlight_mesh::tests::highlight_near_clip_mesh_stays_within_the_rectangle_stroke`
- `pick_highlight_mesh::tests::highlight_near_clip_stops_a_front_of_eye_point_before_projection`
- `pick_highlight_mesh::tests::highlight_near_clip_does_not_join_disconnected_visible_runs`
- `pick_highlight_mesh::tests::highlight_near_clip_preserves_a_fully_visible_closed_outline`
- `pick_highlight_mesh::tests::highlight_near_clip_nonfinite_corner_does_not_connect_its_neighbors`
- `pick_highlight_mesh::tests::highlight_near_clip_keeps_a_segment_crossing_the_positive_w_boundary`

On unchanged code, five pins fail and two pass.
With the fix, all seven pins pass.
Restoring the old code makes five pins fail; the two invariant pins still pass.
Restoring the fix makes all seven pins pass.
Removing the near-plane guard makes its pin fail. Restoring the guard makes it pass.
Removing the positive-w guard makes its pin fail. Restoring the guard makes it pass.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passes: 1,339 tests pass and seven are ignored.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits with code 0.
The heavy gate plan reaches no lane.

None.

No manual GPU or desktop visual check ran.
The snapshot and release lanes did not run.

None. The overlap check used a limit of 200 open PRs.

title: feat(waterjet): Waterjet Profile operation on a shared 2D sheet kernel
body:
## What changed

- **Shared 2D sheet kernel (`crates/motion/src/sheet/`).** The kernel code moves out of `plasma` and `wire_edm` without a change of behaviour:
  - `nest` (contour roles, inner-first cut order) and `ring` (kerf ring, walks), from `plasma`;
  - `laws` (kerf law, cover law) and `lead` (straight and arc leads), from `plasma`;
  - `arclen` (a ring by arc length), from `wire_edm::tabs`;
  - `open` (the one-sided offset of an open run), from `wire_edm::open`.

  A `Voice` keeps each refusal text word for word. Plasma and wire EDM now call the shared code.
- **Cover law.** The law now takes one span or more for each contour, and an `exempt` closure for a tab's bridge. Plasma exempts no point. The law now refuses a closed contour that has no span.
- **Waterjet generator (`crates/motion/src/waterjet/`).** `waterjet_profile` does these steps:
  - It cuts the inner contours first, with the kerf ring at kerf / 2 on the waste side.
  - It adds straight or arc leads, with the pierce in the scrap. A lead with no room is halved up to four times.
  - It pierces a tight hole at its centre when the lead has no room after the halving.
  - It cuts tabs as uncut gaps. Each stretch between two gaps gets its own pierce, lead-in and lead-out.
  - It cuts open runs on the centre line, or to the left or right of travel.
  - It can post G41/G42, and it can send arcs as chords (`Move::chords`).

  The kerf law and the cover law certify the result.
- **App.** The changes are:
  - `OpType::WaterjetProfile` (stored id 44), `Section::Waterjet` and `Family::Waterjet`. The op mounts a `ToolKind::Waterjet` nozzle only.
  - `WaterjetOp` with its command-door sanity check, `waterjet_op.rs` (seed, params, generate) and the digest bytes.
  - A `.camproj` DTO (`waterjet_profile`, additive).
  - Each exhaustive match in the app gets a waterjet arm.
  - Profile (DXF) sources are admitted. The family door has its own words: "mount a waterjet first".
  - MCP reaches the kind through the generic `add_operation` / `edit_operation`. The `add_operation` text now names waterjet.
- **UI.** The changes are:
  - `waterjet_page.rs` with these fields: kerf, compensation, direction, open-run side, send arcs as lines, sheet heights, tabs, lead shape and lengths, cut feed, pierce time, abrasive delay. It has no torch height or THC field.
  - The Waterjet ribbon section.
  - An original glyph (`assets/ui/svg/op-waterjet-profile.svg`, rasterised by `cargo xtask icons`).

## Readings

- Golden `waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes.cl` has 149 moves, 5 pierces and 3 holes cut before the outline. The outline is cut as two led-in stretches between 2 mm tabs.
- The existing goldens do not change. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` shows only the new file. The plasma golden `plasma_plate_with_holes.cl` stays byte-identical after the kernel move.

## Tests (pins)

Each pin was red before this change: the module and the kind did not exist, so the pins could not compile.

- motion `waterjet::tests` (9): `holes_are_cut_before_the_outline_and_every_pierce_is_in_the_waste`, `straight_leads_lay_no_arc_on_a_square_part`, `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_and_each_stretch_is_pierced_and_led_in`, `a_tight_hole_is_pierced_at_its_centre`, `linearize_sends_every_arc_as_chords`, `an_open_run_rides_its_stated_side`, `control_compensation_records_a_comp_span_per_untabbed_contour`, `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`, `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged`.
- app `waterjet_profile` (6): the family door, hole first, tabs, a milling tool refused, create / edit / undo / redo, and a byte-identical `.camproj` round trip.
- app `mcp_waterjet` (1): add, edit, undo, redo and generate over MCP.
- app `golden_cl::waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes_matches_golden`.
- ui `waterjet_ribbon_tests` (2): the section shows on a waterjet only, the tip names the waterjet, the glyph is its own, and the page has a leads tab.
- Plasma and wire EDM: all `camcraft-motion` plasma, sheet and wire tests pass, and all 34 `golden_cl` tests pass.

## Mutation results

Each mutation was applied, the pins were run, and then the code was restored (green again).

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Inner-first order removed | red: `holes_are_cut_before_...`, `a_tight_hole_...` |
| Tabs ignored | red: `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_...`, `bad_input_...` |
| Tight-hole rule off | red: `a_tight_hole_is_pierced_at_its_centre` |
| Linearization ignored | red: `linearize_sends_every_arc_as_chords` |
| Cover law exempts every point | red: `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged` |
| Cover law exempts no point | red: `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_...` (6 mm tabs) |
| Leads on the part side | red: 7 of 9 pins |

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 422 steps ran (374 app, 44 post, 3 motion, 1 cl). The only red steps were kind-count pins that this change extends on purpose: `lathe_voice::tests::every_kind_is_work_spindle_live_tool_or_refused_by_name`, `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input` and `tests/ribbon.rs` (`family_is_derived_not_forked`, `the_probe_appends_its_id_and_lists_in_drilling`). I updated them to 45 kinds and the Waterjet section. Because I edited during the run, the gate marked that run VOID. `--failed` on the committed tree then ran the red step: green. The app lib suite is green (290).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1324 passed, 0 failed. The waterjet row was added to `tips_match_the_imgui_table`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

## Not exercised

- Posting. No post serves `Kind::Waterjet` yet. The pierce time and the abrasive delay are in the path notes only. #1882 adds the CL record and the post hooks.
- `verify` and the post gate for a waterjet op. That is #1885.
- Selection of the cut data from the nozzle's recipe. This is follow-up #3047.
- The MCP skill row. The skill file is a protected path in this session. This is follow-up #3048.
- Heavy lanes. The diff reaches `motion` and the `app` heavy lanes. I did not run `cargo xtask gate heavy` locally.
- The UI page was not opened in a running app. The structural tests cover the ribbon and the tab only.

## Overlaps

- These open PRs also append an op kind to the same enums and tables (`kinds.rs`, `types/params.rs`, `project/params*.rs`): #2920, #2890, #2836, #2831, #2716, #2714. The conflicts are additive (both sides add arms). The PR that merges second takes the next free stored id.
- These open PRs touch `generate.rs` or `job.rs`, in other functions: #2997, #2822, #2678, #2999, #2993, #2992, #2981, #2979, #2978. The PR that merges second refreshes.
- #2932 touches `crates/ui/src/interact.rs`, in other functions.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1883-waterjet-profile.md`.

Effort: max

Changelog: Waterjet Profile operation - inner-first 2D through-cuts with kerf offset, straight or arc leads pierced in the scrap, tabs as uncut gaps, the tight-hole centre pierce, open-run sides, optional G41/G42 and arc linearization; plasma and wire EDM now share one 2D sheet kernel.

Fixes #1883

title: feat(ui): place DXF profiles on the stock from the Stock page and a drop
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the UI for DXF profiles over the #1862 commands (`ImportDxf`, `MoveSketch`, `DeleteEntity`). It follows the maintainer's scope change on the issue: the DXF door is on the Stock page, not on `Model > Open`.

- The Stock page has a new group "DXF profiles". It has the control "Add DXF profile…" (a `.dxf` file picker). The control is disabled when the active setup has no stock.
- The group lists each profile of the active setup with these controls:
  - "Profile X", "Profile Y" and "Profile angle (deg)". These are a draft. "Place profile" queues one `MoveSketch`.
  - "Hide profile" / "Show profile". This is view state, the same list as the browser eye.
  - "Delete profile". This queues one `DeleteEntity`.
- A `.dxf` file dropped on the viewport goes through the same import path. With no stock, the drop is refused by name: "drop refused: <file> is a DXF profile - make a stock first ...".
- A drawing without `$INSUNITS` opens the modal "DXF units". The modal shows the drawing size read in millimeters and read in inches, each with the size in the other unit. "Millimeters" or "Inches" runs `ImportDxf` with that unit. "Cancel", Escape or a backdrop click places nothing. The unit is never guessed.
- The status line shows the import summary: the name, the setup, the unit and its source (file or chosen), the layer count, the closed and open chain counts, the chains not chained, and the skipped entities by type.
- The browser shows each profile as a child row of its setup's Stock row (`Leaf::Sketch`), with the suffix "DXF profile" and the eye. A click opens the Stock page and selects the profile, so Del deletes it through the history.
- The viewport draws the profile lines, arcs and circles of the active setup on the stock top, at `sketch::world_pose`. Each free end of an open chain gets a magenta X. No curve uses that colour, so an open gap does not look closed.
- The overlay lines are cached by the sketch data `Arc` and the pose (`SketchLineCache` on `FrameCache`). A still frame builds nothing (crates/ui/AGENTS.md, frame cost).
- The operation page Source list offers the profiles of the operation's setup for a kind that `sketch_model::admits` (2D milling, plasma, wire EDM). A setup with a stock, a profile and no model can so have an operation on the profile.
- `camcraft_app` re-exports `camcraft_geometry::dxf`, so the UI can name the `Primitive` variants. This adds no crate dependency.

The import does not use `finish_import`. That function handles the model worker. `ImportDxf` checks the drawing at construction, so the typed `DxfUnitsMissing` error is caught where the UI builds the command. `docs/decisions/1863-dxf-stock-ui.md` records this and the other choices.

## Cause

The #1862 commands had no UI door. A user could place a DXF profile only through MCP or the script.

## Tests

New pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/dxf_profile.rs`:

- `the_stock_page_adds_lists_places_and_deletes_a_dxf_profile`
- `a_drawing_without_units_asks_millimeters_or_inches_and_never_guesses`
- `a_dropped_dxf_lands_on_the_stock_or_asks_for_one`
- `the_browser_lists_the_profile_under_its_stock_with_an_eye`
- `the_viewport_draws_the_chains_on_the_stock_top_and_marks_open_ends`
- `the_operation_page_takes_the_profile_as_its_source_without_a_model`
- `a_still_frame_builds_no_profile_lines_and_a_move_builds_once`

Also:

- `page_layout_windows::layout_window_dxf_units` (the named layout test of the new modal).
- `dxf_units_dialog::tests::readings_state_both_units_both_ways`.
- `dxf_drop::tests::dxf_by_extension_in_any_case`.

Red before the fix: yes. On upstream/main the pins do not compile. `CommandKind::ImportDxf`, `CommandKind::MoveSketch`, `State::dxf_units_prompt`, `Leaf::Sketch`, `sketch_overlay` and `op_source` do not exist.

Mutation checks (each red with the mutation, green when restored):

- Guess millimeters for a drawing without units: `a_drawing_without_units...` is red ("nothing lands before the answer").
- Remove the stock check of the drop: `a_dropped_dxf...` is red (the refusal does not name the file).
- Remove the profiles from the Source list: `the_operation_page...` is red.
- Draw a hidden profile: `the_viewport_draws...` is red.
- Bypass the line cache: `a_still_frame_builds...` is red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 4cf20695e (19 steps, 0 failed: app lib, ui lib and 17 ui suites). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No posted G-code, CL file or snapshot PNG changes.

## Not exercised

- Before and after screenshots are not attached. The headless harness of this worker has no renderer. The structural tests pin the labels, the rows and the overlay vertices.
- A `.dxf` dropped in the browser build (wasm) is refused by name. The browser drop path delivers model bytes only.
- The native file picker of "Add DXF profile…" is not driven in a test. The test calls the same `CommandKind::ImportDxf`.

These open PRs touch the same files, in different functions. The PR that merges second refreshes.

title: fix(setup): moving operations into a setup keeps the program order
body:
## What changed
- `SetOperationSetup` gives the moved operation a position at the end of its target setup.
- It uses the same `append_position` helper as `CreateOperation`. The helper also pins the target's siblings at their current positions.
- Undo restores the moved operation and the pinned siblings.
- A move that keeps the effective setup (implicit `None` to the first setup) keeps the position of the operation.
- `append_position` and its `Reordered` type are now visible inside `crate::commands`. They do not change.
- New decision file: `docs/decisions/3022-setup-move-order.md`.

## Cause
The old command set `order = None` on the moved operation. `setup::operation_order` puts an operation without a position after the others, in name order. Operations moved one by one into a new setup thus came out in name order. A tap came before its tap drill.

## Tests
- `crates/app/tests/setup_move_order.rs` (new):
  - `moving_implicit_operations_into_a_named_setup_keeps_their_order`: the case of the issue, at command level, with undo.
  - `moved_operations_append_to_the_target_setup_in_move_order`: two declared setups, a user reorder, a move out and back in, undo of all moves.
- `mcp_setup_moves::moving_operations_into_a_named_setup_keeps_the_program_order`: the case of the issue over MCP (`add_setup`, `set_operation_setup`, `get_job`).
- All three pins failed on unchanged code (`left: ["Alpha", "Mid", "Zeta"]`, `right: ["Zeta", "Alpha", "Mid"]`).
- Mutation 1: the old `setup.rs` back -> all three pins red. Restored -> green.
- Mutation 2: the guard for the same effective setup removed -> the two implicit-setup pins red. Restored -> green.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 26 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The `setups` and `setup_delete_order` suites also pass.

## Goldens moved
None.

## Not exercised
- The UI move through the operation page. It sends the same `SetOperationSetup` command.
- A project file saved before this fix with moved operations that have no position. Those operations keep the old name-ordered tail until the user moves or reorders them.

## Overlaps
- #2920, #2893 and #2716 touch `crates/app/src/commands/operation/create.rs`. They change other functions. This PR changes only the visibility of `append_position` and `Reordered`. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Moving operations into another setup keeps their program order; each moved operation lands last in the target setup (#3022).

Fixes #3022

title: fix(post): a symlinked executable finds the assets beside the real file
body:
## What changed

- `DataFiles::from_process` (`crates/post/src/data_dir.rs`) resolves the executable path with the new `real_exe` before the assets lookup. If the path is a symbolic link, `real_exe` gives the real file (`std::fs::canonicalize`). The lookup then starts in the install folder, not in the folder of the link. The posts and the machines use this lookup.
- `real_exe` changes only a link. A plain path keeps its form, so a Windows path in a message gets no `\\?\` prefix. A link that does not resolve keeps the link path, and the refusal names the folder of the link, as before.
- The refusal of a copy of the executable now ends with `COPY_HINT`: "Start the program from its install folder, or through a symbolic link to the installed executable: a copy of the executable has no assets beside it." No setting or environment variable points at an assets folder, so the hint names none.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3028-symlink-exe-posts.md`.

## Readings (Linux, Manjaro, release build of `camcraft-cli`)

Install-style folder: `install/camcraft-cli` and `install/assets/{posts,machines}`, outside a cargo build tree. Command: `camcraft-cli process examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.camproj -o out.nc`.

| Started as | Before this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| `install/camcraft-cli` | rc 0, 369 lines | rc 0, 369 lines |
| `bin/camcraft-cli`, a symbolic link to the installed file | rc 0, 369 lines | rc 0, 369 lines, the same bytes as the install run |
| `copy/camcraft-cli`, a copy | rc 1, "no posts folder found ..." | rc 1, the same refusal, then the `COPY_HINT` text |

On Linux, `current_exe` reads `/proc/self/exe`, which is already the real file. Thus the symlink case worked on Linux before this change. The fix is for macOS and Windows, where `current_exe` gives the link path.

## Pinning tests

- `data_dir::tests::a_symlinked_exe_finds_the_assets_beside_the_real_file` (Unix only: a symbolic link on Windows needs a privilege). It also checks a chain of two links, a dangling link, and the old result for the link path.
- `data_dir::tests::a_copied_exe_is_refused_with_the_fix`.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 3 steps, 0 failed (`post build`, `post suites: lib`, `post suites: folder_scan`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: the diff reaches the 200 app heavy steps through the crate dependency. Result on head 009623a59: 200 steps, 1 failed, 48.3 min.
  - The three known-fail steps (#1950, #2845, #2849) are red as expected.
  - Red: `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`, test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`. It gives (3158, 3130, 1141). The Linux x86_64 pin is (4726, 4698, 549).
  - The same test on unchanged `upstream/main` at 3c761b5bb fails with the same counts. This PR does not cause it: the test plans a toolpath and reads no posts or machines folder. Issue #3050 (P2) tracks this stale pin. Its body names the same counts on Windows and a stale Linux pin after PR #2904.

## Not exercised

- macOS and Windows. I have no machine for them. The macOS cause is the one in the issue. `std::env::current_exe` documents that it can give the path of a symbolic link. A Windows reading is still necessary for the third "Done means" item.
- `crates/ui/src/theme_dir.rs` finds `assets/themes` with `current_exe` too, and has the same link behaviour. The desktop app is not usually started through a link, so this PR does not change it. A follow-up issue can track it if the maintainer wants that.

Changelog: A `camcraft-cli` started through a symbolic link (the usual macOS PATH set-up) finds the shipped posts and machines beside the real executable. A copy of the executable is still refused, and the message now says how to start it.

Fork synced at v0.24.0; branch made from `upstream/main` at 3c761b5bb.

Fixes #3028

title: fix(2d): keep contour leads on the air side at a closed ring's seam
body:
## What changed
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/lead_fit.rs`: a new function `seam_tangents` gives the lead-in and lead-out tangents. `plan_leads` and `both_fit` use it.
- On a closed ring, it compares the start tangent and the end tangent at the seam.
- If the ring bends to the air side at the seam, the lead-out tangent is mirrored across the start tangent. The lead-in tangent is mirrored across the end tangent.
- Then each lead leaves the seam on the air side of the whole ring.
- A smooth seam, a seam that bends away from the air, and an open walk (tab windows, chains, an exit point) keep their tangents.
- New test file `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_lead.rs`.
- Decision record `docs/decisions/3019-contour-tab-lead-cross.md`.

## Cause
- The seam of a round-cornered outside ring falls on a fitted corner arc.
- The arc's end tangent is about 0.05 degree off the ring's first chord, toward the material.
- The 8 mm linear lead-out goes along that tangent. It crosses the ring's second move about 0.25 mm past the seam.
- The crossing law found this on each level. This is the issue's "feed moves 5 and 13 cross" (one pair on each level).
- Tabs are not the cause. The same crossing occurs with no tabs.
- On a conventional cut, the lead-in has the same fault against the ring's last move.
- The crossing law is correct and does not change.

## Tests
Pins (the issue's plate: 120 x 80, four R6 corners, D10 tool, stepdown 3, 12 deep, 4 tabs 3 x 1, linear lead 8):
- `an_outside_tabbed_contour_with_a_linear_lead_has_no_crossing` (climb, 4 tabs).
- `an_outside_contour_with_a_linear_lead_has_no_crossing_with_or_without_tabs` (climb with no tabs; conventional with 0 and 4 tabs).
- Each case asserts: no `crossed_pairs`, no `Crossing` or `Gouge` from `verify`, and a full 8 mm lead-in and lead-out.

Red before the fix: yes, both pins. Failure text: `feed crossings [[5, 14], [21, 30], [37, 46], [53, 62]]`.

Mutations:
- Old `lead_fit.rs` from upstream/main: both pins red.
- Lead-in mirror removed: the conventional case red (`[[3, 12], [19, 28], [35, 44], [51, 60]]`).
- Lead-out mirror removed: both pins red.
- Fix restored: both pins green.

Gate:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (motion lib, climb_direction, contour_tab_lead, one_descent).
- Also run: motion `contour_start`, `machining2d`, `contour_tabs`, `contour_tab_bridge`, `contour_tab_height`, `contour_tab_necks`, `control_comp`. All green.
- Also run: app `golden_cl`, `conformance`, `control_comp`, `solid_law_goldens`, `microarc_test_part`, `corner_relief`, `verify`. All green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved
None.

## Not exercised
- The QA project file of the issue (`q01-blocked.camproj`) was not opened. The pin rebuilds the same plate and operation in `camcraft-motion`.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` was not run. A run is necessary before the PR is flagged ready.
- Inside contours (bores) with a bend at the seam. The law uses the air side, so it applies to them too. No pin covers them.

## Overlaps
None. No open PR changes `lead_fit.rs`.

Changelog: A 2D Contour with a linear lead on a part with round corners no longer gets a lead-in or lead-out that crosses the cut at the seam, so verify does not hold the post.

Effort: high

Fixes #3019

title: fix(chamfer): take a wall's lean from the frame, not from the sections
body:
## What changed

- `wall_lean` (new, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs`) gives the plan move of an upright wall in the operation frame. With no frame or an upright frame, the move is zero. With the tool axis in the world XY plane, it gives `None`.
- `ride_loops` takes this move as a new argument. The app caller (`material_source.rs`) computes it from the frame and the chamfer depth.
- `leans` accepts only this move. It does not read the move from the section centroids any more. The `centroid` helper is removed.
- `partly_bevelled` cuts each top segment at the foot of each wall vertex inside it. Then it judges each piece as before.
- The unit tests move to `chamfer_ride_tests.rs`, so that the source file stays under 400 lines.
- `docs/decisions/2936-chamfer-leaning-wall.md`: the sentence "Thus the new test cannot hide a case of #2887" is corrected.
- New decision file: `docs/decisions/2944-chamfer-lean-frame.md`.

## Cause

The part has a 1 mm bevel on the -X side and a 1 mm undercut lip on the +X side. The top section `[-29,31] x [-20,20]` is the wall section `[-30,30] x [-20,20]` moved 1 mm in X. The old `leans` found this move from the centroids and skipped the #2887 refusal.

A second cause showed in the test. Each Y side of the top section is one segment from X-29 to X31. Its X31 end is off the wall. The old judgement read the whole segment as bevelled. Thus no segment was sharp, and the refusal did not occur even without the lean exemption. The cut at X30 now gives a 59 mm sharp piece and a 1 mm lip piece.

## Tests

- Pin: `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::an_upright_bevel_beside_an_equal_undercut_lip_still_refuses`. Red on unchanged code (the part rode the wall `[-30,30]` all round). Green with the fix.
- New: `the_wall_lean_is_the_frames_own` (no frame, upright, 10 degree tilt, horizontal axis).
- The box under a 10 degree tilt (#2936) still generates: `framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number` (`stock_source_holes`) passes.
- Mutations:
  - Lean sign flipped in `wall_lean`: `framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number` red (partly-bevelled refusal). The sign is checked end to end.
  - No segment pieces: the pin red.
  - Lean read off the sections again: the pin red.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 136 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- A real STEP model of the bevel-and-lip plate. The pin uses hand-built sections.
- A tilted frame with a part that has true draft walls. It is read as before #2936 (the safe reading).
- Heavy lanes were not run.

Fixes #2944

title: feat(post): waterjet records, CR LF, travel, programBounds and a generic waterjet post
body:
## What changed

- The post engine reads a `lineEnding` manifest entry. The value `"lf"` is the default. The value `"crlf"` ends each line with `\r\n`. The engine refuses any other value by name. The engine reads the entry after `onClose`, so `onOpen` can set it from a declared option.
- `machine.travel` gives the stated linear strokes `{X, Y, Z}` to scripts. Each value is `[min, max]` in mm, or `null`. The mirror now carries the `travel` of a linear axis. The raw door reads a vendor tree through `parse_mch`.
- The engine publishes `programBounds` before `onOpen`. It is the XY box of the cutting records, or `null`. Arcs count at the quarter points that they pass (`machine::move_extremes`). Rapids do not count.
- New stream records `WATERJET [ABRASIVE] [DWELL<ms>] [LAG<ms>]` and `JET ON C<id> <ROLE>` / `JET OFF C<id>`. The cl types are `cl::WaterjetCut` and `cl::JetSpan` (`crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs`). The reader takes the `.cnc` form and the `.cl` comment form.
- The new hooks `onJetOn` / `onJetOff` fire under a `JetLaw` (`cnc_jet.rs`). The law refuses by name: a jet with no header, an ON while a jet is on, a rapid while a jet is on, and a jet that stays on. It shares no state with the plasma `TorchLaw`.
- `linearizeArcs = true` posts each arc as chords through `onLinear`, at `chordTolerance` mm (0.01 when unstated). The engine refuses a bad tolerance by name. The chords come from `cl::Move::segments3`. The last chord ends on the arc's end point. All chord lines map to the arc record.
- A WCS flip on a waterjet section is refused by name, the same as for plasma.
- New post `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps` (generic ISO abrasive waterjet). It writes `G20`/`G21`, `G90 G94 G17 G40`, a work offset, and `G0`/`G1`/`G2`/`G3` (or G1 chords). It writes XY only. Each contour gets: water on, `G4` valve lag, abrasive on, `G4` pierce dwell, the cut, abrasive off, water off. The four M numbers, the G4 word form, the arc form and the line ending are declared options. The default M numbers (M10/M11, M12/M13) are placeholders, and the post header says so.
- The post refuses by name: an rpm (S, G95), a surface speed (G96), coolant, a section with no `WATERJET` header, a machine not declared `kind: waterjet`, a rotary, a cycle, a Z cutting move, and a cut outside the stated `machine.travel`.
- Docs: `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` (records, properties, "Waterjet records") and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` (hooks, sheet-cutting seams, the waterjet post).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1882-waterjet-post.md`.

## Cause

This is new work for #1882. The engine wrote only `\n` lines. It did not publish linear travel or a cut box. It had no waterjet records or jet hooks, and no waterjet post was available.

## Tests

Pins (all red on the upstream sources, 17 of 17):

- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_engine.rs` (12 tests): `line_ending_crlf_ends_every_line_with_cr_lf`, `line_ending_other_words_are_refused_by_name`, `program_bounds_box_the_cut_moves_and_skip_rapids`, `machine_travel_publishes_the_linear_strokes`, `machine_travel_rides_the_mirror_and_the_raw_file`, `linearize_arcs_posts_chords_ending_on_the_arc_end`, `linearize_arcs_refuses_a_bad_tolerance_by_name`, `waterjet_records_fire_the_jet_hooks_with_their_properties`, `waterjet_records_round_trip_in_both_spellings`, `waterjet_law_refuses_what_the_stream_cannot_mean`, `waterjet_header_and_open_jet_end_with_their_section`, `waterjet_section_under_a_flipped_wcs_is_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_iso_post.rs` (7 tests): the goldens `plate.nc` (mm, G2/G3) and `plate_inch_chords.nc` (inch, G1 chords, CR LF, `G4 P` ms, custom M numbers), and the refusals for spindle words, a section that is not a waterjet cut, a machine that is not a waterjet, travel, a Z cut, a dry cut and a cycle.
- `crates/post/tests/script_waterjet_iso.rs`: the recorded-stream suite (11 refusal goldens; no recorded stream is a waterjet cut).
- `crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs` unit tests: line round trip, bad words, span sanity.

Mutation checks (one guard changed, its pin run, the guard put back): 21 of 21 red. The guards: the CR LF join, the `lineEnding` refusal, the bounds publish, the rapid skip, the arc quarter points, the travel in props, the travel in the mirror, the chord branch, the tolerance check, the jet-hook check, the jet rapid law, the jet section end, the jet fire, the WCS-flip refusal, the post rpm, CSS, header, kind, travel and Z refusals, and the order abrasive off before water off.

title: fix(build): the catalog timing line is one write, and the contract test runs its two cases in order
body:
## Cause

The post-merge run 44780029308 (main `768fe23f0`) failed in `contract::two_broken_cases_report_both_names_and_times` (`crates/app/tests/example_catalog/contract.rs:59`). The step log (artifact `gate-logs-post-merge-44780029308-1`, `494-app_suites_example_catalog.log`) shows:

```
missing time for 2d/contour-tabs:
...
catalog 2d/contour-tabs regenerates
thread '<unnamed>' (1052938) panicked at crates/app/tests/example_catalog/support.rs:68:5:
2d/first-part: missing model/
 elapsed=0.000s budget=60.000s
```

- The scratch-root override works. The inner cases fail in 0.000 s on the empty root.
- The inner run starts the two cases in parallel.
- `within` wrote its timing line with `writeln!` to stderr. Stderr has no buffer, so the line went out in pieces.
- The panic message of the other case thread fell between the pieces. The assert did not find `catalog 2d/contour-tabs regenerates elapsed=`.

This is a race. It occurs more on the loaded Linux runner. The 59 s is the time of the full binary, not of this test.

## What changed

- `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/support.rs`: the new `timing_line` makes the whole line with its newline. `within` writes it with one `write_all` on the locked stderr.
- `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/contract.rs`: the inner run uses `--test-threads=1`. The two cases run in order. The asserts do not change.
- `docs/decisions/3043-catalog-timing-line.md`: the decision, and what was dropped (a retry, a looser assert).

- `contract::two_broken_cases_report_both_names_and_times` (the red test).

body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps`: `g76Why` refuses the one-block LinuxCNC `G76` when the record's `StartInAir` is not `true`. The check uses the same refusal channel as the other G76 refusals. It runs before the drive-line rapid and the `G76` block, so no block of the cycle is written and the in-app gate writes no file. The cycle words do not change. The text has the form of the Fanuc text of #2878:
  `G76 threading cycle refused - the start point is above material (G76 moves the insert to pass depth at rapid traverse) - start the thread in free air in front of the end face or in a relief groove wider than the insert, regenerate the operation, or choose G33 passes`
- The value is the `start_in_air` of PR #2892 (`crates/app/src/operation/g76_start.rs`). The post adds no geometry.
- `crates/app/tests/tormach_lathe_support/mod.rs`: `thread_world` keeps the solid bar (Z-16 to Z40, start Z14). The new `g76_world` bar runs from Z-26 to its free end face Z14.693, with the top one lead higher (16.3). The cycle starts at Z16 in free air. This is the fixture change of #2892 for Fanuc. Each test that must post a Tormach `G76` now uses `g76_world`.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2952-tormach-g76-start-in-air.md`.

## Readings

- The public LinuxCNC G-code reference, G76 section: with no entry taper, "the tool will rapid to the cut depth then synchronize and begin the cut". This post writes no entry taper (no `E` / `L`). Thus each pass moves the insert in at rapid at the start Z.
- The old golden started at `Z14` on a bar that runs to Z40. That is a rapid into solid material.

## Golden lines that changed

Regenerated only with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test lathe_post_tormach_thread`.

- `golden/nc/tormach-lathe/thread_g76_mm.nc`:
  - line 12 `G0 Z14` -> `G0 Z16`: the start is now in front of the end face.
  - line 17 `G0 Z40` removed: the #1604 departure goes +Z only up to the stock face. The new face (Z14.693) is below the Z24 retract, so no move is necessary.
- `golden/nc/tormach-lathe/thread_g76_inch.nc`: the same two lines (`G0 Z0.5512` -> `G0 Z0.6299`; `G0 Z1.5748` removed).
- No other golden changed. The G33 goldens are the same.

## Other posts checked for a thread cycle

Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` (refuses since #2878) and `tormach-lathe.cps` (this PR) write a thread cycle and define `onThreadCycle`. `linuxcnc.cps` `G33.1` is a rigid tap. `tormach.cps`, `grblhal.cps` and `tinyg.cps` refuse `G84`. The other posts have no thread word. The decision file has the table.

## Pins

- New `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_tormach_g76_start.rs`:
  - `tormach_g76_refuses_by_name_when_the_start_point_is_inside_a_solid_bar` (mm and inch; the gate writes no file)

  - `tormach_g33_passes_still_post_when_the_start_point_is_inside_a_solid_bar`
  - `tormach_g76_refuses_a_legacy_stream_without_the_air_word`
- `a_g76_record_the_cycle_cannot_state_exactly_is_refused_by_name`: 9 cases -> 10 ("the start point is above material").
- `inch_g76_pass_bottoms_match_pathpilot_hub_8l_readings`: the golden line is now `G0 Z0.6299`. The DRO pass bottoms (X and depth) do not change.

## Gate (quick, local, worktree issue-917, `-j 18`, sccache)

- camcraft-app, each binary green: `lathe_post_tormach_thread` 10, `lathe_post_tormach_g76_start` 4, `lathe_post_tormach_g76_ladder` 3, `lathe_post_tormach_g30` 4, `lathe_post_tormach` 8, `lathe_post_g76_start` 5, `lathe_post_g76` 8, `lathe_post_g76_schedule` 7, `lathe_post_inch` 6, `lathe_post_thread_dips` 7, `lathe_post` 7, `conformance` 7, `solid_law_goldens` 7, `program_units` 7, `example_catalog` 29, `example_catalog_edge_work` 1, `catalog_groove_part_off` 1, `lathe_work_spindle` 5, `setup_post_options` 13, `mcp_post_options` 7.
- `camcraft-post` lib: 78 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 2 steps, 0 failed.
- No catalog example uses the Tormach lathe post (`cone-thread` uses Fanuc Lathe).
- `rustfmt --check`: not a repo gate (no config; files on `main` show the same diffs). Not applied.

## Not exercised

- A Tormach start in a relief groove wider than the insert: the Tormach suites have no grooving fixture. The judge is pinned by `g76_start_tests.rs` (`relief_groove_wider_than_insert_passes_when_grooved_and_refuses_when_uncut_or_narrow`).

A cached record without the value reads false. Its Tormach `G76` is refused by name until the threading operation is regenerated. This is the same rule as the Fanuc post.

title: fix(post): scale output budget with the input program
body:
## What changed

The post engine scales its output budget with the parsed input record count.
The budget is `max(100_000, 16 * records + 1_024)`, capped at `u32::MAX` with saturating arithmetic.
A Tormach operation with 100,001 feed moves now posts whole and per operation.
An output refusal states the limit, attempted line count, and operation.

The emitter keeps a private counter.
The host preserves a refusal after a script catches the exception or resets its public counters.
Direct output buffer writes use the same budget.
The output extraction helper moves into `js_host` to keep `js.rs` below 400 lines.

## Cause

The runaway guard used a fixed 100,000-line cap for every input size.
A valid operation could exceed this cap by itself.
The error gave no limit, count, or operation.

## Tests

All eight pins in `post_output_budget` fail with the upstream implementation and pass with the fix:

- `tormach_posts_over_100k_moves_in_a_whole_program`
- `tormach_posts_over_100k_moves_per_operation`
- `runaway_writers_report_limit_count_and_operation`
- `caught_runaway_refusal_keeps_limit_count_and_operation_after_reset`
- `large_input_still_refuses_a_runaway_script_at_its_scaled_limit`
- `top_level_runaway_names_the_first_operation`
- `runaway_in_the_second_operation_names_that_operation`
- `resetting_public_output_counters_cannot_bypass_the_guard`

The initial unchanged-code run fails at the old guard and its incomplete diagnostics.
The mutation check restores all three upstream production files and makes all eight pins fail.
Restoring the fix makes all eight pins pass.

The initial quick gate passed all 80 steps, including the sandbox tests and mapped downstream app suites.
The initial clippy run passed. The current-head results are below.

### Review validation follow-up (2026-11-20)

Head: `8ff39f5480e6acbffbbb2fbe038fbe1fc1e60cf1`.
Merged upstream `main` at `f85163b0ca948250fd6a51360d14754a282e0340`.
This brings in the tracked baseline fix for #3050 from PR #3078.
The merge was clean. No hand resolution or new source change was needed.
The PR stays a draft for re-review.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: passed all 83 steps; 700 tests passed, with no failed or ignored tests.
- All eight `post_output_budget` pins: all eight passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: passed all 200 selected steps in 24.9 minutes; 41 tests passed, six expected known failures, and no unexpected failures.
- `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`: passed; all six `shared_face_bodies_finish` tests also passed.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: both steps passed. One light twin passed in 7.21 seconds; total time was 2.5 minutes.

The sole review finding requires validation and its record.
No new test or mutation applies to that finding.
The eight output-budget pins retain the RED then GREEN mutation evidence above.

## Goldens moved

None. The `.nc` and `.cl` diff is empty.

## Not exercised

The user's private `sc_logo.camproj` was not available.
No physical PathPilot controller, GUI posting flow, or MCP posting flow was exercised.
The pins use synthetic streams through the shared whole and numbered per-operation post engine.

## Overlaps

None found for the changed source, test, or decision files.

title: feat(mcp): compact read modes and chat context budgets
body:
## What changed

MCP read modes for small context windows (`crates/app/src/mcp/`):

- `get_job` takes `summary: true`. The summary removes `machine.definition`. Each operation keeps only the `params` fields that differ from the kind defaults. Null and empty fields outside `params` are removed.
- `list_operation_types` takes `kind` (key or label) and `section`. An unknown name is refused with the valid names.
- `list_features` takes `compact: true`. Compact rows keep the id, the name and the pick facts. Counts replace the loops. The compact default `limit` is 25. The full default stays 500.
- `provider::tools_in(provider, ToolSet::Core)` gives a core set of 25 workflow tools. `tools(provider)` is unchanged.
- The new code is in `mcp/compact.rs`. `job.rs`, `features.rs`, `pick.rs` and `tools.rs` get small hooks only.

Chat worker limits (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/ai_chat/budget.rs`):

- A tool reply to the model is cut at 12000 JSON characters, with a hint that names the compact modes. The tool card keeps the full text.
- A request carries at most one viewport image (the newest).
- A turn stops after 12 model rounds. The old `MAX_TURN_STEPS` moved to `budget::MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` and now has a test.
- A request carries at most 6 earlier turns. When older turns are dropped, the latest `get_job` reply goes in front of the first kept prompt.
- A local endpoint gets the core tool set. A cloud endpoint gets the full table.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1944-ai-context-budgets.md`.

## Cause

Enhancement. The full tool table and one full `get_job` or `list_features` reply can fill the context window of a small local model.

## Tests

Pins (all new; network is not used):

- `crates/app/tests/mcp_compact.rs`: `get_job_summary_drops_the_machine_definition_and_default_fields`, `get_job_summary_refuses_a_non_boolean`, `list_operation_types_filters_by_kind_and_by_section`, `list_features_compact_rows_are_short_and_the_default_limit_is_chat_sized`, `the_core_tool_set_is_a_small_subset_of_the_full_table`. Each asserts a character budget.
- `egui_app::tests::ai_chat::budget`: `a_long_tool_reply_is_cut_to_the_character_cap_with_a_hint`, `a_local_model_gets_the_core_tool_set_and_a_cloud_model_the_full_table`, `a_turn_stops_at_the_round_cap`.
- `egui_app::ai_chat::budget::tests`: `a_cut_keeps_whole_characters_and_says_how_much_was_shown`, `a_small_reply_passes_and_a_long_one_is_one_capped_text_block`, `only_the_newest_image_goes_with_a_request`, `old_turns_are_dropped_and_the_latest_get_job_reply_is_kept`.

Mutation checks (old code put back, pin red; code restored, pin green):

- `job.rs` from upstream: the two `get_job` pins and the `list_operation_types` pin are red.
- `features.rs` from upstream: the `list_features` pin is red.
- Core filter turned off in `provider.rs`: the core set pin is red.
- `worker_mcp.rs` from upstream: the reply cap pin is red.
- `turn.rs` from upstream: the image pin and the history pin are red.
- `tool_set_for` gives `Full` to local: the tool set pin is red.
- Loop runs `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS + 1`: the round cap pin is red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (131 steps, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The branch merges cleanly with the current `upstream/main`.

## Goldens moved

None. No posted G-code changes.

## Not exercised

- A real provider endpoint. The tests use the scripted transport.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill does not list the new arguments yet. The tool schemas describe them.

## Overlaps

These open PRs touch the same files, in different functions or lines. Whichever merges second refreshes.

- #2836: `list_operation_types` (a field inside the loop; this PR changes the signature and the end).
- #2920 and #2716: `features.rs` views and `list_features`; `tools.rs` `list_features` row (this PR adds three lines in `list_features` and edits the `get_job` and `list_operation_types` rows).
- #2554, #2678, #2773: other rows and functions of `job.rs` and `tools.rs`.

Changelog: AI chat keeps large jobs inside the model's context: compact MCP read modes (`get_job` summary, `list_operation_types` kind/section filter, `list_features` compact), a core tool set for local models, and caps on tool reply size, images, rounds and history.

- The local Prompt-JSON context (`provider::prompt_context`) now starts with `RULES`. The old format sentence follows it without a change.
- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` is the generated reference: 116 tools, with their arguments and full descriptions.

Examples: `edit_machine`, `suggest_cutting_data`, `delete_tool`, `edit_tool`, `pick_in_box`, `electrode_from_faces`, `set_units`, `set_program`. A new paragraph tells how to get the reference and the local prompt.
- `tools::all` is now `pub(super)`, so that the catalog reads the same rows as `tools/list`.
- `docs/decisions/1947-mcp-single-source.md` records the choices.

## Cause

The skill, the guide and the local prompt were written by hand. Nothing compared them with the tool table, so they drifted.

## Tests

The new file `crates/app/tests/mcp_doc_drift.rs` has six pins:

- `the_committed_reference_matches_the_live_tool_table`: the failure message gives the command that writes the reference again.
- `every_tool_named_in_the_agent_docs_is_live`: it scans the Claude skill, the `.agents` skill, `GEMINI.md` and the guide.
- `every_live_tool_is_in_the_guide_and_the_local_prompt`
- `the_local_prompt_json_context_carries_the_shared_rules`

## What changed

The shipped sinker post can post Sinker Side Burn with explicit machine data.
The machine must state `edm.codes.side` with `{x}`, `{y}`, `{z}`, and `{f}`.

The post fills absolute endpoints in the work offset and converts coordinates and feed to the document units.

Straight burns still need no lateral code.

The decision is in `docs/decisions/3001-sinker-side-burn.md`.

title: fix(multiaxis): generate rotary contour rings about X
body:
## What changed

Rotary Contour generates rings around a cylindrical workpiece along X.
For a nearly horizontal axis, top and bottom specify axial ball-center stations.
Clearance and retract specify tool-tip radii about the fitted axis.
The planner reuses waterline contact geometry and radial links.
It refuses unsafe radii and invalid station bounds by name.
The decision record explains the parameter contract and alternatives.

## Cause

The station conversion divided world height by the fitted axis Z component.
An X axis has a zero Z component, so the generator refused it.
Removing that refusal alone would retain the invalid division and axial links.

## Tests

The initial geometry pin failed on unchanged upstream/main `97a880c53`.
The motion pins measure complete rings, axial bounds, radial poses, and link clearance:

All five passed after the fixed generator was restored.
