title: fix(import): read the STEP short name of the plane angle unit
body:
Stacked on #2927 (merge #2927 first).

## What changed

- The STEP model import expands two more ISO 10303-21 short names: `PLANUN` (`PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT`) and `GC` (`GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT`).
- The `GUAC` and `SUNT` names of #2927 move into the same table, in the new module `crates/kernel/src/step_units_guard.rs`.
- A new check refuses a file by name when a plane angle unit cannot be converted to radians.
- The check also refuses a unit that measures a plane angle but is not marked as one. An angle is never read in a unit that the file does not state.
- New fixture `testdata/models/short_units_degree_cone.step`. It is our own 1 degree draft frustum (base radius 10 mm, height 10 mm), with short-name units.
- The STEP agreement bench gets a `Truck::NotRecorded` variant. #2790 removed the truck reader, so a new fixture has no truck reading. The bench must not make one up.

## Cause

The pinned p21 parser leaves `PLANUN` short. The solidcore-step unit reader then does not find the plane angle unit and uses radians. The cone semi-angle of 1 degree was read as 1 radian. With our fixture, the pcurve check then refused the solid with a misleading reason: "an edge lies 8.32 mm off the face's surface". A file whose edges do not hold the surface could pass with the wrong shape.

The short names come from the issue's reading of the public ISO short-name registry (`PLANUN` at line 1554). I could not fetch the registry again in this session.

## Tests

Pins (red before the fix):

- `step_short_units::short_name_degree_cone_keeps_its_angle`: volume and top radius of the 1 degree frustum. Before the fix: refused, "an edge lies 8.32039972978102 mm off the face's surface".
- `step_short_units::unmarked_angle_unit_is_refused_by_name`: the degree unit without its marker is refused, and the message names `#13`. Before the fix: the misleading pcurve refusal.
- `step_units_guard::tests::short_name_context_reads_degrees_and_uncertainty`: degrees and the `GC` uncertainty are read.
- `step_units_guard::tests::angle_unit_on_a_steradian_is_refused`.

Controls (green before and after): `long_name_degree_cone_control_keeps_its_angle`, `degree_unit_passes_the_angle_check`, and the five #2927 tests.

Mutation results:

- M1: remove the `PLANUN` mapping. The cone pin is red, and the check alone refuses the file by name ("unit #13 measures a plane angle but is not marked..."). Restored: green.
- M2: remove the `GC` mapping. The uncertainty unit test is red (`uncertainty: None`). Restored: green.
- M3: remove the `check_angle_units` call. The refusal pin is red. Restored: green.
- M4: skip the base-unit check. The steradian unit test is red. Restored: green.

Gates on the final code:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base base-2927` (the head of #2927): 82 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "kernel heavy"`: 16 steps, 0 failed (lib, bins, agreement, blend, heal_import, import_corpus, machining_mesh_shortfalls, mesh_deviation_bench, solidcraft_hostile, solidcraft_import, step_agreement, step_closed_form, step_import, step_short_units, step_twisted_flank, doc).

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes of `motion` and `app` were not run. They are reached only through the crate dependency graph (the `lib.rs` change). They must run before this PR is ready.
- The bench's raw tessellator (test-only `step_util::solidcore_mesh`) does not expand short names. #2919 recorded the same for lengths. Its pinned verdict for the new fixture is its refusal. The app meshes the record from `read_step`, which is correct.

## Overlaps

- #2927 changes the same rename step in `read_guarded` (`crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs`). This PR is stacked on it.

Changelog: STEP import reads a plane angle unit given by its short name (PLANUN), and refuses by name an angle unit that it cannot read, so an angle in degrees is never read as radians.

Effort: high

Fixes #2973

title: fix(post): leave Agie jobs unarmed until the loaded work quality is verified
body:
Stacked on #2993. Review the [quality-binding correction above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/feb802a77a99878951d5faf5ba2f41f65270c018...ba5ff0ae123a87310a475692447f93a841d581a5).

A stale native quality can change the effective Ra, pass count and wire offsets while the controller formal check passes. A 40 mm Cobra trial bound the same 0.30 request to different existing records. The wrong selection ran three passes at 0.245, 0.165 and 0.140 mm. The intended selection ran four at 0.250, 0.170, 0.145 and 0.135 mm. A deliberately conflicting semantic name also defeated the returned handle and success-status checks after a new piece import.

CAMCraft now writes a complete native setup bundle and leaves every work with zero erosion steps. Geometry, start holes, work definitions and separation settings are present. The bundle records a stable quality name for the requested tuple and checks each assignment. The operator must review each effective native work in place before generating any machining steps. The operator can correct a mismatched quality without importing the piece again.

Check the actual wire, stock height, Ra, Tkm, Te and visible options in Work Details. For a mismatch, use Quality (Kwaliteit) and Define (Definiëren) on that same work. Confirm the requested values. Open Technology (Technologie), select TECCUT, and use Assign (Toewijzen) on the matching row. Check the individual working steps and their offsets before running GRAFICHECK and FORMALCHECK. The user guide gives the full procedure and the expected values for each supported setting. The native dialog exposes two of the three authored checkbox values.

On the deliberately polluted installation, a new import showed both works at [0]. FORMALCHECK reported a blocking technology error for each. Correcting Ra on the first work kept both at [0]. Explicit TECCUT assignment armed only the checked work. The installation retained the other unarmed work until its own review. The saved two-work piece then passed FORMALCHECK. GRAFICHECK produced 16 correctly ordered profile and separation blocks. All nine nominal faces had the verified 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm offsets. Both rough bridges measured 1.000 mm. The two cutting envelopes remained disjoint. The effective Ra 0.30 Berco process was checked independently at 15, 20, 40 and 80 mm. No physical cut was made.

The independent gate passed 96 app tests, 18 native post tests and three geometry tests. The app count includes machine, machine library and posting suites. It exported 20 jobs with 32 works. All 52 geometry and resource files matched previous output. Each of the 20 piece files changed from automatic machining to setup-only. Each repeat export preserved every file. Strict Clippy passed for the app, post, UI and geometry libraries. The final source revision reproduced all 72 files and reported working_steps_generated=false for all 20 jobs. The only change after that source revision is an operator guide sentence about the repeat-import result.

After manual release and plotting of both a mixed-radius Ra 0.30 piece and a rectangular Ra 0.35 piece, the tester reimported each exact SBL on its existing control. Each import created a new default-named piece with the intended ISO resource and zero steps. FORMALCHECK again reported technology undefined. The earlier named piece stayed separate. Select the newly created row and confirm its geometry and [0] before assigning the technology.

The real GUI status before the change reported the posted job. After the change it reports zero working steps, the requested targets, wire and stock values, and the required offsets. The two UI screenshots were checked locally. Public screenshot attachment is pending.

title: fix(app): judge the first traverse of a 3+2 plane against the machine table
body:
Stacked on #2985 (merge #2985 first). This PR has one commit of its own on top of the #2985 head `73e10f954`: `7e6e2ffe3`.

## What changed

- The first-traverse law (#2985) now reads the machine table on a 3+2 plane. Before, it skipped the table in each tilted frame.
- The law reads the table's top face over the stated X/Y travel. The table box is clipped to the Z travel, which starts at the table top. The 1e6 mm slab under the top face is out of the tool's reach.
- The law reads the table only when the head can tilt. The machine file states which rotaries turn the work (`turns_part`, #804). When each tilting rotary turns the work, the table stays under the work, and the law does not read the table.
- A mounted machine that states no X, Y and Z travel has no table box. A 3+2 plane on such a machine gets a note: "First traverse: the machine table is not judged on this tilted plane: ...". It is not a silent pass.
- Files: `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` (the predicate `work_tilts`, the clip `table_top_face`, the note), and `generate.rs` (passes the rotary list, adds the note to the path).
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2987-table-tilted-first-traverse.md`.

## Cause

- #2985 skipped the table in a tilted frame. A full read of the table box refused each indexed operation on the microARC 4.
- I measured why. A read of the top face alone still refused them: Z 190.5 at A 90 and Z 336.55 at A 180. Those refusals are false. The microARC 4 turns the work, so its table never stands over the plane.
- On a head-tilt machine the table is fixed in the world. The tilted plane drops toward it on its low side. That collision passed.

## Tests

New file `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_table.rs`. It uses a small test machine (X and Y travel +-100 mm, Z travel 0..300 mm) with three rigs: head tilt, work tilt, and head tilt with no travel.

- `a_head_tilt_plane_under_the_table_inside_the_travel_is_refused_by_name`: B 30 deg, plane 20 mm over the origin, table top face at 32.68 mm along the axis. The verdict is `FirstTraverseLow { fixture: true }` and the post is refused by name. **Red before the fix.**
- `a_head_tilt_machine_with_no_travel_names_the_table_unjudged`: the note is on the path. **Red before the fix.**
- `a_head_tilt_past_90_reads_the_table_top_face_not_its_slab`: B 120 deg. A plane 100 mm over the origin passes, and a plane 90 mm over it is refused at the top face (96.6 mm).
- `a_head_tilt_plane_over_the_table_top_face_passes`: control.
- `a_work_turning_rotary_keeps_the_table_under_the_work`: control, the same plane as the refused case.

Mutation checks (each run, then restored):
- The old `first_traverse.rs` and `generate.rs` from #2985: the refusal pin and the note pin fail.
- No top-face clip (the full slab): `a_head_tilt_past_90_reads_the_table_top_face_not_its_slab` fails.
- `work_turns = false`: `a_work_turning_rotary_keeps_the_table_under_the_work` fails.

Gate:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base base-2985` (the #2985 head; my diff only): 116 steps, 0 failed.
- These suites passed separately (45 binaries): `first_4axis_part`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `index_swing`, `index_swing_horizontal`, `tilt`, `tilt_a180`, `tilt_a180_routes`, `tilt_heights`, `tilt_basis_compat`, `stock_source_holes`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `first_router_part`, `tormach_fourth_axis`, the `wcs_*` suites and others.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes. The indexed example operations that posted on #2985 still post.

## Not exercised

- App heavy lanes: the [reviewer ran `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2997#issuecomment-7045080077) on this head trial-merged with main at `97a880c53`: 199 steps, 198 ok, 1 failed (`pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`). The reviewer reproduced the same failure with main's `first_traverse.rs` and `generate.rs`, so the failure is not from this PR.
- No machine run.
- The law runs at generation only (as in #2985). If the user loads a different machine after a generate, the first traverse is not judged again until the next generate. This gap is in #2985's design and also applies to the fixtures.
- A machine with a head tilt and a vertical work C: the table footprint is read without the C turn.
- An old project whose rotary has no `turns_part` is read as a head tilt (the conservative reading). It can be refused where it posted on #2985.

## Overlaps

- Stacked on #2985: the same function `operation::first_traverse::judge` and the `Over` struct. #2985 adds the file.
- No other open PR changes these files.

Changelog: The first rapid of a 3+2 operation on a head-tilt machine is now refused by name when its clearance plane goes under the machine table top inside the machine travel; a machine that states no travel gets a note that the table was not judged.

Effort: high

Refs #2985

title: feat(ui): draw the viewport overlay as wide anti-aliased lines, with MSAA
body: ## What changed The viewport overlay drew as `wgpu` lines. A `wgpu` line is always 1 hardware pixel and has no anti-aliasing. Toolpaths, height planes, outlines, triads and the ground grid now draw as wide anti-aliased lines. The viewport also has MSAA. - **Wide lines** (`crates/ui/src/viewport/wide.rs`): - Each segment is one 32-byte instance: two f32x3 points and two RGBA8 colours. The grid fades along a line, thus each end keeps its own colour. - The vertex shader makes a quad that faces the screen. The fragment shader fades the sides and the ends over 1 px. - The old 1 px `LineList` overlay pipeline is removed. - **Clean corners.** Each end reaches half the line width past its point. Two lines that meet close the corner and do not overlap past it. - **Depth lift.** Each vertex moves toward the eye by 3 line widths (`LIFT_WIDTHS`). The world size of one pixel comes from the `mvp` matrix, so the lift is correct in perspective and in orthographic projection. - The lift prevents this: without it, the depth test hid half of a line that lies on a face. - Effect: a line behind a face by less than 3 line widths shows through. This is a few pixels of depth on the screen. - **Near plane.** The shader clips a segment to the near plane before it calculates the screen direction. Thus an end behind the eye does not turn the quad over. - **Line width setting.** The choices are 1, 1.5, 2 and 3 pt. The default is 1.5 pt. The value is multiplied by the display's pixels per point, and the result is held to 1..16 px. - **Anti-aliasing setting.** The choices are Off, 2x and 4x. The default is 4x. - All viewport pipelines and the traced-stock composite use the same sample count. - A change rebuilds the pipelines and the multisample and depth targets one time. The resolved colour target stays, so the egui texture stays bound. - The traced stock writes one depth for each pixel. Thus its own edges are not smoothed, and its cost does not change. - **Sample counts that the device offers.** - Bring-up requests `TEXTURE_ADAPTER_SPECIFIC_FORMAT_FEATURES` when the adapter has it. The shell then reads the adapter's counts for the colour and depth formats. - Without the feature, only WebGPU's guaranteed counts 1 and 4 are offered. The browser build offers 1 and 4. - A row for a count that the device does not offer is disabled, and its hover text gives the reason. A queued pick of such a count is refused by name. - A kept count that the device does not offer falls back to the highest offered count below it. The status line says so one time. - **Where the settings are.** - They are in the viewport's Display menu (#2818), in its Graphics group, after the projection: "Line width" and "Anti-aliasing". The first version put them in the Theme door; a manual test found that place wrong (they are not part of a theme), so they moved when #2818 reached `main`. A general Settings window is proposed in #3025. - Like the other Display menu entries, a pick calls its `State` method directly (`select_line_width`, `select_antialias`). No command is queued. - They are kept in the per-user `view.json` (`app::view`), with the origin-name switch. A file word that the build does not know reads as the default and does not refuse the file. - They are not on the undo history and do not make the document unsaved, the same as the theme. - The origin-name switch now writes all the view settings, so it does not reset the line settings. - **File size.** The pipelines and the render targets moved to `viewport/pipes.rs` and are built through one helper. `viewport.rs` went from 1543 to 1265 lines. - **Docs.** - The guide has a short section "Line width and anti-aliasing" (`first-run.md`). - The decision record is `docs/decisions/2958-wide-overlay-lines.md`. ## Screenshots Before and after: 1 px lines without anti-aliasing (`main`), and 1.5 pt lines with 4x anti-aliasing (this PR, the defaults). The Display menu with the new "Line width" and "Anti-aliasing" entries in its Graphics group (2x is not offered on this device): The line widths: 1 pt with anti-aliasing Off, 1.5 pt with 4x (the default), and 3 pt with 4x: ## Readings Frame time: a 2560×1440 target, a release build and DX12, the median of 35 frames (submit and wait). The scene is one plate and a raster path at the overlay limit (512k segments), or a typical path (20k segments). "Before" is `main` at acd5b02d3 (1 px lines, no MSAA). "After" is 1.5 px wide lines. | GPU | Path | Before (1 px) | After, Off | After, 2x | After, 4x | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER | 20k segments | 0.17 ms | 0.20 ms | 0.26 ms | 0.29 ms | | NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER | 512k segments | 0.27 ms | 0.70 ms | 0.72 ms | 0.78 ms | | AMD Radeon (integrated) | 20k segments | 1.00 ms | 1.33 ms | 3.38 ms | 3.64 ms | | AMD Radeon (integrated) | 512k segments | 1.77 ms | 6.92 ms | 8.76 ms | 9.09 ms | On the integrated GPU, the cost is clear: - 4x adds approximately 2.3 ms to a typical frame at 1440p. - At the overlay limit, the frame is 9 ms. This is near the 10 ms frame target. The default 4x follows the issue. If the maintainer prefers the lower cost on integrated graphics, the default can change to 2x or Off. This is a one-word change (`Antialias::default`). - Upload (`set_overlay`) of 512k segments: 9.6 ms (NVIDIA) and 8.8 ms (AMD), against 7.1 ms and 7.0 ms before. The upload occurs only when the scene changes, not when the camera moves. - Overlay buffer at the limit: 16 MiB (32 bytes for each segment). Before, it was 24 MiB (two 24-byte vertices). - Without the lift, the pinning test counts 292 px of a 6 px line on a face against 628 px in the air. With the lift, the two counts are the same. ## Pinning tests - `crates/ui/tests/gpu_render/wide_lines.rs` (in the `gpu_render` binary): - `a_line_on_a_face_keeps_its_full_width`: fails without the lift (292 vs 628 px). - `two_lines_that_meet_close_the_corner_and_do_not_reach_past_it`. - `the_line_width_setting_widens_the_band`. - `msaa_smooths_the_edges_that_one_sample_leaves_hard`. - `crates/ui/tests/trace_composite.rs`: `the_traced_stock_paints_the_same_with_msaa`. The 4x pass with the composite has no validation error. - `crates/ui/src/viewport/wide_tests.rs`: - `each_segment_is_one_32_byte_instance` - `an_odd_vertex_and_bad_colours_never_reach_the_gpu_as_garbage` - `the_line_width_scales_with_the_display_and_stays_in_range` - `an_unoffered_sample_count_falls_back_to_the_highest_offered_below_it` - `the_shader_lifts_by_the_documented_widths` - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/display_quality.rs`: - `the_defaults_are_one_and_a_half_points_and_four_samples` - `a_line_width_pick_is_kept_survives_a_restart_and_undo_leaves_it` - `an_offered_antialias_pick_is_kept_and_an_unoffered_one_is_disabled` - `the_graphics_group_offers_the_line_widths_and_the_antialiasing` - `a_pick_of_an_unoffered_count_is_refused_by_name_and_not_kept` - `crates/app/tests/view_file.rs`: `the_line_width_and_the_antialias_round_trip`. ## Gates - `main` was merged into the branch (b78bef768). The conflicts were with #2818 (display modes): `viewport.rs` keeps the hidden-edge stage and the `draw_list::plan` loop of `main`, with its pipelines from `viewport/pipes.rs`. `app/view.rs` and `state_view.rs` keep the fields of both sides. - Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) on bdea342b6: 22 steps, 0 failed (2.3 min). - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. - Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`) on the final head bdea342b6: the change in `app::view` reaches all the `app` heavy lanes. 199 steps ran in 29.2 min, and 198 are green. The known-fail markers are red as expected. (The run on 0cd1a634f, before the merge of `main`, had the same result: 201 steps, 200 green.) - One step is red: `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (got `(3158, 3130, 1141)`). The same test on the base commit `acd5b02d3` (`main`, without this PR) fails with the same triple. This PR does not touch the planner. The only `app` change is the view-settings file, which the test does not read. The planner triple is exact for each measured platform (#1010, see #984 and #1402). ## Not exercised - The browser (wasm) build is not compiled here: the target is not installed on this machine. The `shell_web.rs` change only passes the existing `scale` value to `view_pass::encode`. - macOS and Linux devices are not tested. The tested devices are NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER and AMD Radeon integrated graphics (DX12), and the software adapter (Microsoft Basic Render Driver) in the test suite. - The pixel goldens (`docs/images/`, the snapshot PNGs) are release-lane and change at the cut, not in this PR. - MCP: none. These are per-user screen settings like the theme and the colour vision, which also have no MCP tool. They do not change the document. ## Effort The issue has `effort:medium`. The work went to two crates (`app::view` for the kept settings) and to the GPU bring-up, so `effort:high` fits it better. The maintainer decides. Changelog: The viewport draws toolpaths, height planes and the other overlay lines as anti-aliased lines 1.5 pt wide, and smooths edges with 4x MSAA. The viewport's Display menu (Graphics) sets the line width (1–3 pt) and the anti-aliasing (Off, 2x, 4x). Fork synced at v0.24.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 111). The control requested manual setup and reported option 131072 at both works. No physical cut was made.

The independent gate passed 25 scoped app tests, 17 native post tests and strict Clippy for the app, geometry and post libraries. The final integrated branch reproduced all four controller-tested files byte for byte.

title: feat(post): emit Agie straight cutoffs with separate air endpoints
body:
Stacked on #2969. Review the [open cutoff changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/a6e3a1310cae5f94df32b930c7e4a44da8b54845...980ed2af14fef01a6a1129ef973518563ed1d9ac).

Post one straight open cutoff on a selected retained wall. Set left or right compensation from the operation. The ISO line is nominal. The native job uses separate entry and exit points beyond opposite faces of the stock. The post checks the approach, wire radius, rough offset and centered XY travel. This first cutoff process uses 20 mm stock.

The main cut separates the stock before the three trims. The operator must confirm that both pieces remain independently clamped through all passes. A separate confirmation locates the stock center at the midpoint of the machine travel. Both operation settings default to false when loading an older project. The existing capture setting can describe a catcher.

Run either original example from the repository root:

```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/cutoff-lower.camscript
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/cutoff-upper.camscript
```

The actual offline control ran four alternating traversals for both native sides. Each pass crossed the stock once along the 88 mm line. At a nominal Y of −6, the left cut measured Y −5.755, −5.845, −5.860 and −5.866 mm. The right cut gave the mirrored values about positive Y 6. All other cutting moves stayed in air. Both formal checks had zero job errors. The control requested machining and reference setup and reported option 131072. No physical cut was made.

All 16 scoped cutoff, die and native integration tests passed. The wire DTO test, 13 native post tests and all nine wire page tests passed, including Apply and Undo for the new fields. Strict Clippy passed for the app, motion, post and UI libraries. The before and after screenshots show the Passes page in the tested application.

![Passes before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/5ec50c1daf4a1973250c2c14390e74ec97c8f870/before.png)

![Passes after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/5ec50c1daf4a1973250c2c14390e74ec97c8f870/after.png)

Effort: high
Changelog: Native Agie wire posting supports a checked straight open cutoff in 20 mm stock. It requires distinct outside endpoints and explicit confirmations of clamping and stock placement.

Fixes #2962

body:
**Apply the quality-binding correction in #2984 before machine use or merge.** These offsets describe the measured resident selection. A colliding quality name can select a different process, so the effective recipe and its rough clearance require the corrected binding.

Stacked on #2955. Review the [height changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/6b790f4dd6aa0f4e37feeb03bd16b911fb19d664...4915595814341646b6d5e26160084754c5467b36).

Use a measured rough-pass offset for each supported QN2 stock height. Apply it to the stock and corner clearance checks. Require the work to span the stock, with the work zero at its top. Unlisted heights and unsupported machine settings still refuse.

| Stock height (mm) | Rough (mm) | Trim 1 (mm) | Trim 2 (mm) | Trim 3 (mm) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 15 | 0.245 | 0.155 | 0.140 | 0.134 |
| 20 | 0.245 | 0.155 | 0.140 | 0.134 |
| 40 | 0.260 | 0.170 | 0.140 | 0.130 |
| 80 | 0.266 | 0.176 | 0.143 | 0.133 |

These are straight-face offsets from the native controller plot for the supported Berco Cut 0.25 mm wire, material and QN2 selection. The control owns the individual passes. Each new CAMCraft job produced eight plotted cut blocks including the 1 mm separation section. The threading hole and stock extended to the specified depth. The formal check reported no job error. The control requested machine and reference setup, and reported option 131072. No physical machine cut was made.

The 87 post library tests and all 10 native app integration tests passed. The app test qualified_qn2_heights_set_both_piece_and_work_with_stock_top_at_zero checks the stock and work Z spans. Strict Clippy passed for the app and post libraries.

Effort: high
Changelog: Native Agie QN2 posting now accepts verified 15, 40 and 80 mm stock heights in addition to 20 mm. Corner checks use the measured rough-pass offset for the selected thickness.

body:
## What changed

Add `examples/catalog/2d/adaptive-pocket` with an original U-shaped open pocket.
Include the mesh generator, mesh, build script, portable project, NC program, and README.
Run 2D Adaptive before 2D Pocket with the same 6 mm end mill.
Adaptive leaves 0.5 mm on the walls and floor.
Pocket removes these allowances and reaches Z6.
The README explains the extra corner scallops and material left in sharp corners.

## Cause

The catalog had no case for Adaptive roughing followed by Pocket finishing.
The existing commands already support this sequence.
No machining algorithm changes are needed.

## Tests

- Pin: `adaptive_pocket_case_roughs_above_the_finished_floor_then_finishes`.
- The pin failed before the case existed. It passes with the case.
- Mutation: remove the new NC file to restore the upstream absence. The pin fails, then passes after restoration.
- Mutation: change the Adaptive wall allowance from 0.5 to 0. The pin fails, then passes after restoration.
- Mutation: change the Adaptive bottom from Z6.5 to Z6. The pin fails, then passes after restoration.
- Mutation: change the Pocket wall allowance from 0 to 0.5. The pin fails, then passes after restoration.
- Mutation: change the Pocket bottom from Z6 to Z6.5. The pin fails, then passes after restoration.
- `cargo xtask catalog --check`: all six cases pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: all five tests pass.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: all three steps pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passes.

The new case has no prior file on `upstream/main` to restore with `git show`.
Each mutation restores the exact original fixture bytes.
The pin checks operation types, order, allowances, posted depths, and model portability.
The catalog tests regenerate, verify, rebuild from the script, and compare NC bytes.

## Goldens moved

One new golden: `examples/catalog/2d/adaptive-pocket/adaptive-pocket.nc`.
It contains 13,325 lines for Adaptive roughing to Z6.5 and Pocket finishing to Z6.
The diff adds only this case's program. No existing NC or CL golden changes.

## Not exercised

No physical CNC machine was run.
Both operations omit a holder.
Verification checks for gouges. It does not prove complete stock removal.
The cutter leaves material in sharp inside corners.
Pocket recuts the selected region. This case does not demonstrate rest machining.

## Overlaps

None. The pin uses a new test file and leaves the shared catalog test unchanged.

Effort: medium

Changelog: Add an open-pocket example with 2D Adaptive roughing and 2D Pocket finishing.

Fixes #2860

title: fix(build): report each catalog case with a time budget
body:
## What changed

Each catalog case has separate `regenerates` and `rebuilds` tests.
The five cases now have ten independent workflow results.
The suite has 16 tests, up from five. No test is ignored.
Each workflow has a 60-second wall-clock budget.
Each workflow prints its name, elapsed time, and budget, including when it fails.
Shared assertions move to a helper module. Both source files stay below 400 lines.
Each rebuild removes only its own scratch directory.
The existing NC comparisons and portability checks remain in place.

## Cause

Two loops ran all cases inside two tests.
The first failed assertion stopped each loop.
The tests did not measure or limit each case.

## Tests

Pins:

- `contract::every_case_has_two_named_test_results` checks both workflow names for every discovered case.
- `contract::two_broken_cases_report_both_names_and_times` checks two named failures and their times in each workflow.
- `support::a_case_over_its_budget_fails_by_name` checks a named timeout and its heavy-lane guidance.

The first two pins failed on unchanged upstream/main `61a817bed` before the fix.
Both pass with the fix.
The budget pin passes with a 1 ms limit and a 50 ms worker.

Mutation checks:

- Restoring the original file and retaining the contract pins makes both pins fail. Restoring the fix makes both pass.
- Replacing `recv_timeout` with unbounded `recv` makes the budget pin fail. Restoring the timeout makes it pass.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passes all 16 tests.
All ten workflows run in debug mode. Their times range from 0.256 to 12.415 seconds in the gate.
The first full debug run took at most 21.617 seconds for a case.
All cases stay below the budget, so none moves to the heavy lane.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

The release heavy lanes, UI, and a real machine did not run.
A real hanging model did not run. The timeout pin uses a sleeping worker.
The timeout bounds the test result. It cannot cancel the worker thread.

## Overlaps

#2913 touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
It adds `slots_case_posts_a_slot_and_a_trochoidal_slot_to_the_same_floor` and its helper.
It does not change the two loops replaced here.
Its new catalog case will also need two workflow tests when the changes combine.

Changelog: none (test structure and timing only)

Effort: medium

Fixes #2857

Compute the separation clearance along the entry face. Keep compensation at the control and preserve the source vertices. A reentrant profile still refuses.

The original sample uses five straight sides and an oblique 3:4 entry face. The hole is at X-20.5 Y6 and the perpendicular seam is at X-12.5 Y0. The material, wire, stock thickness and QN2 settings are the same as in #2951.

Run the example using a new POLY20 destination:
```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/oblique-punch.camscript
```

The CLI preserved the original rectangular output byte for byte. On the oblique job it preserved all nominal vertices and the hole position. A tight acute corner and a separation or lead shorter than 3 mm produced a refusal and no output directory. Head 6b790f4dd handles a perpendicular foot between five-decimal grid points. The post keeps the hole fixed and selects an exterior point within 0.00001 mm of the true foot. It checks both split lengths and the approach using the emitted coordinates. It refuses a near-limit face if a valid grid point cannot preserve the required clearances. On the final head all 86 native post library tests and strict all-targets Clippy passed. The control plotted SLOPE20, a 7:10 face, with the four expected exterior offsets and a 1 mm final section.

Pinning tests: oblique_punch_preserves_nominal_vertices_and_perpendicular_seam and an_acute_miter_needs_more_stock_than_a_round_corner. The rough-pass 1 mm separation section followed the oblique face from X-12.696 Y0.147 to X-12.096 Y0.947. The control returned to the original hole at X-20.5 Y6. Stock was Z-20 to Z0. No physical machine cut was made.

Effort: high

**Hold for the quality-binding correction in PR #2999 for #2984 before machine use or merge.** A preexisting controller quality with the same generic name can select a different target, pass count and wire offset. The original tests establish the plotted geometry on the tested control. They do not establish the requested quality on another installation.

Stacked on #2948. The parent is a fork branch. This draft targets upstream main. Review the [native writer changes above the machine template](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/08601a2bc50abcbe2e550c86d3f9e708cbd49071...83affaca1bf4920ed07e29bf7c52bf9c48561b80).

## Change

The desktop Post command and cam.post write a native Agie job directory with linked ISO, SBR and SBL files. CamCraft writes the nominal contour in Rust and selects resident control technology. The post validates the work before it creates the destination. It publishes all three files together and preserves an existing directory.

The supported case is one vertical rectangular punch in 20 mm stock. Select the Classic 2S template from #2948. Enter the AGIE_QN2 condition for Berco Cut 0.25 mm wire and cold die steel. Select the 1.0 mm separation cut explicitly. The template starts without an installed condition. A cut needs 0.4 mm clearance at each stock face and 3 mm of straight face on each side of the entry. Other contours, tapers, skims, custom X/Y travel limits and additional workpieces are refused.

## Reference material for review

The contributor's team wrote [Agie-CAM at 11b1bb9](https://github.com/qsmits/Agie-CAM/tree/11b1bb9ef2c752b94b6fefc1f0814acd2e030c42) and released it under the MIT license. This draft retains the license and copyright notice. The implementation reference documents observed controller examples for parts of the JEScript sequence and the resident technology selection. The published guides linked on #2945 give the file roles and some interface arguments. They do not document the full sequence and all defaults. Please review that source against the project rules before merge.

The controller supplies its own runtime and technology table. This PR includes the writer and original synthetic examples and expected output. It includes no controller image, vendor post, runtime library or technology database.

## Control verification

The offline Classic Cut 2S control imported a CamCraft-generated 40 by 20 mm punch. Its formal check reported zero errors. It reported warnings for setup, reference values and selected option 131072. Its graphical check plotted the rough pass and three trims outside the nominal punch. Their straight-face offsets were 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm. The first passes skipped a 1 mm segment. A later sequence cut that segment and returned to the threading hole at X-30 Y0. The simulated stock extended from Z0 to Z-20. No physical machine cut was made.

The synthetic example runs from the repository root:
```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/punch.camscript
```
Use a new PUNCH40 destination.

## Final head checks

At head 83affaca1, all nine native application integration tests passed. The tests include the_native_files_match_the_control_checked_rectangular_punch, qn2_requires_the_rough_wire_size_in_the_mounted_condition and the_work_must_fit_between_each_stated_guide. The ordinary command script generated three files identical byte for byte to the earlier offline control input.

The unconfigured machine, absent or wrong condition role, missing wire diameter, and missing or unsupported separation each produced a diagnostic and no output directory. Independent verification passed 93 scoped checks: 81 app integration tests, four native writer tests, one geometry test, six existing Post dialog tests and one actual desktop Post button check. Both GUI and CLI output matched all three controller input files byte for byte. Strict all-targets Clippy passed on camcraft-app, camcraft-post, camcraft-geometry and camcraft-ui.

The quick planner selected a 983-step workspace batch. The heavy planner selected 248 steps. Only the plans ran for those full gates. This PR remains a draft.

## Desktop Post dialog

| Before (Generic ISO) | After (native Agie) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Generic ISO Post dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/625ef345a047980ab6974df99ea8ca2ac5f783b2/before.png) | ![Native Agie Post dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/625ef345a047980ab6974df99ea8ca2ac5f783b2/after.png) |

Effort: high
Changelog: The Wire EDM desktop and script workflows can post a supported Classic Cut 2S punch as a native Agie job directory.

Fixes #2945

body:
## Change

Add the AGIECUT Classic 2S wire EDM machine template to the desktop and embedded machine libraries. Mounting the template preserves the selected post.

The template states the X/Y rapid speed of 900 mm/min, the Z/U/V rapid speed of 600 mm/min and U/V travel of ±70 mm. It lists the four standard wire sizes from 0.20 to 0.33 mm. The X/Y/Z stroke lengths appear in the description. The operator supplies the installed datum, guide planes and cutting conditions. The handbook qualifies its maximum taper angle by guide type and work height.

The native job post is separate work in #2945. This change does not select an Agie dialect.

## Source

[AGIE, AGIECUT Classic technical handbook, edition 06.2002 C2.1](https://static.gindumac.com/products/9ccc9b7e-b589-49db-9843-eff1da09434c/documents/ES-EDM-AGI-2002-00001.pdf). Section 1.1 on printed page 4 identifies the model group, travels and speeds. Section 5.2 on printed page 44 lists the wire sizes.

## Verification

Independent checks used head 08601a2bc. All 68 tests in machine, machine_library, mcp_wire_contour and posting passed. Clippy passed on all camcraft-app targets with warnings denied.

The pinning tests are:
- agiecut_classic_2s_exposes_the_sourced_axes_and_wire_sizes
- agiecut_template_refuses_a_wire_job_without_an_installed_condition
- every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks_its_declaration

The normal command script selected the exact library name and mounted AGIECUT CLASSIC 2S. An attempted wire job with C110 failed with a missing-condition diagnostic. It created no NC file. Physical travel and cutting were not tested.

The full quick gate passed 250 of 251 steps in 36.0 minutes. The failing test was a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_operation. Both the branch and its base safely refused the missing machine with the setup name. The assertion expected an operation name. Neither replay created NC.

The reached heavy gate passed 198 of 199 steps in 41.8 minutes. The failing pocket3d_hsm bore test measured 3158 moves, 3130 planar moves and 1141 arcs on macOS ARM64. Base commit 20c81cbc1 reproduced the exact same diagnostic. See #2371 for the platform-specific measurement.

The standalone Generic ISO wire post also reported missing machine codes on a committed contour stream. This template supplies neither a native writer nor an installed condition. The PR remains a draft.

Effort: medium
Changelog: The machine library includes an AGIECUT Classic 2S wire EDM template with the manufacturer's stated axes, rapid speeds and standard wire sizes.

Fixes #2946

title: ci(gate): batch lanes for separate runners (--lane N/M) and gate-verdict
body:
This PR is the `xtask` part of #2908. It does not change `post-merge.yml`. The issue stays open for the workflow.

## What changed

- `cargo xtask gate batch --lane N/M` runs lane N of M of the batch plan (new module `xtask/src/lane_split.rs`).
  - The split is a round-robin deal in plan order. It reads no timing file. Thus each runner computes the same lanes for the same commit.
  - Each test step and clippy is in exactly one lane. The steps that share the machine are dealt first, then the steps that run alone (`lanes::ISOLATED`, ui, clippy).
  - A lane keeps the `debug build: <crate>` step of each crate that it tests.
  - `--lane 1/1` is the full batch plan of today.
  - The batch plan of this repository has 973 steps. Three lanes get 325, 324 and 324 steps.
- A lane run writes `lane-result.tsv` into its `gate-logs/batch-<stamp>/` (new module `xtask/src/verdict.rs`). The record has the lane, the runner name (`RUNNER_NAME`), the result, the wall time, the planned step count and one row for each step that ran.
- `cargo xtask gate-verdict <dir>...` reads the records below the directories and prints one Markdown verdict. The verdict names each lane, its runner, its time, its result and its record path, then each red step with its note. The exit code is 0 for green and 1 for red.
- Refusals, each with a message:
  - `--lane` on a tier that is not `batch`.
  - A lane that is not `N/M` with `1 <= N <= M <= 16`.
  - A lane with no step.
- The verdict is red when a lane has no record, has two records, is void, ran fewer steps than its plan, or has a record that cannot be read.
- `xtask/src/exec.rs`: the field `clock` of `Run` is `pub(crate)`, so that the record can read the wall time.
- `.claude/skills/gate/SKILL.md`: a section "Batch lanes for separate runners" and the flag row.
- `docs/decisions/2908-batch-lanes.md`: the decisions.

## Cause

The batch tier had no deterministic way to run as parts. `post-merge.yml` thus runs all 973 steps in one job on one runner, and the second runner waits. A lane job also had no result file that a collector could read.

## Tests

Pins, in `xtask/src/lane_split_tests.rs` and `xtask/src/verdict_tests.rs` (14 tests):

- `each_batch_step_runs_in_exactly_one_lane` (the real batch plan, 1 to 6 lanes: no step lost, no step in two lanes)
- `one_lane_of_one_is_the_whole_batch_plan`
- `a_lane_builds_each_crate_that_it_tests_before_the_tests`
- `the_lanes_share_the_queued_and_the_alone_steps_evenly`
- `the_split_is_the_same_on_each_call_and_reads_no_timing_file`
- `a_bad_lane_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_lane_with_no_step_is_an_error_not_a_green_run`
- `a_record_reads_back_as_written`
- `a_damaged_record_is_an_error`
- `all_lanes_green_is_a_green_verdict_that_names_each_lane`
- `a_red_step_is_named_with_its_lane_runner_and_note`
- `a_missing_a_double_a_void_or_a_short_lane_is_red`
- `the_runner_name_comes_from_the_environment`
- `the_collector_finds_the_records_of_downloaded_artifacts`

Red before the change: `cargo xtask gate batch --lane 1/2 --dry-run` on `upstream/main` `0306743de` gives `xtask: unknown gate option '--lane'`.

Mutation results (each mutation made the named pin red; the restored code is green):

| Mutation | Red pins |
|---|---|
| The alone steps get no lane | `each_batch_step_runs_in_exactly_one_lane` and 3 others |
| No build step is kept | `a_lane_builds_each_crate_that_it_tests_before_the_tests`, `one_lane_of_one_is_the_whole_batch_plan` |
| `N > M` is accepted | `a_bad_lane_is_refused_by_name`, `a_damaged_record_is_an_error` |
| An empty lane is not an error | `a_lane_with_no_step_is_an_error_not_a_green_run` |
| `--lane` is accepted on each tier | `a_bad_lane_is_refused_by_name` |
| A missing lane is not a fault | `a_missing_a_double_a_void_or_a_short_lane_is_red`, `the_collector_finds_the_records_of_downloaded_artifacts` |
| A short lane is not a fault | `a_missing_a_double_a_void_or_a_short_lane_is_red` |
| A void lane is not a fault | `a_missing_a_double_a_void_or_a_short_lane_is_red` |
| The red steps are not listed | `a_red_step_is_named_with_its_lane_runner_and_note` |

With the `main.rs` of `upstream/main` restored, the new test modules are not part of the build, and no pin runs. That restore is not a red test. The CLI error above is the red reading.

Readings on Linux:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (`xtask unit tests`, 251 s).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --lane 1/3 --dry-run`: 9 builds, then 325 of 973 steps. Lane 3: 324 steps.
- One real lane step: `cargo xtask gate batch --lane 1/3 --only "cl suites: lib"` was green and wrote `lane-result.tsv`.
- `cargo xtask gate-verdict gate-logs` on that one record: verdict RED, exit code 1, "lane 2/3 has no record" and "lane 3/3 has no record". This is correct for one lane of three.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- No full lane ran. Only one step of lane 1/3 ran for real.
- No GitHub Actions run. No workflow uses the lanes. The record was not written on a self-hosted runner, so `RUNNER_NAME` was not set (the record said `unknown`).
- Windows and macOS.
- The time balance of the lanes. The lanes have equal step counts, not equal measured times.

## Overlaps

- #2606 (`needs-maintainer`) changes the `report` job of `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`. This PR does not change that file. The workflow part of #2908 waits for the decision on #2606.
- #2787 (`needs-rework`, `conflicts`) changes `parse_gate` and `gate` in `xtask/src/main.rs` (a new tier). It touches the same functions, different lines. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2910 and #2915 list many `xtask/` files because their branches carry a process file sync. They do not change the lane code.

Process change: yes
Changelog: none
Effort: high

Refs #2908

title: fix(geometry): preserve faces and edges on touching solids
body:
Stacked on #2904 (merge #2904 first)

The prerequisite merged as bac4a96c while this work was in progress.
The merge-base diff now contains only the changes for #2845.

## What changed

- Link contact-face fragments only when a four-use edge has one complete matching.
- Keep existing two-use bodies together. Check all shared edges after the links.
- Preserve the closure, winding and outward-volume checks.
- Keep all incident facets until the feature graph checks the contact. Emit one facet pair for each valid solid.
- Store two edge uses inline. Allocate extra storage only for edges with more uses.
- Enable both known-fail pins for #2845. Add geometry pins for whole-face contact and line-only refusal.
- Require a contour over two closed solids in one model to match the single-block reference cut.

## Cause

A contact face can have no plain boundary edge. Plain-edge links then leave that face apart from its solid.
The feature graph kept only three incident facets. It marked every edge with more than two uses as non-manifold.

The old stitching test called two complete outward cubes one self-touching body because they shared one model.
That fixture is the legal whole-face contact case in this issue. The updated test compares the complete cut and verification result.

## Tests

These four pins failed on unchanged production code. They passed after the fix:

- `solids_that_touch_face_to_face_are_two_outward_bodies`
- `no_pickable_edge_is_a_tangent_piece_of_a_longer_one_in_any_step_fixture`
- `solids_sharing_a_whole_face_slice_as_one_outline`
- `a_whole_contact_face_keeps_each_solids_features`

`sample_ap214.step` had 216 tangent edge pairs that picked apart. The pin now finds none.
The face-to-face stack changed from one `NonManifold` verdict to two `Outward` bodies.

The pairing unit tests pass. They cover ambiguity, odd and unbalanced uses, zero edges, invalid apices and pinched bodies.
The full winding, feature, slicing and shared-face safety suites pass. The sample generates finish and pocket paths with no gouge.

Mutation checks:

- Restore the old upstream slicer caller: the slice pin fails. Restore the fix: it passes.
- Restore the old upstream winding caller: the winding pin fails. Restore the fix: it passes.
- Restore the old upstream feature builder: the feature pin fails. Restore the fix: it passes.
- Restore the parent's old slicer: `touching_closed_solids_in_one_model_cut_as_their_union` fails. Restore the fix: it passes.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` selected the batch plan. It completed 972 steps.
971 steps passed. The only failure was the old refusal assertion for the legal whole-face contact fixture.
After that expected-change test was updated, the failed-step gate passed all six `stitch_cross` tests.
Production code did not change between these gate runs.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
The full gate's clippy check also passed for all eight crates.

## Final-head verification requested by review

Head: `3121d66caed46a2bbcb1168b471247f20f9945fb`.

The latest review requested a fix for the reached `pocket3d_hsm` heavy-test failure and a green reached heavy gate.
The Linux pin still described the old 952-facet truck mesh.
PR #2904 replaced that mesh with the 6228-facet solidcore mesh at the same chord cap.
Decision #917 records the mesh change. The fixture and HSM planner did not change.
The new mesh changes the cutting regions and fitted arcs. Rejected arc fits retain their safe chords.

The Linux pin now requires exactly `(3158, 3130, 1141)` moves, planar feeds and arcs.
The heavy test also requires 6228 imported facets and all four cutting levels: Z 0, 5, 10 and 15.
The clean verification, fallback and planning-budget checks remain in place.
The new `the_linux_x86_64_bore_count_pin_is_exact` test rejects six adjacent count variants.

Pinning tests:

- `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`
- `the_linux_x86_64_bore_count_pin_is_exact`

Mutation check: restore only the old Linux tuple `(4726, 4698, 549)`.

`the_linux_x86_64_bore_count_pin_is_exact` fails at line 219.

Motion: 56 tests passed. Two known-fail pins failed as expected.

title: fix(chamfer): a wall that leans in the frame is not a modelled chamfer
body:
## What changed

A 2D Chamfer with no picks generates again on a box stock under a tilted frame.
The check of #2887 no longer reads a wall that leans in the operation frame as a modelled chamfer.

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs`: the new functions `leans` and `centroid`, the constant `LEAN_SLACK`, and one call in `partly_bevelled`.
- `docs/decisions/2936-chamfer-leaning-wall.md`: the decision record.

No fixture changes. `crates/app/tests/stock_source_holes.rs` is not touched.

## Cause

The fixture of #1700 is a 70 x 70 x 20 box stock with no part. The operation frame is tilted 10 degrees.
In that frame the top section (Z10) and the corner section (Z9) are the same rectangle. The top section is moved 0.176327 mm (`1 mm * tan(10 deg)`) in Y.
`partly_bevelled` (#2887, PR #2894) compares each segment of the top loop with the wall loop.
It read the segments that touch the moved corners as bevelled. It read the middle segments of the X sides as sharp.
It then refused the loop with "carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length".
No edge of the box carries a chamfer. The refusal was wrong for this model.

The loops of the fixture (from a debug print, not committed):

- top: X -35..35, Y -33.776662..37.303201
- corner: X -35..35, Y -33.952989..37.126874

## The fix

`leans(top, wall)` is true when the top loop is the wall loop moved whole by one plan vector.
The vector is the difference of the two area centroids. A collinear vertex does not change an area centroid.
Each segment of each ring (two ends and the middle) must then be on the other ring within `LEAN_SLACK` (1e-4 mm).
When `leans` is true, `partly_bevelled` returns `None`. `ride_loops` then rides the wall at the corner depth, as it did before #2887.

A loop that carries a bevel on part of its length is not a moved copy of its wall. Its bevelled side moves in and its sharp sides stay.
Thus the refusal of #2887 holds for each case that it was written for.

## Tests

Pins:

- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::a_wall_leaning_in_the_frame_is_not_a_modelled_chamfer` (motion lib, new). It uses the loops of the fixture.
- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::a_moved_outline_with_one_side_bevelled_still_refuses` (motion lib, new). It guards the other direction.
- `framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number` (app, `stock_source_holes`, not changed). This is the test of the issue.

Red before the fix, on `upstream/main` afbf1590e:

- The app test fails with the text of the issue (`... carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length - it is sharp near X-35.000 Y-16.176 ...`).
- The new unit pin fails with the same text.

Mutation results:

- The call `leans(top, wall)` disabled: the new unit pin is red, and the app test is red with the text of the issue. Restored: the two are green.
- `leans` replaced by `true`: `a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_by_name`, `a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_with_an_extra_vertex_too` and `a_moved_outline_with_one_side_bevelled_still_refuses` are red. Restored: green.

The old file was not copied back whole, because the new tests are in the same file. The disabled call gives the old behaviour.

Gate on the final source:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 4 steps, 0 failed (motion lib, `chamfer_modelled_edge`, `chamfer_partly_bevelled`).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test stock_source_holes`: 9 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test chamfer_partly_bevelled --test chamfer_modelled_edge`: 2 and 7 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

The quick gate did not select `stock_source_holes`. Its gate map does not name `motion::machining2d::chamfer_ride`. I ran the suite by hand.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes and the release tier.
- A tilted frame on a part with curved walls. The unit pin uses a rectangle only.
- A part with a draft wall on some sides only, in an upright frame. Its two sections are the same as those of a modelled chamfer on those sides. The check of #2887 still refuses it and asks for picks. This PR does not change that.
- macOS and Windows.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs` or the `stock_source_holes` files.

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer with no picks on a stock or part whose walls lean in a tilted operation frame generates again; it was refused as "a modelled chamfer on only part of its length".

Effort: high

Fixes #2936

title: fix(kernel): divide a runaway strip face over its boundary nodes
body:
## What changed

- The kernel seam divides a face with a runaway triangle count a second time, over its boundary nodes only.
- The new division is the Delaunay fill of the boundary loop of the face. It adds no node. It keeps each shared edge node as it is.
- The seam keeps the new division only when `mesh_deviation::measure_within` proves it inside the tolerance. If not, the face keeps the triangles of the planner.
- The measure of the whole plan runs after that, as before. The guarantee of a machining mesh does not change.
- A kept division is a note in the mesh report: `face N: divided over its K boundary nodes (...)`.
- The known-fail marker of the thread flank test is removed. The test runs in the default suite again.

New files:

- `crates/kernel/src/mesh_redivide.rs`: the selection of the faces, the boundary loop, the checks, the measure.
- `crates/kernel/src/mesh_redivide_fill.rs`: the polygon fill (ear clipping, then Lawson flips).
- `crates/kernel/tests/machining_mesh_redivide.rs`: the test of the tolerance gate.
- `docs/decisions/2844-strip-division.md`: the decisions.

A face is divided again only if it has 10 000 planned triangles or more, and 16 or more for each boundary node. A face with a hole, a pole or a period is not divided.

## Cause

solidcore-tess plans the long, thin helicoid strip isotropically. Our seam (`machining_mesh::planned`) could only pick the chord. The replan at half the chord made the count larger.

Options 1 and 2 of the issue are changes in `NeoTech/solidcore`. This PR is option 3 of the issue comment of 2026-11-20: the seam replaces the inside division of one face.

## Readings

Four-turn thread flank at 5e-3 mm, debug build:

| Plan | Planner | Boundary division | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| chord 5e-3 mm | 274192 triangles | 926 triangles | 7.3e-3 mm, not kept |
| chord 2.5e-3 mm (replan) | 391338 triangles | 1150 triangles | 3.8e-3 mm, kept |

The test time is 35 s. It was 68 s.

## Tests (pins, mutation results)

Pins:

- `a_four_turn_thread_flank_meshes_at_full_fidelity_in_a_bounded_count` (app, `import_step_thread`). Red on unchanged code: `facet count over the bound: 391338 facets for a four-turn strip`. Green with the fix. All its other asserts stay as they were.
- `a_wide_twisted_face_keeps_the_planner_division` (kernel, `machining_mesh_redivide`).
- `mesh_redivide::tests::a_face_is_divided_over_its_boundary_nodes_with_the_same_boundary_and_sense` (kernel lib).
- `mesh_redivide::tests::a_face_that_is_not_a_plain_region_of_its_shared_nodes_is_not_divided` (kernel lib).
- `mesh_redivide_fill::tests::a_long_strip_is_filled_with_short_sides_across_it` (kernel lib).
- `mesh_redivide_fill::tests::collinear_runs_and_a_notch_keep_every_boundary_side` (kernel lib).
- `mesh_redivide_fill::tests::a_polygon_that_cannot_be_filled_is_refused` (kernel lib).

Mutations:

| Mutation | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `machining_mesh.rs` from `upstream/main` (no call) | the thread flank pin | red (391338 facets), then green after the restore |
| the tolerance gate in `redivide` removed | `a_wide_twisted_face_keeps_the_planner_division` | red (`FaceCapped`), then green |
| the Lawson flips removed | `a_long_strip_is_filled_with_short_sides_across_it` | red (a side 99.75 long), then green |
| the check of the last ear removed | `a_polygon_that_cannot_be_filled_is_refused` | red, then green |

Gate on the final head `48071efd4`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 10 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- These app suites also ran in debug and are green: `contour_whole_step`, `fixture_step_library`, `import_step_closed_shell`, `import_step_corner_blend`, `import_step_curve_guard`, `import_step_doubly_curved`, `import_step_guard`, `import_step_guard_default_cap`, `import_step_open_shell`, `import_step_outward`, `import_step_twisted_flank`, `model_fidelity`, `step_budget`, `step_chord_units`, `step_fidelity`.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes did not run. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches 246 release steps. A reviewer must run them before this PR is ready.
- The 14-turn faces of the user's parts (#1602) did not run. Their boundary has about 4000 nodes, under the bound of 8192 vertices of the fill.
- No face with a hole was divided: the code refuses such a face before the fill.
- The time of the planner itself does not change. The planner still makes its isotropic division, and the replan at half the chord remains. The speed item of #2780 stays open.
- solidcore-tess stays at the pinned rev. No dependency changed.

## Overlaps

- #2918 touches `crates/kernel/src/lib.rs` (the same file, different lines). Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2795 touches `crates/app/tests/import_step_thread.rs` (the same file, a different function: `flank_step`). Whichever merges second refreshes.

Effort: max

Changelog: A STEP thread flank (a long, thin helical strip) meshes in about 1000 facets, not 391 000; the kernel divides such a face over its edge nodes and keeps the division only when it measures inside the tolerance (#2844).

title: fix(mcp): accept an explicit zero taper on a wire contour
body:
Accept an explicit zero taper when a script or MCP client adds or edits a Wire Contour. The patch validator reads the typed operation value when the saved form omits its default. Other operation kinds and unknown fields retain their existing checks.

The regression test wire_contour_accepts_an_explicit_zero_taper_on_add_and_edit creates a vertical operation, sets a taper and clears it. It also checks a misspelled field and a field on the wrong operation kind.

The quick gate passed all 16 steps and 373 tests. Strict clippy passed on all camcraft-app targets. The normal CLI produced the same 331-byte vertical program for an omitted taper, zero, 0.0 and an edit from 3 degrees to zero. The 3 degree control produced 496 bytes. A misspelled field, a wire taper on a Face operation, and a string value each failed without an NC file. The release suite pocket3d_hsm failed on macOS (Apple silicon). The measured triple was 3158 moves, 3130 planar moves and 1141 arcs. Base commit 3ffe2338f reproduced these three counts and failed the same assertion. See #2371. The remaining heavy suites are running. Verification used the offline software only.

Effort: high
Changelog: A Wire Contour accepts an explicit zero taper on creation and when an edit returns it to a vertical cut.

Fixes #2925

title: feat(ui): Display menu quality preset, ground shadow, ambient occlusion and Look at a work plane
body:
Stacked on #2835 (merge #2835 first).

## What changed

- The Graphics group of the Display menu has four new rows:
  - "Performance" and "Quality": the quality presets (one choice).
  - "Ground shadow": a soft shadow of the model on the floor.
  - "Ambient occlusion": darker shading in the corners of the model.
- The Look at group has a new entry: "Look at a work plane".
- Each entry has a tooltip. Each entry is view state. No entry queues a command.
- A preset sets the two switches. "Performance" sets the two off. "Quality" sets the two on.
- The menu shows the active preset. The active preset is derived from the switches. If the user changes one switch, no preset is active.
- The two switches are saved in the per-user `view.json`. An old file without the keys loads them off. The default is off, so the view of #2818 does not change.
- Ground shadow: the model bodies are projected straight down on the floor (`floor::floor_z`). The footprint is sampled on a grid, blurred, and drawn as blended triangles (`ground_shadow`). The draw list has the new step `Pipe::GroundShadow`, after the model and before the stock.
- Ambient occlusion: each model vertex gets one baked value (`occlusion`). The value is the share of short rays over the face that meet the body again. The draw list has the new step `Pipe::FacesOccluded`. It is the face shader with the baked value on its light. The values are a second vertex buffer. The model vertex buffer does not change.
- The shadow data and the occlusion data are cached (`shade_cache`):
  - The shadow key is the facets and the shown pose of each body, and the floor height.
  - The occlusion key is the facets of one body. A moved body keeps its values.
  - A switch that is off builds nothing. A still frame builds nothing.
- Wireframe draws no lit face and no shadow. The two switches are disabled in Wireframe. They keep their values, and their tooltip says why.
- No entry is hidden on wasm. The two passes are vertex buffers and alpha blending in the one wgpu pass that the two shells share. They use no texture.
- "Look at a work plane" arms one click on an origin axis in the view. The view turns to face the plane of that axis: Z gives XY, X gives YZ, Y gives ZX. A click on the origin point gives the XY plane. The origins are the work offsets (WCS) and the world origin. The view does not pan or zoom. A miss changes nothing and says so.
- `world_verts` moved from `egui_app/world.rs` to the new `egui_app/world_verts.rs`. The code is the same. `world.rs` was at 392 lines and the new scene data put it past 400.

## Cause

This is new work that the maintainer asked for in #2818. #2834 is the part that #2835 does not include.

## Screenshots

`examples/guide-workholding.camproj`. The stock and the toolpaths are hidden, so that the model shows.

| Before ("Performance") | After ("Quality") |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2834/before-performance.png) | ![after quality](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2834/after-quality.png) |

| "Ground shadow" only | "Ambient occlusion" only |
|---|---|
| ![shadow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2834/after-ground-shadow.png) | ![occlusion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2834/after-ambient-occlusion.png) |

| The Display menu | After "Look at a work plane", a click on the X axis of G54 |
|---|---|
| ![menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2834/after-display-menu.png) | ![look at](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2834/after-look-at-yz-plane.png) |

The screenshots come from the off-screen harness of the guide images, on a software GPU. They are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch. No image is in this branch.

## Tests

Pins (all new, all green on the head):

- `ui::draw_list::tests` (3 new tests): the draw list with the shadow pass and with the occlusion pass, on and off.
  - `the_ground_shadow_pass_draws_after_the_model_and_before_the_stock`
  - `the_occlusion_pass_takes_the_model_face_slot`
  - `the_longest_draw_list_holds_each_pass`
- `egui_app::tests::display_quality` (8 tests): the menu.
  - `each_quality_switch_sets_its_field_and_shows_the_check`
  - `a_preset_sets_its_switches_and_one_changed_switch_leaves_no_preset`
  - `wireframe_disables_the_two_switches_and_keeps_their_values`
  - `the_quality_switches_are_kept_in_the_view_file`
  - `look_at_turns_the_view_to_face_a_picked_work_plane`
  - `a_click_on_the_origin_point_gives_the_xy_work_plane`
  - `look_at_a_plane_away_from_each_axis_changes_nothing_and_says_so`
  - `arming_one_look_at_pick_disarms_the_other`
- `shade_cache::tests` (4 tests): the counter tests and the changed-input tests.
  - `a_still_frame_builds_no_shadow_data_and_a_moved_body_builds_again`
  - `a_still_frame_builds_no_occlusion_data_and_new_facets_build_again`
  - `switches_that_are_off_build_no_shade_data`
  - `the_scene_digest_follows_the_shade_data`
- `occlusion::tests` (3 tests), `ground_shadow::tests` (3 tests): the data, with degenerate input.
- `look_at_plane::tests` (2 tests), `display_quality::tests` (1 test).
- `gpu_render::the_ground_shadow_darkens_the_ground_and_not_the_model` and `gpu_render::the_occlusion_pass_darkens_model_faces_only`: a real GPU pass. They compile the new shader stages.
- `view_file::the_shading_switches_round_trip_and_an_old_file_loads_them_off` (`camcraft-app`).

Red before the change: yes. The pins name new items, so they did not compile on the unchanged head of #2835 (`ui lib: FAIL, compile error`). The mutation checks below show that each guard is pinned.

Mutation results. For each row the guard was broken, the pin went red, the guard was restored, and the pin went green. 27 of 27 went red.

| Broken guard | Red test |

| `shade_cache`: the shadow key ignores the pose | `a_still_frame_builds_no_shadow_data...` |
| `shade_cache`: the shadow is built on each frame | `a_still_frame_builds_no_shadow_data...` |
| `shade_cache`: the occlusion is built on each frame | `a_still_frame_builds_no_occlusion_data...` |
| `shade_cache`: a switch that is off still builds | `switches_that_are_off_build_no_shade_data` |
| scene digest: the shade data is not read | `the_scene_digest_follows_the_shade_data` |
| `shell.rs`: the armed plane click is not sent | the two `look_at_*plane*` tests |
| `look_at_plane`: the origin point does not give Z | `a_click_on_the_origin_point_gives...` |
| `look_at_plane`: a reversed WCS axis is not applied | `the_plane_normal_follows_the_rotation...` |
| `look_at_plane::arm` keeps the face pick armed | `arming_one_look_at_pick_disarms_the_other` |
| `occlusion`: no ray meets the body | `the_floor_is_darker_at_the_wall...` |
| `occlusion`: the ray origin is not lifted off its face | `a_convex_body_is_open_at_each_vertex` |
| `ground_shadow`: no blur | `a_box_on_the_floor_shades_its_footprint...` |
| `ground_shadow`: the mesh is not on the floor | `a_body_above_the_floor_casts...` |
| shader: `fs_occluded` does not read its value | `gpu_render::the_occlusion_pass_darkens...` |
| shadow pipeline: no depth test | `gpu_render::the_ground_shadow_darkens...` |

Changed tests (the change explains each):

- `layout_window_display_menu` lists the five new rows of the menu.
- `draw_list_tests.rs` and `view_file.rs` build `Counts` and `ViewPrefs` with `..Default::default()`. Each structure has two new fields.

Original author validation: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` was green (21 steps, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` was clean. The review-fix results below replace these results for the current head.

One of three gate runs failed: the `ui lib` process ended with `SIGSEGV` two seconds after the software GPU driver printed its device warnings. No test failed. The two other runs and one more run of the suite were green (1314 passed) on the same code. The new lib tests make no GPU device.

## Review fixes

Head: `615584eedad2e550aa6fa8b4092085322fbdf1f0`.

The picked face normal now uses `setup_align::view_pose`, as drawing and picking do. This includes the active setup alignment.

`egui_app::tests::display_menu::look_at_uses_the_face_normal_in_the_active_setup_frame` pins a setup rotated 90 degrees about X. It asserts the shown -Y normal and the camera direction after the click.

Mutation check: the test failed with normal `[0, 0, 1]` when `model::transform_of` replaced `setup_align::view_pose`. The restored code passed with the expected -Y normal.

Final-head validation:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: RED. Of 21 steps, 19 passed and 2 failed (`ui lib` and `ui shell`).
- The UI library had 1308 passed, 7 failed, and 7 ignored tests. Six report tests failed with `No adapter found`. `headless_run_succeeds` reported `metal found no adapters`.
- The shell suite had 20 passed and 1 failed test. `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero` returned 1 instead of 0 with the same renderer.
- `gpu_render` reported 14 passed and 1 ignored test. Device tests returned early because no adapter was available. GPU rendering remains unverified here.
- The new rotated-setup pin passed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN. All 184 selected steps passed in 21.0 minutes. The changed `app::view` reached all app heavy targets. The gate also confirmed the expected failure for known-fail #1950.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN in 1 minute 1 second.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` file, no `.cl` file and no snapshot PNG changed against #2835.

## Not exercised

- The wasm build did not run. The two passes use only code that the two shells share.
- No frame time measurement on a large model. With the two switches off ("Performance"), a frame builds nothing and draws the list of #2835.
- With a switch on, a still frame builds no data. It does these reads more: the scene digest reads the shade values, and the shadow reads `floor::floor_z` one more time. `floor_z` walks the facets on each call today (the grid calls it too).
- The first frame after "Ambient occlusion" goes on bakes each body on the UI thread. The time was not measured on a large model.
- The occlusion is a value for each vertex. A large flat triangle shows a linear ramp between its corners, not a narrow dark line in the corner. A fine mesh shows the corner well. `docs/decisions/2834-display-quality-shadow-ao.md` has the alternatives.
- The values are for one body alone. A part does not darken the vise that holds it.
- The shadow is faint on the dark viewport ground (see the screenshots). It was not looked at on a light theme.
- A lathe view (the floor stays at world Z=0).
- Construction planes. The document has no construction plane entity. "Look at a work plane" takes the WCS origins and the world origin.

No new command, so no MCP tool is owed. Decision record: `docs/decisions/2834-display-quality-shadow-ao.md`.

title: feat(ui): "Wireframe, see-through" display mode
body:
Stacked on #2835 (merge #2835 first).

## What changed

- The Display menu has a fifth display mode: "Wireframe, see-through". It stands after "Wireframe".
- The mode draws each edge of the model and of the stock, front and back.
- The mode draws no face. No face goes to the color buffer. No face goes to the depth buffer.
- The model hides nothing behind it: not the stock, not a fixture, not a toolpath.
- A click in the mode picks hidden edges too. The "Pick through" switch stays as the user set it.
- The wireframe switch of the toolbar shows as active in the two wireframe modes. One press in either mode gives "Shaded, with edges".
- The view file stores the mode with the key `wireframe-see-through`.
- The traced stock is a shaded surface. The mode draws the stock wire in its place, as "Wireframe" does.

#2835 gives the other parts of #2636: "Shaded" (faces, no edges), the draw list of each mode, and the saved display mode. This PR adds only the mode that #2835 left out.

The picking rule of the mode:

1. Each edge can be picked, front or back.
2. The edge that draws nearest to the cursor wins.
3. When two edges draw at the same distance from the cursor, the edge nearest to the camera wins.

This is the existing rule of `camcraft_app::pick::pick_bodies` with `through`. The mode asks for `through`.

## Cause

This is new work that the maintainer asked for in #2636. The viewport had no wireframe mode that shows the hidden edges.

## Screenshots

Before (unchanged `main` at 380c29b3c):

| Browser "View" door with the "Solids" radios | Shaded | Wireframe |
|---|---|---|
| ![before view door](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2818/before-browser-view-door.png) | ![before shaded](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2818/before-shaded.png) | ![before wireframe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2818/before-wireframe.png) |

After (this head):

The after images come from the off-screen harness of the guide images. The toolpaths show.

| Shaded, with edges | Shaded |

| Wireframe | Wireframe, see-through (new) |

| ![wireframe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2636/after-wireframe.png) | ![see-through](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2636/after-wireframe-see-through.png) |

The Display menu with the new entry:

![display menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2636/after-display-menu.png)

The before and after images are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch. No image is in this branch.

## Tests

New pins:

- `ui::draw_list::tests::see_through_wireframe_draws_each_edge_and_no_face`
- `egui_app::tests::see_through::the_see_through_entry_exists_sets_its_mode_and_shows_the_check`
- `egui_app::tests::see_through::the_see_through_mode_is_kept_in_the_view_file`
- `egui_app::tests::see_through::in_see_through_a_click_over_a_hidden_edge_picks_that_edge`
- `egui_app::tests::see_through::the_wireframe_switch_leaves_see_through_for_the_default_mode`
- `egui_app::tests::see_through::the_hidden_line_wireframe_still_picks_only_what_is_in_sight` (a control: "Wireframe" keeps its pick. It is green before and after.)
- `feature_pick::see_through_takes_the_edge_nearest_the_cursor_then_nearest_the_eye` (`camcraft-app`). It states the picking rule. The rule is not new, so this test is green before and after.

Red before the change: the five pins of the new behaviour failed on the unchanged base (#2835 head `b5718f464`). They then read the mode by its stored key, so that they compiled. The draw list was `[Faces, Edges, Stock, Edges, Region]`. The menu had no entry. The click took the near face.

Mutation results (the guard was broken, the pin went red, the guard was restored, the pin went green):

| Broken guard | Red test |
|---|---|

title: fix(wire): refuse work outside the stated guide heights
body:
Check the work height against each stated wire guide before the post writes NC. Compare both heights in world coordinates. Use the operation, the part and the stock to determine the full work height.

A 3 degree taper through 12 mm of stock previously posted 496 bytes with its upper guide at Z5. The normal CLI now refuses this case and creates no output file. A 0.001 mm overrun also fails. A fractional setup origin that puts the work exactly at the guide passes.

The valid vertical and tapered control programs match their original NC files byte for byte. A straight cut still accepts a machine with no stated guide heights.

The pinning tests are work_above_the_upper_guide_blocks_the_post and the shifted-stock test in wire_taper. The quick gate passed all six steps, including all 291 app library tests. The release suite pocket3d_hsm failed on macOS (Apple silicon). The measured triple was 3158 moves, 3130 planar moves and 1141 arcs. Base commit 3ffe2338f reproduced these three counts and failed the same assertion. See #2371. The remaining heavy suites are running. The verification also used the normal command script, all 10 related wire suites (62 tests), and strict clippy on all camcraft-app targets.

The offline 40 by 20 mm punch comparison used the same nominal geometry in three tools. The two Agie generators agreed on the nominal contour. CamCraft put its wire center 0.165 mm outside each face. The offline Agie control formally checked and plotted its native vertical bundle. Its technology added its own trim offsets. It did not run the CamCraft generic program or verify a tapered cut.

Effort: high
Changelog: Wire EDM refuses a post when the work extends past a stated guide height.

Fixes #2923
