title: fix(import): preserve STEP short-name length units
body:
## What changed

The model importer expands `GUAC` and `SUNT` in the parsed STEP records.
The unit checks and topology reader then use the same long names.
Short-name inch and metre models keep their correct size in millimetres.

The model read also refuses a length unit that it would read as millimetres
(`crates/kernel/src/step_length_units.rs`):

- A file with a length unit when no unit context states a length unit.
- A unit context that names a unit that is not in the file.
- An item (solid, sheet, or a piece split from a surface model) with no
  unit context, or with a context that states no length unit. This refusal
  applies only when the file states a unit other than the millimetre. In a
  millimetre file, the reader's 1 mm default is the file's own unit.

Since PR #3010 merged, the short names expand in
`crates/kernel/src/step_units_guard.rs` on `main`.

## Cause

The pinned parser expands some short names but leaves these two unchanged.
The unit reader only finds the long names.
It can miss the unit context and silently assume millimetres.

The mappings come from the public [ISO short-name registry](https://standards.iso.org/iso/10303/tech/short_names/short-names.txt).
The fixtures use our unit-box geometry.

## Tests

- `short_name_inch_import_keeps_scale`
- `short_name_metre_import_keeps_scale`
- `short_context_only_import_keeps_scale`
- `short_si_unit_only_import_keeps_scale`
- `long_name_context_controls_import_with_correct_scale`
- `length_unit_without_unit_context_is_refused`
- `unit_context_naming_missing_unit_is_refused`
- `solid_in_unitless_context_is_refused`
- `solid_listed_by_no_representation_is_refused`
- `split_surface_model_pieces_in_unitless_context_are_refused`
- `split_surface_model_pieces_in_inch_context_keep_scale`
- `millimetre_file_keeps_items_with_no_unit_context`

The four regression tests failed before the fix. The long-name controls passed.
All five tests pass with the fix.
The tests check the units, solid count, bounding coordinates, and volume.

Mutation results:

- Restoring the full upstream source makes all four regressions fail. Restoring the fix passes all five tests.
- Removing the `GUAC` mapping fails its isolated test. Restoring it passes.
- Removing the `SUNT` mapping fails its isolated test. Restoring it passes.

The two new fixture rows are in `crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement/rows.rs` after the merge of main.
`step_short_units_inch` and `step_short_units_metre` remain.
The rows keep the recorded legacy reader refusals.
The removed reader stays removed.
`recorded_truck_readings_keep_their_findings` checks both refusal readings.
Removing each row makes its per-file test fail. Restoring each row passes.
Changing each refusal makes the preservation pin fail. Restoring each refusal passes.

Final validation on head `2238ea799f6b4bb222ac1470181e442885283911`:

- The STEP files of this head are the same as in the stack-4b batch gate
  (`bfdff2fa4`). The result of that gate goes in a PR comment.
- Re-run on the stack: kernel `step_short_units` (15 tests),
  `step_agreement`, `step_import`; app `import_step_doubly_curved`,
  `import_step_thread`; clippy for `camcraft-kernel`.
- Heavy lanes: not run on this head. The cut gate covers them.
- The earlier results on head `20214c9f8` do not apply to this head.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` files changed.

## Not exercised

No physical machine, release gate, or manual GUI import was exercised.
This change does not repair the raw tessellator or the legacy STEP reader.

## Overlaps

PR #3010 (merged) moved the short-name expansion into `step_units_guard.rs`.
The angle-unit gap for items with no unit context is tracked by #3079.
PR #2918 changes the tool-body reader in other files.

Effort: high

Changelog: STEP model import preserves inch and metre scale when unit entities use ISO short names.

Fixes #2919

title: feat(2d): Slot and Trochoidal Slot read DXF sketch chains
body: Stacked on #2716 (merge #2716 first) This branch starts at the head of #2716 (`2e77ca0ee`). The diff against `main` shows the changes of #2716 too, until #2716 merges. The changes of this PR are the one commit `feat(2d): Slot and Trochoidal Slot read DXF sketch chains`. ## What changed - A `Slot` and a `Trochoidal Slot` now take one picked chain of a DXF profile (`FeatureSel::SketchChain` or a `SketchLayer` that holds one chain). - One closed line-arc slot outline seeds `a`, `b` and `width`. - One open straight chain is the centerline. It seeds `a` and `b`. The typed `width` stays. - The pick seeds in its own command (`CreateOperation`, `SetOperationGeometry`). One undo takes back the pick and the seed. This is the law of #1504. - Generation judges the stored slot against the picked chain. A slot that left its outline is refused by name. A slot whose ends are not the ends of its centerline is refused by name. - The verification and the stock simulation use the setup stock (`part_solid = false`), as #2716 does for the 2D Contour. - The project file does not change. A `.camproj` file with a two-point slot opens and generates as before. These picks are refused by name: - a closed chain that is not a slot outline (a rectangle, a circle): "is not a slot outline"; - an open chain that is not straight: "the picked centerline is not straight"; - more than one chain: "a slot on a DXF profile cuts one chain, and this selection has 2 chains"; - the whole profile as the source: "needs one picked chain"; - a channel narrower than the tool. The `Slot` refusal now gives the slot width and the tool diameter. title: feat(sim): generate a loose machine model posed by axis values
body:
## What changed

- The PR adds the module `camcraft_sim::machine_model`.
- The input is plain data of the module: `MachineSpec` and `PartSpec` (parts, parent, joint kind, axis, pivot, offset, travel, spindle body, tool station).
- `camcraft-sim` gets no edge to `camcraft-post`. The caller (#2586) maps `MachineTree` into the input.
- `generate` makes one closed body for each part that states a number:
  - a block for a table, a bed or a slide, sized from `travel`;
  - a cylinder for the spindle body, sized from the spindle diameter and length;
  - a cylinder for the tool envelope, sized from the tool station. Its kind is `BodyKind::ToolEnvelope`. It is not steel.
- Fixed, linear and rotary heads keep their stated spindle and tool-envelope bodies. A linear head with travel also keeps its slide block.
- `MachineModel::pose` moves the bodies along the joint chain for a set of axis values. It handles linear joints, rotary joints, a pivot and an offset.
- Each body has `BodySource::Generated`. `BodySource::judged_on()` gives "judged on a generated model".
- A part with no number gets no body and a named note in `MachineModel::notes`. No size is guessed.
- Degenerate input refuses with the part id and the key. No path panics.
- `docs/decisions/2584-machine-model.md` records the decisions.

## Cause

This is new work, not a defect. `camcraft-sim` had no machine model. The maintainer asked for a loose model from the machine file (#2574).

## Tests

Pins, in `crates/sim/tests/machine_model.rs`:

- `vmc_bodies_at_two_axis_positions`
- `a_linear_head_keeps_its_spindle_tool_envelope_and_travel_block`
- `a_rotary_head_keeps_and_turns_its_spindle_and_tool_envelope`
- `tilt_head_bodies_at_two_axis_positions`
- `a_rotary_turns_about_its_pivot_and_a_part_sits_at_its_offset`
- `each_body_is_closed_and_marked_generated`
- `a_part_with_no_number_gets_no_body_and_a_named_note`

Pins, in `crates/sim/tests/machine_model_refusals.rs`:

- `the_plain_input_generates_and_poses`
- `travel_must_be_finite_with_max_over_min`
- `a_joint_axis_must_be_a_finite_direction`
- `positions_must_be_finite`
- `spindle_and_tool_station_sizes_must_be_real_lengths`
- `the_part_list_must_be_a_tree_with_unique_ids`
- `a_pose_states_each_joint_one_time_with_a_finite_value`

Red before the change: yes. On unchanged code the suite did not compile, because the module did not exist.

Mutation results: 32 mutations, one at a time. Each one made a pin red. The restored tree is green.

| Guard removed or changed | Red pin |
|---|---|
| length finite, length more than zero, length maximum | `spindle_and_tool_station_sizes_must_be_real_lengths` |
| position finite, position maximum | `positions_must_be_finite` |
| axis finite, axis not zero | `a_joint_axis_must_be_a_finite_direction` |
| travel on a fixed part, travel finite, travel zero or reversed, travel maximum | `travel_must_be_finite_with_max_over_min` |
| no part, too many parts, blank id, repeated id, parent order | `the_part_list_must_be_a_tree_with_unique_ids` |
| pose value finite, pose value maximum, two values, unknown part, fixed part, missing value | `a_pose_states_each_joint_one_time_with_a_finite_value` |
| chain order of the frames | `tilt_head_bodies_at_two_axis_positions`, `a_rotary_turns_about_its_pivot_and_a_part_sits_at_its_offset` |
| pivot, offset | `a_rotary_turns_about_its_pivot_and_a_part_sits_at_its_offset` |
| circumscribed round face | `each_body_is_closed_and_marked_generated` |
| stack over the spindle, stack under the table | `vmc_bodies_at_two_axis_positions`, `tilt_head_bodies_at_two_axis_positions` |
| table needs X and Y travel, no travel gives no block | `a_part_with_no_number_gets_no_body_and_a_named_note` |
| the words "judged on a generated model" | `each_body_is_closed_and_marked_generated` |

Gate:

Final tested head: `376a0f53161916cad358700c2a61c68c084fb2f3`.

- Both moving-head pins fail with the original generator. Both pass after the final generator is restored.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 4/4 steps. The sim library has 192 passes. Each machine-model suite has 7 passes.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 223/223 steps, 0 failed steps, 63.2 minutes.
  - `motion heavy: *`: 34 steps, 56 tests passed. Two registered failures failed as expected.
  - `app heavy: *`: 188 steps, 42 tests passed. One registered failure failed as expected.
  - The remaining step is the shared release build. All three registered failures refer to #1950. No unexpected test failed.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` file and no `.cl` file changed.

## Not exercised

- `pose` has a last check that each posed vertex is finite. The input checks ahead of it stop each non-finite value. Thus no test reaches it. It stays as a backstop.
- The winding flip of a block face for a left-handed basis. The pinned axes give right-handed bases.
- A slide on a skew axis (not along X, Y or Z). The code handles it, but no pin has one.
- The mapping from `MachineTree` to `MachineSpec`. It is the work of #2586. The tilt-head pin maps `assets/machines/tilthead.mch` by hand.
- No check uses the bodies yet. The collision of machine parts is #2586.
- The batch tier and the release tier did not run.

## Notes for the review

- The type is `feat`, because the issue is an enhancement with new behaviour.
- The PR adds no user-facing command. Thus it adds no MCP tool.
- The PR adds no dependency.
- The sizes are loose by design. The ratios are `SECTION_RATIO` (0.25) and `BED_RATIO` (0.1).
- A joint `axis` is the direction in which the part itself moves. The caller reverses it for a part that moves the table. The decision file gives the reason.

## Overlaps

- #2763 touches `crates/sim/src/lib.rs` for a different module line. It touches the same file, different lines. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Effort: high

Changelog: sim: `camcraft_sim::machine_model` generates a loose machine model (blocks and cylinders) from plain part data and poses it by axis values; each body is marked "generated" (#2584).

Fixes #2584

body:
## What changed

This PR adds the example case `examples/catalog/2d/slots`.

- The part is a 100 x 60 x 12 mm block with two closed slots along X. Each slot is 10 mm wide, 6 mm deep and 60 mm long.
- `Slot1` (Slot) cuts the slot at `Y15` in rows, at the levels `Z9` and `Z6`.
- `Trochoidal slot1` (Trochoidal slot) cuts the slot at `Y-15` in 113 loops, at the full depth.
- The two operations use the same tool (`EM-0600-4FL`), the same width and the same floor.
- The README compares the two programs in a table and says what to look at.
- `model/gen_slots_obj.py` writes the mesh. The geometry is original. The script checks that the mesh is watertight and that its top area is correct.
- `docs/decisions/2861-slots-example.md` records the decisions.

No product code changes. The only Rust change is one new test with its helper in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`.

## Cause

The case did not exist. The maintainer asked for a set of example cases (#2392).

## The two programs

| | Slot | Trochoidal slot |
|---|---|---|
| Motion blocks | 19 | 803 |
| Arc blocks | 0 | 459 |
| Cut levels | `Z9`, `Z6` | `Z6` only |
| Cutting feed | `F600` | `F1200` |
| Time of the feed moves | 0.60 min | 1.28 min |

## Bug found

#2906: a Slot wider than the tool leaves up to 0.86 mm in its round ends, and `verify` is ok. The rows touch a round end only at their end points. The README names the bug. The bug has a link on #2392.

## Tests

Pin: `slots_case_posts_a_slot_and_a_trochoidal_slot_to_the_same_floor` in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`.

- Red before the case: `case 2d/slots must hold .../examples/catalog/2d/slots/slots.nc: No such file or directory`.

- The case rebuilt from that script: the pin is red (`the Slot cuts two levels with a 3 mm stepdown`, left `[6.0]`, right `[9.0, 6.0]`). Restored: green.

## What changed

Git for Windows checks out text files with CRLF (`\r\n`) by default when `core.autocrlf=true`.
Pin test fixtures and golden output paths to LF line endings (`text eol=lf`) in `.gitattributes`:
- Post output golden files and recorded streams (`crates/*/tests/golden/**`, `crates/*/tests/recorded/**`, `crates/*/tests/fixtures/**`)
- Machine configuration files (`crates/*/tests/**/*.mch`, `assets/machines/**/*.mch`)
- STEP, STL, and OBJ model fixtures (`testdata/**/*.step`, `testdata/**/*.stp`, `testdata/**/*.stl`, `testdata/**/*.obj`)
- Skill, agent, and GitHub workflow definitions (`.claude/**`, `.github/**`)

Renormalize line endings for `testdata/models/fig8.step`.

## Readings and Pinning Tests

- `xtask/tests/example_line_endings.rs:all_golden_and_fixture_files_have_eol_lf`: asserts `git check-attr eol` reports `lf` across all fixture, model, and workflow paths.
- `xtask/tests/example_line_endings.rs:golden_and_fixture_files_keep_lf_with_autocrlf`: asserts checked-out fixture files contain no carriage returns under `core.autocrlf=true`.
- Verified affected test suites pass: `explain_fanuc_family`, `wire_taper_angle`, `import_step_curve_guard`, and `post_merge_concurrency`.

## What was not exercised

- Non-Windows systems were not exercised locally (covered by CI).

title: fix(motion): turning rides keep no sample closer than half the chord share
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/turning/offset.rs`: a new private step `thin` runs after the bisection in `profile_offset` and `profile_offset_in`.
- `thin` drops each sample that is closer than half the chord share (`MIN_GAP_SHARE = 0.5`) to the last kept sample.
- The first and the last sample (the window ends) always stay. At the end, a kept sample that is too near the last sample gives way to it.
- Each kept sample is an exact point of the offset curve. No new point is made.
- A chord moves by at most two gaps (one share). The callers pass a quarter of the user tolerance as the share, so the ride stays within half of the user tolerance.
- The module doc now states this bound.

## Cause

The bisection (`settle`) halves the interval toward a vertical tangent of the offset curve. The samples come closer than 1 micrometre. Exact float twins of candidate stations also occur (a gap of 1e-16 mm). `out.dedup()` removes only exactly equal samples. The lathe posts wrote these runs as identical `G01` blocks.

## Tests

New file `crates/motion/tests/turning_offset_spacing.rs`:

- `od_ride_has_no_move_shorter_than_half_the_share`: the stepped bar and the collar, tol 1e-2, 2.5e-3 and 1e-4.
- `id_ride_has_no_move_shorter_than_half_the_share`: the stepped hole wall.
- `a_window_end_next_to_a_candidate_keeps_the_gap`: the window ends 1e-7 past a candidate station. This pins the give-way at the end.
- `thinning_keeps_the_window_ends_and_the_nose`: the ends stay, and each sample is at distance d from the profile.
- `thinned_chords_stay_within_the_bound`: 9 points on each chord stand at least `d - 2 * tol` from the profile.

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged `offset.rs` the OD and ID spacing pins fail with `gap 0.00000000000000044` (OD) and `gap 0.00000000000000011` (ID).

Mutations:

- The old `offset.rs`: 2 pins red. Restored: green.
- The tail give-way disabled (`while ... && false`): `a_window_end_next_to_a_candidate_keeps_the_gap` red (`gap 0.0000001`). Restored: green.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (motion lib, turning_bore, turning_offset_spacing, turning_prof).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Also green by hand: motion `turning_contour`, `turning_contour_stock`. App debug: 25 lathe and turning binaries (`lathe_post*`, `turning*`, `sim_lathe_body`, `coarse_laws`, `project_roundtrip` and others).
- Release `--ignored` on 16 app lathe and turning binaries: green (1 heavy test in that set).

Review fix (head after the merge of main at `97a880c53`):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. 643 steps, 0 failed, 56.8 min.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 19 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: the full reach ran, 233 steps, 86.0 min.
  - motion heavy: 34 lanes, all green. 2 of them are known fails of #1950, red as expected.
  - app heavy: 197 lanes. 196 are green. 6 of them are known fails (#1950, #2845, #2849), red as expected.
  - app heavy `pocket3d_hsm`: red. The test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` gives (3158, 3130, 1141). The Linux pin expects other counts.
  - This failure is on `main` too and is tracked as #3050. I ran an A/B check: with the `offset.rs` of `upstream/main` in this tree, the test gives the same (3158, 3130, 1141). The diff changes only turning code, and no 3D pocket code calls `profile_offset` or `profile_offset_in`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Catalog example

`examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread` came to main after this branch was made. The branch merges main and rebuilds the case with `cargo xtask catalog --case turning/cone-thread`.

- `cone-thread.nc`: 1197 lines to 732 lines. 465 `G01` lines are removed and 0 lines are added. The runs of same-X `G01` blocks go from 509 to 82.
- `cone-thread.camproj`: rebuilt with the new ride samples.
- `README.md`: the limit line for #2882 (repeated blocks) is removed. The taper blocks and the thread blocks that the README names stay the same.
- Mutation: with the old `.nc` back, `catalog_turning_cone_thread::regenerates` and `catalog_turning_cone_thread::rebuilds` are red. With the new `.nc`, they are green.

## Goldens moved

4 files. Each diff only removes lines (516 removed, 0 added):

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/profile_rough_finish.nc` (-129)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/fanuc-lathe/profile_rough_finish.nc` (-129)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/turning_mm.nc` (-129)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/turning_inch.nc` (-129)

Most removed lines are runs of identical blocks, for example 40 x `G01 X7. Z2. F0.04` and 39 x `G01 X9.1 Z3.05 F0.05`. The other removed lines are sub-gap steps at the start of the same face, for example `Z2.001` to `Z2.005`. The goldens were made again with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lane `pocket3d_hsm` is red on `main` (#3050). This PR does not change it (A/B check above).
- At a very small user tolerance (for example 0.001 mm) the gap is less than the posted resolution. Two rounded blocks can then still be equal. This costs no position.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `offset.rs` or the new test file.

## Decision

`docs/decisions/2882-ride-min-spacing.md`. The post-side alternative (drop a repeated block in each lathe post) was dropped.

Written by an Opus lead + Haiku workers (lane trial). The workers wrote about 85% of the lines: `thin` and its call sites, the first four pins, and the decision record. The lead wrote about 15%: the chord-bound correction (1.5x to 2x share, because the give-way at the end can double the gap), the tail pin, the clippy fix, the golden refresh and the review.

Effort: high

Fixes #2882

title: fix(2d): refuse a no-pick chamfer on a partly bevelled edge loop by name
body:
## What changed

A 2D Chamfer with no picks now refuses at generation when a top edge loop carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length.
The message names a point on the bevelled part and a point on the sharp part. It asks the user to pick the edges.

Example text, from the unit test fixture: `the edge loop near X1.000 Y20.000 carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length - it is sharp near X30.500 Y0.000 - a chamfer with no picks would cut the sharp part; pick the edges to break`.

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs`: the new function `partly_bevelled`, and one call in `ride_loops`.
- `crates/app/tests/chamfer_partly_bevelled.rs`: the plate of the issue, with and without the extra vertex.
- `docs/decisions/2887-chamfer-partly-bevelled.md`: the decision record.

The issue permits two results: a ride of the bevelled segments only, or a named refusal that asks for picks. This PR takes the refusal.

## Cause

`ride_loops` classified each top loop whole, by the farthest vertex from the wall loop.
A loop that is bevelled on one side has two readings.
With an extra vertex on the top edge of the bevel, the loop read as bevelled. The ride then cut the three sharp sides.
Without that vertex, the two bevel corners lie on the wall, and the loop read as sharp. The tip then stood inside the part at the bevel.
The verifier refused the two programs as a gouge at a coordinate, with no reason.

## The check

The check runs for each segment of the matched top loop. It measures the two ends and the middle against the wall loop.

- A segment within 1e-6 mm of the wall is sharp.
- A segment more than 0.05 mm from the wall is bevelled.
- A segment between the two values counts as neither.

The loop is refused when it has a bevelled segment and more than one chamfer width of sharp length.
The result does not depend on tessellation.

## Tests

Pins:

- `a_no_pick_chamfer_on_a_plate_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_by_name` (app, `chamfer_partly_bevelled`)
- `the_refusal_does_not_depend_on_an_extra_vertex_on_the_bevel` (app, `chamfer_partly_bevelled`)
- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_by_name` (motion lib)
- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_with_an_extra_vertex_too` (motion lib)
- `machining2d::chamfer_ride::tests::a_loop_bevelled_all_round_is_not_partly_bevelled` (motion lib)

Mutation: with `chamfer_ride.rs` of `upstream/main` 17b1b2b81, the two app pins fail (`a partly bevelled edge loop with no picks is refused: ()`: generation succeeds). With the fix, the two pins pass.
The motion unit pins were not run against the old file: they call the new function, so the old file does not compile with them.

Unchanged and green: the six older `chamfer_ride` unit tests and the seven tests of `chamfer_modelled_edge` (#303, #2435, #2596).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 7991bc04b (4 steps, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Heavy review results

Verified head: `7991bc04bba6db467460b375821a8ea30011786d`. No source changes were needed for the review finding.

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed: 223 steps, 0 failed, 47.6 minutes.

- Release build: passed (1 step).
- Motion heavy lane: passed (34 steps). Tests: 56 passed. Two registered failures for #1950 failed as expected.
- App heavy lane: passed (188 steps). Tests: 42 passed. One registered failure for #1950 failed as expected.
- No unexpected failure occurred. No golden file changed.

The three registered #1950 cases are:

title: feat(drilling): fine boring cycle (G76) with a required shift
body:
Stacked on #2823 (merge #2823 first).

## What changed

Fine boring is a new cycle on the drilling operation. This is the last slice of #1445, and it is the work of #1479.

- `CycleChoice::FineBore { shift_x_um, shift_y_um }` is a new cycle choice. The shift is a required part of the choice. There is no default shift.
- `CycleKind::FineBore` is a new CL cycle kind. The `.cl` text writes `FineBore`. The `.cnc` stream writes `CYCLE FINEBORE`.
- The chain of one hole is: feed in, shift at the bottom, rapid out at the shifted XY, shift back at R.
- The post engine reads the shift from the chain. It gives the shift to the script as `ShiftX` and `ShiftY`.
- The post engine refuses the cycle by name for a script that does not declare `fineBoring = true`.
- The Haas post declares `fineBoring`. It writes `G76 X Y Z R I J P F`, one whole block for each hole. It never writes `Q`.
- Each of the other 17 shipped posts refuses the cycle by name.
- A machine file can state `spindle.orientation`. The value `false` refuses a fine bore with any post.
- The generator refuses a shift that the bar has no room for. The room is `(tool dia. - shank dia.) / 2`.
- The commands refuse a zero shift, a shift above 5 mm on one axis, and a shift that is not smaller than a hole radius.
- The verifier reads the three stopped-spindle rapids with the stopped bar. It still reads the shank and the holder at the shifted position.
- The reach law holds a fine bore to the shank fit in the hole, as it does for a bore and a ream.
- The project file, MCP `edit_operation` and the Cycle combo of the drill page carry the choice and its shift.

A program that does not choose the cycle posts the same bytes as before.

## Cause

Hole making had no fine boring cycle. A bore cycle rapids out with the tip on the wall, and the tip marks the finished bore.

## Design

- The shift is in the chain, not in a new record field. The posted `I` and `J` are the shift of the chain, so the two cannot disagree. The WCS flip, the WCS yaw and the axis mirror already transform the moves and the cycle centre together.
- The refusal for a post is in the engine. A new post is refused until it declares the flag.
- Haas `G76` reads `I` and `J` as the shift along X and Y. The `Q` form takes its direction from Setting 27. A program cannot state that setting, so the post never writes `Q`.
- Fanuc, Mazak and Doosan take the direction of `Q` from a control parameter. These posts refuse. #2886 has the work for these controls, for Heidenhain `CYCL DEF 202`, for Sinumerik `CYCLE86` and for Mach4.
- The verifier models the tool as the cylinder that the turning edge sweeps. That cylinder, shifted by `s`, enters the bore wall by `s`. With the spindle stopped, the bar reaches `bar radius + s` from the hole axis and the tip reaches `tool radius - s`. The two stay inside the cylinder that the feed in cut while `s < tool radius - bar radius`. The feed in was read over the same cylinder.
- The shank and the holder are not inside that cylinder. The solid law reads them at the shifted position.
- `docs/decisions/1445-fine-boring.md` has the options that were dropped.

MCP: `edit_operation` takes `"cycle": {"fine_bore": {"shift_x": 0.3, "shift_y": -0.4}}` (millimetres). The word `"fine_bore"` with no shift is refused.

## Tests

Pins:

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `drilling::tests_fine_bore` (6 tests): the chain, the choice with no default, the room door, the bore door.
- `camcraft-post`, `fine_bore_cycle` (9 tests): the stream word, the Haas `G76` block, the `P0` word, the refusal with no shift, the output-unit refusal, the refusal of each other post, the machine gate, the file word, the golden.
- `camcraft-sim` lib, `verify::fine_bore` (5 tests): the acquittal, the cases that keep each conviction, the holder that is still read, the holder collisions that the full verifier preserves.
- `camcraft-app`, `fine_bore_cycle` (9 tests): the command with undo and redo, the project file, the `.cl` text, the stamp, the command doors, the generator door, the shank fit, the Haas post, the machine gate, the post refusal, MCP.
- `camcraft-ui` lib, `egui_app::tests::cycle_combo` (3 tests) and `egui_app::tests::holes_fine_bore` (2 tests).

Red before the change: the pins do not compile on the base. `CycleChoice::fine_bore`, `CycleKind::FineBore` and `fine_bore_gate` do not exist there. This is a new cycle, so there is no old behaviour to show red at run time. The first run of the app pin on the new generator, before the verifier change, was red:

```text
the verifier accepts the shifted retract: [RapidInStock { at: 2 }, RapidInStock { at: 3 }]
post blocked - 2 warning(s): FineBore1: rapid move 2 travels through stock ...; FineBore1: rapid move 3 travels through stock ...
```

title: fix(post): refuse Fanuc G76 when the start point is above material
body:
## What changed

- Added `start_in_air: bool` to `cl::ThreadCycle` and `ThreadCycleDto` (defaults to `false`).
- Added optional `AIR 1` flag to `THREAD` records in `crates/post/src/post/cnc_thread.rs` and exposed it to post scripts as `properties.StartInAir`.
- Refused G76 by name in `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` (`g76Why`) whenever `p.StartInAir !== true`.
- Added `cycle_infeed_band` and `part_band_clear` in `crates/motion/src/turning/thread_cycle.rs` to check the full rapid-infeed axial band `[min(start_s, s_deep) - insert_width/2, max(start_s, s_deep) + insert_width/2]` against the part silhouette and raw stock.
- Added `crates/app/src/operation/g76_start.rs` to refine `start_in_air` against the revolved part, stock and prior cuts. `TurnedAhead` now carries the grooving blade half-width `band`.
- Replaced isolated stock samples with continuous coverage checks after review. Each interval between stock profile breakpoints has a conservative bound above the root. Prior cuts must cover the full bound. Bounded subdivision checks coverage from several cuts. The check refuses G76 when it cannot prove clearance.
- Reduced blade and nose credit by the clearance margin. Blade credit follows the actual swept segment. The check also proves coverage between radial samples. It does not credit uncertain stock holes.
- Updated `crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs` and `crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs` so a threading pass can start in free air in front of a free end face without false out-of-domain rest warnings.
- Updated the Fanuc G76 test bar fixtures and three golden `.nc` files to start in free air (`Z16.` / `Z16.625` / `Z0.6299`) instead of inside a solid `Z=40` bar.
- Moved the clearance algorithm to `crates/motion/src/turning/g76_clearance.rs`. The public API takes cut and pilot values.
- Kept stock breakpoints and document integration in `app`. Moved the radial-gap and diagonal-blade tests to the motion crate.
- Recorded the design choice in `docs/decisions/2878-fanuc-g76-start-in-air.md`.

## Cause

A Fanuc-type G76 cycle moves the insert from the start point to each pass depth at rapid traverse. Previously, `fanuc-lathe.cps` emitted G76 without checking whether the start point stood in free air, and `turning::thread` clamped pass starts to the part silhouette domain. As a result, G76 started inside solid material (for example at `Z77.4` inside a `Z=78` end face on the cone-thread part).

## Tests

### Pinning tests (red before fix, green after fix)

- `lathe_post_g76_start::g76_refuses_when_start_point_is_inside_a_solid_bar` (G76 refused by name, G32 still posts)
- `lathe_post_g76_start::g76_refuses_on_cone_thread_start_inside_end_face` (reproduces #2878 cone-thread part)
- `lathe_post_g76_start::g76_posts_when_start_point_is_in_free_air_in_front_of_end_face`
- `lathe_post_g76_start::g76_refuses_uncut_stock_in_front_of_end_face_and_posts_after_facing`
- `lathe_post_g76_start::g76_refuses_legacy_stream_without_air_flag`
- `camcraft-app::operation::g76_start::tests::relief_groove_wider_than_insert_passes_when_grooved_and_refuses_when_uncut_or_narrow`
- `camcraft-app::operation::g76_start::tests::flank_infeed_refuses_when_deep_pass_overlaps_end_face`
- `turning_thread_cycle::start_in_air_distinguishes_solid_bar_from_free_end_start`
- `operation::g76_start::tests::narrow_stock_rib_between_old_stations_refuses` pins the reviewer's narrow rib between axial samples.
- `turning_g76_clearance::radial_gap_between_prior_cut_capsules_refuses` pins a radial gap and permits cuts with a safe overlap.
- `turning_g76_clearance::diagonal_blade_does_not_credit_its_deep_tip_across_the_whole_band` pins the actual blade sweep.

- `turning_g76_clearance::pilot_values_prove_only_the_removed_cone` pins the motion API for pilot dimensions and cone coverage.

### Earlier mutation checks

- Removed `p.StartInAir !== true` guard in `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`: 4 of 5 tests in `lathe_post_g76_start` failed (red), then passed after restore (green).
- Disabled `g76_start::judge` in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: `g76_refuses_uncut_stock_in_front_of_end_face_and_posts_after_facing` failed (red), then passed after restore (green).
- Restored post-retain `lat.push(w0); lat.push(w1);` in `crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs`: `g76_posts_when_start_point_is_in_free_air_in_front_of_end_face` failed with `6.0000 mm rest` (red), then passed after restore (green).
- Forced `start_in_air = true` in `crates/motion/src/turning/thread_cycle.rs`: `start_in_air_distinguishes_solid_bar_from_free_end_start` failed (red), then passed after restore (green).

- Review fix mutation: restored the sampled production checks while keeping the new tests. All three new regression tests failed (RED). Restored the continuous checks: all five `operation::g76_start::tests` passed (GREEN).

### Earlier gate and clippy results

These results apply to the previous head, before the domain move.

- Previous head: `41ce5778c17a886edf7288bf4db544ce4e5b1d04`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` fell back to batch because `crates/cl` changed. The full run completed 955 steps in 36.6 minutes. Only clippy failed. A minimal guard change fixed that lint. On that head, all five clearance pins passed. The failed-only clippy rerun passed: 1 step, 0 failed, 37 seconds.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on that head: 2 minutes 58 seconds, 0 warnings.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` ran the reached motion and app lanes on that head. Result: 220 steps, 0 failed, 53.8 minutes. Motion passed 56 ordinary tests. App passed 42 ordinary tests.
- Three known #1950 failures remain. The gate classified these failures as expected and accepted them. They are failures, not passes:
  - `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_reaches_the_air_planner_with_the_stock`
  - `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note`
  - `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level`

### Latest review fix and checks

Head: `3c3f8b1d8b72b225459a63d71948f15c2c100267`.

- Moved `AheadCut`, coverage checks, and focused tests to `camcraft-motion`. App collects the cut and pilot values.
- Placement mutation: restored the original app-only module and kept the motion API test. The test build failed with `E0432` (RED).
- Restored the domain move. All three `turning_g76_clearance` tests passed (GREEN).
- All three retained `operation::g76_start::tests` passed. These include the narrow-stock-rib regression.
- `rustfmt --check` passed for the changed concrete files.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN: 956 steps, 0 failed, 22.5 minutes. The gate used the batch fallback because `crates/cl` changed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN: all four touched crates passed with 0 warnings in 36.82 seconds.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN: 220 steps, 0 unexpected failures, 36.9 minutes. Motion passed 56 ordinary tests. App passed 42 ordinary tests. The gate accepted the three known #1950 expected failures listed above. These are failures, not passes. Reached lanes: motion and app.

## Goldens moved

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc`: `G00 X12.1 Z14.` -> `G00 X12.1 Z16.` (start point moved into free air past the free end face).
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/thread_g76_area.nc`: `G00 X12.1 Z14.625` -> `G00 X12.1 Z16.625` (flank-infeed start point moved into free air past the free end face).
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc`: `G00 X0.4764 Z0.5512` -> `G00 X0.4764 Z0.6299` (inch start point moved into free air past the free end face).

## Not exercised

- Execution on a physical Fanuc lathe control or third-party Fanuc simulator.
- `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps` G76 refusal (out of scope for #2878; can reuse `properties.StartInAir` in a follow-up).

## Overlaps

- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: touches the same file, different function/arm as open PRs #2853, #2836, #2833, #2831, #2822, #2716, #2714, #2678; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `crates/app/src/operation/mod.rs`: touches the same file, different module declaration as open PRs #2853, #2836, #2833, #2716, #2714, #2678; whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Refuse Fanuc lathe G76 cycles whose start point stands above material and allow free-air starts in front of the end face or in a relief groove wider than the insert.

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Adaptive from the previous operations
body:
Stacked on #2822 (merge #2822 first).

This PR is a `feat`: it adds a parameter group. The default (off) does not change an output.

## What changed

The 2D Adaptive operation has the rest machining group.
With the group on, the operation cuts only what the earlier operations of the same setup left.

- `OpParams::Adaptive2D` has the field `rest: Option<RestParams>`. `None` is off and is the default.
- `machining2d::rest_adaptive_previous` (new, motion crate) reads the stock of the previous operations with `rest_stock_from_columns` (#2033). It gives that stock to the rest Adaptive planner `rest_adaptive` (#2031).
- Each plunge stands where that stock proves the whole cutter clear. The planner holds the optimal load on the material that stands.
- `adaptive::rest_levels` (new) gives the cut depths of the rest planner. The stock is read at exactly those depths.
- The group rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest` of the 2D Adaptive and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter. A file without the key reads as off.
- The stamp writes byte `0xD9` and the allowance when the group is on. An operation without the group keeps its stamp.

Refused by name, at the edit and again at generation:

- An entered previous tool (`REST_ADAPTIVE_ENTERED`). An entered diameter does not prove where material is absent (#2031). The 2D Pocket keeps that mode.
- The Trochoidal method, arc turns, a tilt. The rest planner does not read them, so they are not dropped silently.
- A negative or non-finite allowance.

Refused by name at generation:

- An earlier operation with no toolpath, a stale toolpath, or a suppressed cut (the refusals of #2033).
- No stock ahead (`REST_ADAPTIVE_NO_STOCK`). The 2D Pocket cuts the whole pocket in this case. The 2D Adaptive does not, because the rest planner cannot enter a full pocket.
- A roughing pass that stops above the floor: "rest Adaptive has no entry with proved clearance".

## Cause

The rest Adaptive planner (#2031) had no door from an operation.
The retired Adaptive strategy of the 2D Pocket was its only possible caller (#2253).
The 2D Adaptive operation had no rest parameter and no producer of the proved stock.

## Two findings

- The column reading of #2033 leaves a band along each wall that an earlier tool cut to. On a 0.1 mm grid the band is 0.14 mm thick. With the film of #2033 (one cell diagonal) the planner read the band as rest material and refused the fixture ("would reach 23 passes by a retract"). The film is now `cell * (1 + sqrt 2)`. The band still stands for each plunge and each load reading. No pass is planned for it. The path note states the film.
- An allowance of 0.6 mm grew that band to 0.74 mm, and the planner found no entry. The allowance now grows only material that is thicker than the film. It never makes the standing material smaller.

## Tests

Red before the change: the pins use the new field and the new function, so they do not compile on unchanged code. The mutation results are the proof for each guard.

Pins, all new:

- `crates/app/tests/rest_adaptive_op.rs` (6 tests):
  - `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left`: the real job (60 x 40 pocket, 3 mm corners, 12 mm roughing tool, 4 mm rest tool) against an independent simulation of the roughing pass. Each standing column is cut. No plunge goes down a column that the roughing pass left under the cutter. No rapid is below the top of the stock, but a straight lift. Each feed stays at a corner.
  - `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_is_refused_by_name`
  - `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit`
  - `a_document_past_the_door_is_refused_at_generation`
  - `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_a_project_file_key_and_moves_the_stamp`
  - `mcp_sets_the_group_refuses_the_entered_tool_undoes_and_the_project_keeps_it`
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`, `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_adaptive_tests.rs` (lib): `each_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `the_allowance_never_makes_the_standing_material_smaller`, `bad_rest_values_are_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`: `the_column_stock_of_the_previous_operations_plans_the_rest_adaptive_pass` (the laws of #2031 on the column stock: verifier, plunges, rapids, load, coverage), `the_previous_operations_planner_refuses_what_it_cannot_prove`.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored and green):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant |
|---|---|---|
| generate: the rest planner is called | `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_...` | red |
| generate: the refusals stand at generation | `a_document_past_the_door_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: entered tool refused | `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: Trochoidal refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: arc turns refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: tilt refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: bad values refused without a tool | `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool` | red |
| `rest_op`: the 2D Adaptive reads the previous operations (job stock, earlier-operation refusals) | `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_...` | red |
| `params`: stamp byte `0xD9` | `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` | red |
| `params`: the allowance in the stamp | same | red |
| project: the key is written | `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_...` | red |
| project: the key is read | `mcp_sets_the_group_...` | red |

title: fix(turning): allow threading passes to start in front of the end face
body:
## What changed

- Removed the post-filter push of `w0` and `w1` in `revolve::lattice` (`crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs`). Every in-domain band endpoint is already in `lat`. Removing those four lines keeps `lat` strictly inside `[d_lo, d_hi]`. Free air past an end face no longer creates intervals where the scan reads `E(s) = 0` as rest.
- Computed `k_hi` in `thread_planned_in` (`crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs`) from the unclamped `f.station_of(p.top_z)`. Kept `s_lo..=s_hi` clamped to `[d_lo, d_hi]` for `ref_top`, valley phase discovery, and the empty-window refusal. A threading pass can now start in free air in front of the end face.
- Added `crates/motion/tests/turning_thread_end_face.rs` with four pinning tests.
- Added `docs/decisions/2879-thread-free-air-start.md`.

## Cause

Two defects prevented a free-end thread from starting in front of the end face:

1. `revolve::lattice` filtered `lat` to `[d_lo, d_hi]` and then pushed `w0` and `w1` back into `lat`. Whenever a move band extended past `d_hi` (by 0.1 mm on a free-end groove, or by whole pitches on a free-air lead-in), `revolve::scan` evaluated an air interval where `E(s) = 0` and reported the capped wave floor (5.0 mm) as rest.
2. `blade::setup` clamped `s_hi` to `d_hi`, and `thread_planned_in` used that clamped `s_hi` in `k_hi`. Setting `top_z` in front of the end face (such as Z81 for a Z78 end face) still started each pass inside the bar at Z77.5.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/turning_thread_end_face.rs`:

- `free_end_groove_band_past_end_face_is_not_rest`: red before fix (`rest_mm: 5.000000000000001`), green after fix.
- `free_air_lead_in_starts_in_front_of_end_face_and_judges_clean`: red before fix (started at `77.5` instead of `80.5`), green after fix.
- `free_air_start_still_convicts_real_gouge_and_real_rest_on_part`: checks overcut, shallow cut, missed turn, and a free-air lattice point whose flank clips a solid end face.
- `groove_at_free_end_face_spilling_into_end_air_is_not_rest`: red before fix (`rest_mm: 4.0`), green after fix.

Mutation checks on `turning_thread_end_face`:

- Reverted `crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs` to `upstream/main`: red (3 of 4 failed with `rest_mm: 5.0` and `rest_mm: 4.0`). Restored: green.
- Reverted `crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs` to `upstream/main`: red (`free_air_lead_in_starts_in_front_of_end_face_and_judges_clean` failed: `got 77.5`). Restored: green.

Gates:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (10 steps, 0 failed: `motion build`, `lib`, `turning_blade`, `turning_coarse`, `turning_stock`, `turning_thread`, `turning_thread_cycle`, `turning_thread_dips`, `turning_thread_end_face`, `turning_thread_infeed`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Final-head verification for the review finding (2026-11-20):

- Head: `5de53b78267abc3f10eaac8b749f9e7ff81975f9` (unchanged). The review requested missing test evidence. No source or test changed.
- Base: `upstream/main` at `3ffe2338f775b2f254524f5f8e642aae5181aebb`.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=8 cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: passed, 220 steps, 0 failed, 144.2 minutes.
- Motion heavy lane: passed, 34 steps. All 56 ordinary heavy tests passed. Both declared known-failure checks for #1950 matched their expected failures.
- App heavy lane: passed, 185 steps. All 42 heavy tests passed.
- The combined release build accounts for the remaining step. Selected targets with no ignored tests completed without failures.

- These results use the unchanged PR head. The review used a trial merge with main, so its library test count differs.
- No new mutation check applies to this evidence-only update. The existing mutation results above were independently repeated in the latest review.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- No app-level end-to-end Fanuc G76 post run (tracked in #2878).
- No UI test or physical machine run.

title: feat(catalog): add the turning case cone-thread - a cone with a threaded end
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the example catalog case `examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread`.
The case is a spun turning profile: a cone with a threaded end.

- The stock is a 30 mm bar, 79 mm long.
- The part has a collar, a 20 mm to 10 mm cone over 40 mm, an 8 mm neck and an M10x1.5 thread, 15 mm long.
- The machine is the built-in `Lathe` (`assets/machines/lathe.mch`). The post is `Fanuc Lathe`.
- The program has six operations: `Face`, `Rough profile`, `Finish profile`, `Neck`, `Thread`, `Part off`.

The case folder has the layout of #2393:

- `model/gen_cone_thread_obj.py` and its two meshes
- `build.camscript`
- `cone-thread.camproj`
- `cone-thread.nc`
- `README.md`, which walks through the steps

The PR also adds one test to `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs` and the decision file `docs/decisions/2394-cone-thread.md`.
No file in `crates/*/src` changes.

## Cause

Issue #2394 asks for this case. The catalog infrastructure of #2393 is on `main` since v0.24.0.

## Decisions that differ from the issue text

The decision file gives each one with its reason.

- The case imports two models: the turned blank and the finished part. Profile Finish cannot finish the model that the Threading operation needs (#2880).
- The neck needs a sixth operation, a Groove Finish. The issue lists five.
- The thread posts as G32 passes, not as the G76 cycle. A G76 cycle would start inside the part (#2878, #2879).
- The threading insert is a tool definition in the script. No catalog insert fits a 1.5 mm pitch (#893).
- The shoulder has no fillet (#2881).

## Bugs filed on the way

The issue says: "Any refusal or wrong output found on the way is filed as its own bug and linked here."

- #2878 (`P1`): a G76 cycle starts inside the part.
- #2879 (`P3`): a threading pass cannot start in front of the end face.
- #2880 (`P3`): Profile Finish reads thread valleys and a neck step as rest.
- #2881 (`P3`): a steep fillet chord sends the profile ride far out of the bar.
- #2882 (`P3`): the profile rides post runs of identical `G01` blocks. The committed program has 408 such blocks.

## Tests

Pin: `example_catalog::turning_cone_thread_case_posts_the_taper_and_the_thread`. It reads the committed program and asserts:

- the operation order,
- the slope of each finish block on the cone (10 mm of diameter over 40 mm),
- the G32 passes at lead 1.5, the last pass at the 8.16 mm root, the pass end at Z63.9,
- the neck plunge to X8 and the part-off to X0.

The two suite tests that iterate all cases also cover the new case: `every_catalog_case_opens_regenerates_verifies_and_posts_byte_for_byte` and `every_catalog_case_rebuilds_from_camscript`.

Red first: without the case folder the pin fails with `catalog case turning/cone-thread is missing`.

Mutations of the committed `.nc`, each restored after the run:

| Mutation | Pin |
|---|---|
| case folder removed | red |
| `G01 X10.212 Z58.4` changed to `X12.212` (taper) | red: `is off the taper: -0.141` |
| `G32 Z63.9 F1.5` changed to `Z65.4` (thread end) | red: `each pass ends at the neck, Z63.9` |
| files restored | green |

The first form of the taper assert let the taper mutation pass. The assert now checks each block on the cone.

Gates on the final head:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (`app:example_catalog`, whole suite, 16 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask catalog --check`: `checked 2d/first-part`, `checked turning/cone-thread`.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run`: the diff reaches no heavy lane.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` shows one new file, `examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread/cone-thread.nc` (1197 lines). No file under `tests/golden/` changes.

## Not exercised

- No machine or control simulator ran the program.
- The lathe stock simulation does not cut threads. The verify verdict says so, and the thread is judged by its own operation verdict.
- The tool holders are not judged: the tools have no modelled body.
- `cargo xtask catalog --screenshots` and `--pdf` did not run.
- The UI did not open the project.

## Notes for the review

- `cone-thread.camproj` is 1.5 MB. The seed case is 0.2 MB. The project holds two meshes and the toolpaths.
- When #2882 is fixed, the committed `.nc` changes. That PR must rebuild the case.

## Overlaps

#2877 (draft, case `2d/contour-tabs`) touches the same file, `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`, in a different function. The two PRs each add a new test function at the end of the file. Whichever merges second refreshes and keeps the two functions. The case folders do not overlap.

title: fix(multiaxis): rotary operations read a face selection or refuse it
body:
## What changed

- Rotary Parallel keeps its cut over the picked faces. The kernel plans the raster on the full model, as before. Then it keeps each cut point where the line from the axis through the ball centre meets a picked facet. The radial relink builds the links between the kept pieces.
- The axis fit, the gouge laws and the verify still read the full model.
- Rotary Parallel refuses, by name, a selection that it cannot use:
  - a pick that is not a face;
  - picks on two models;
  - a face that does not look away from the axis (an end face, a bore wall);
  - picks that form separate groups;
  - picks that no pass lies over.
- Rotary Contour and Rotary Offset refuse a face selection by name. They do not cut the full model silently. Face containment for these two kinds is not in this PR: #2851 (Rotary Contour) and #2852 (Rotary Offset) hold that work.
- The generation stamp of a rotary operation with a selection gets a version mark. A path that was cached under the old reading becomes stale.
- An operation with no selection (source `Entity` or `Stock`) generates as before.

New files:

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_pick.rs`: the clip, `faces_outward`, `groups`.
- `crates/app/src/operation/rotary_picks.rs`: the picks read from the world, and the refusals.
- `crates/app/tests/rotary_face_selection.rs`: the pins.
- `docs/decisions/2848-rotary-face-selection.md`: the decision record.

## Cause

`material_of` reads a selection as the full facets of the picked models. The rotary arms of `run_job` gave those facets to the kernels. No code read which faces were picked, and no code refused the selection.

## Scope against the issue's "Done means"

| Item | State |
|---|---|
| Rotary Parallel accepts `SrcRef::Selection` | done |
| Rotary Contour, Rotary Offset accept `SrcRef::Selection` | not done: they refuse by name; #2851, #2852 |
| Toolpath stays in the picked faces | done for Rotary Parallel |
| Axis fit uses the full model | done, pinned |
| Stock simulation reads only the generated toolpath | no change necessary: the simulation reads the stored path |
| UI enables face selection for rotary operations | no change necessary: `SetOperationGeometry` has one door for all kinds (`crates/ui/src/state.rs`) |
| Unusable selections refuse with a clear message | done for all three kinds |
| Full-model operation is the same | done: the `None` path is the old code |
| Tests | done |

The maintainer's triage comment names the defect: the operation ignores the selection without a message. This PR removes that for all three kinds. If the maintainer wants the issue open until #2851 and #2852 merge, change `Fixes` to `Refs`.

## Tests

Pins (`crates/app/tests/rotary_face_selection.rs`), all red on `upstream/main` 326c938b1:

- `rotary_parallel_keeps_its_cut_over_the_picked_faces` - red before: "a cut at station -16 is off the picked neck (2..16)".
- `rotary_parallel_keeps_to_a_sector_and_still_turns_about_the_whole_models_axis`.
- `rotary_parallel_reads_a_welded_wall_pick_as_its_strips` - red before: "a cut at station -16.204 is off the picked patch".
- `rotary_parallel_refuses_a_selection_it_cannot_use_by_name` - red before: "the selection must be refused, not cut".
- `rotary_contour_and_offset_refuse_a_face_selection_by_name` - red before: "the selection must be refused, not cut".

Unit tests (`multiaxis::rotary_pick::tests`): the clip, `faces_outward`, `groups`.

Mutations (each was put in, the pins ran, the fix was put back):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| The two rotary arms of `generate.rs` as before the fix | 5 of 5 pins red |
| The kernel clip off (`rotary_parallel_over` ignores the picks) | 3 keep pins red |
| A chain pick read as "no facets" (no "is not a face" refusal) | refusal pin red |
| The `faces_outward` guard off | refusal pin red |
| The `groups` guard off | refusal pin red |

A file-level restore of `generate.rs` from `upstream/main` does not compile with the new job field. The arm-level mutation replaced it.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 294 steps, 0 failed, wall 25.2 min. `upstream/main` moved to 5fdbed9bd during the work, so the gate selected the suites of those new commits too. The branch base is 326c938b1; the new commits do not touch `crates/app/src/operation` or `crates/motion/src/multiaxis`.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

The gate ran with the compile cache off (`CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`, no `RUSTC_WRAPPER`). The sccache server of this machine did not answer.

## Goldens moved

title: fix(geometry): order sheet cuts before material release
body:
Stacked on #2808 (merge #2808 first)

## What changed

Add `camcraft_geometry::nesting::cut_order` for one placed sheet.
Build a global containment forest for closed loops and open chains.
Resolve closed `Auto` sides by depth parity and open `Auto` sides to `OnLine`.
Traverse the forest iteratively. Sort siblings by enclosed area, then stable ID.
Schedule marking, internal, rough profile, and final breakthrough phases.
Use an explicit `release_phase` to distinguish blind pockets from through cuts.
Refuse invalid geometry, side requests, incomplete schedules, and cuts after material release.
Report circular-tool corner limits without changing the picked geometry.

## Cause

The geometry crate lacked one cut order across a nested sheet.
An enclosing hole can free a smaller part before that part's cuts finish.
Independent operation orders cannot enforce that sheet relationship.

## Tests

The initial pinning build failed on unchanged upstream base `f3b0e1955` with `E0432` because the planner API was absent.
The tested stacked base is parent commit `1947b6b6c30d214baf3db2072f95ed51ccb2dae3` from #2808.

All 17 pins pass:

- `sheet_tree_cuts_parts_in_holes_before_release_and_small_siblings_first`
- `sheet_pass_phases_keep_marking_first_and_breakthrough_last`
- `sheet_refuses_a_phase_that_frees_a_hole_before_its_nested_part`
- `sheet_order_validator_refuses_released_ancestors_missing_and_extra_passes`

- `sheet_open_chain_sides_resolve_and_invalid_sides_name_the_chain`
- `sheet_refuses_invalid_width_ids_and_pass_requests`
- `sheet_refuses_degenerate_self_crossing_and_retraced_geometry`
- `sheet_refuses_area_accumulation_overflow_by_name`
- `sheet_refuses_crossing_or_touching_contours_and_boundary_crossing_chains`
- `sheet_crossing_open_features_keep_the_same_containing_parent`
- `sheet_corner_limits_use_tool_radius_and_ignore_input_winding`
- `sheet_open_side_corner_limits_follow_the_directed_cut_side`

Each of 21 runtime guard mutations failed its pins. Each restored version passed again.
The mutations covered:

- Width, duplicate IDs, pass requests, release requests, mandatory breakthrough release, and open/closed side requests.
- Minimum vertices, finite coordinates, coordinate bounds, zero-length segments, open closure, retracing, self-crossing, boundary crossing, and area overflow.
- Unknown cuts, extra or duplicate passes, global phase order, released material, and missing passes.

The area mutation used wrapping addition. Only the new overflow pin failed; the other 16 pins passed.
The spiral fixture checks positive and negative overflow in a valid 642-vertex loop.
Copying the upstream nesting entry back failed with `E0432`. Restoring the stacked entry passed all 17 pins.
The four planner/test files stayed byte-identical when the branch moved onto #2808.
The stacked branch passed the focused pins and the upstream-entry mutation again.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: batch fallback, 937 steps, zero failures.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

## Goldens moved

The direct comparison with newer upstream also shows eight upstream-only Explain fixtures added by #2793:
`carvera.nc`, `grblhal.nc`, `sinker-iso.nc`, `sinumerik.nc`, `tinyg.nc`, `tormach-lathe.nc`, `tormach-plasma.nc`, and `wire-iso.nc`.
These are under `crates/post/tests/golden/explain/`. The child patch does not change or delete them.

## Not exercised

I did not run release-only heavy lanes or pixel snapshots.
I did not trial-merge later parent changes after `1947b6b6c` or newer main commits into this branch.

The #2159 change in that file adds the `cut_order` export beside the placement API.

title: feat(motion): equal depth steps as an opt-in ladder parameter
body:
## What changed

- The default depth ladder does not change. It keeps the remainder in the last step. `top 20, bottom 2, stepdown 5` cuts `[15, 10, 5, 2]`.
- A new operation parameter, `equal_steps`, is in the `links.approach` object. The default is off.
- With `equal_steps` on, the ladder cuts the same number of levels in equal steps. The same example cuts `[15.5, 11, 6.5, 2]`.
- `camcraft_motion::machining2d::equal_stepdown` gives the stepdown of the equal ladder. The level law `cut_levels_under` walks it. There is still one level law.
- `cut_levels_for(top, &approach, bottom, stepdown)` reads the mode and the stock top from the approach. These ladders call it: 2D Pocket (rings, adaptive, HSM, trochoidal, avoid), 2D Adaptive rest, 2D Contour, Slot, Bore, Circular (and its vault rings), 3D Pocket (plain, shell, rest refine).
- With stock above Top Z (#2004), the level at Top Z stays. The steps below it are equal.
- The project file writes `equal_steps` only when it is on. Older files load without a change.
- The params digest takes one byte only when the mode is on. The stamp of each existing operation does not change.
- The pocket region law of the app (`operation::area::ladder_planes`) reads the same mode through `OpParams::ladder_stepdown`. The region is built at the planes that the generator cuts.
- The Lead in / Lead out tab has one new row, "Equal depth steps", in the Linking group.
- `docs/decisions/2012-equal-steps.md` records the decision.

The parameter is undoable through `EditOperationParams`. The MCP `edit_operation` patch reaches it as `params.links.approach.equal_steps`. No new command and no new MCP tool are necessary.

## Cause

Issue #2012 asks for a decision between a remainder last step and equal steps. The level law had only the remainder ladder. The project rule "CAM choices are parameters" asks for a parameter with a default.

## Scope limit

Face, Trace, Engrave and Trochoidal Slot have no `links` object. They cannot save the parameter and keep the remainder ladder. Issue #2832 adds the parameter to them. Turning has its own infeed laws and is not part of this change.

## UI screenshots

The images show the Lead in / Lead out tab before and after the new row.
The before image uses the same merged scene with only the new row removed.
A temporary CPU renderer drew the real egui meshes, fonts and textures.
The test harness uses a placeholder viewport. The environment has no WGPU adapter.
No capture code or images are in the PR branch.

![Before: Linking group without Equal depth steps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/d20bbdb08204c89873c18935732cf7039c10375c/pr-2842/leads-before.png)

![After: Linking group with Equal depth steps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/d20bbdb08204c89873c18935732cf7039c10375c/pr-2842/leads-after.png)

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/equal_steps.rs`:

- `the_default_ladder_keeps_the_remainder_and_equal_steps_is_opt_in`
- `equal_steps_keep_the_level_count_and_never_pass_the_stepdown`
- `equal_steps_keep_the_level_at_top_z_under_stock`
- `equal_steps_refuse_what_the_remainder_ladder_refuses`
- `a_pocket_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_pocket_with_keepouts_and_relief_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_trochoidal_adaptive_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_contour_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_slot_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_bore_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_circular_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_3d_pocket_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`

Pins in `crates/app/tests/equal_steps.rs`:

- `edit_sets_equal_steps_and_undo_restores_the_remainder_ladder`
- `the_project_file_writes_equal_steps_only_when_on_and_reads_it_back`
- `the_stamp_tells_the_two_ladders_apart`
- `the_region_law_reads_the_stepdown_of_the_ladder_mode`
- `the_generated_contour_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `mcp_edit_operation_reaches_equal_steps`

Red before the change: yes. The motion pin did not compile on `upstream/main` 3970d3d03 (`Approach` has no field `equal_steps`; `cut_levels_for` and `equal_stepdown` do not exist).

Mutation results:

- Mutation 1: `ladder_stepdown` ignores the mode. Result: red. 10 of the 11 motion pins fail. The refusal pin stays green, which is correct.
- Mutation 2: the 12 caller files are the files of `upstream/main`, and the new law stays. Result: red. The 7 operation pins fail. The 4 law pins stay green.
- Mutation 3: the digest byte and the DTO write are removed. Result: red. `the_stamp_tells_the_two_ladders_apart`, `the_project_file_writes_equal_steps_only_when_on_and_reads_it_back` and `mcp_edit_operation_reaches_equal_steps` fail.
- After each mutation the code was restored and the pins were green again.

The first stamp pin did not fail in mutation 3. A default approach hashes no bytes, so each approach that is not the default already has a different stamp. The pin now also compares two approaches that are not the default.

Gate on the reviewed-finding fix:

- Head: `db53a0a827db8d3a59b518e1960f1f862198e0cd`. It merges `upstream/main` at `81407b31bab58d4037bbae90b18bbecfe9229103`.
- The merge conflict affected imports only. Both import sets stay. `pocket_avoid_with_relief` calls `cut_levels_for`.
- New pin: `a_pocket_with_keepouts_and_relief_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`. It checks both ladders with keep-outs and dogbone relief endpoints.
- Caller mutation: bypass `cut_levels_for`. The pin is RED on the equal cut planes. Restore: GREEN.
- Relief mutation: suppress corner relief. The pin is RED on the missing bottom relief endpoint. Restore: GREEN.
- Law mutation: ignore the equal mode. Eleven pins are RED. The refusal pin stays GREEN. Restore: all 12 motion pins GREEN.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: RED. 163 of 164 steps pass in 22.8 minutes. Both motion and app `equal_steps` suites pass.
- The one failed step is `ui suites: lib`: 1,278 passed, seven failed, seven ignored. All seven failures report `No adapter found`.
- The explicit UI library rerun has the same result in 54.50 seconds. Neither run has a SIGSEGV.
- The seven failures are six `egui_app::report_tests` capture tests and `egui_app::tests::headless_run_succeeds`. The environment exposes no WGPU adapter.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN on this head.
- The final worktree has no capture helper, review evidence or image files. The merge takes main's process version without a manual edit.

File length: `crates/motion/src/approach.rs` was 440 lines and is now 446. `crates/motion/src/machining3d/entry.rs` is now 402 lines.

## Latest review validation

Head: `db53a0a827db8d3a59b518e1960f1f862198e0cd` (unchanged). No source change was required by the latest review.

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: RED. 232 of 233 steps passed in 32.4 minutes.
- Motion heavy tests: 56 passed, zero failed. App heavy tests: 40 passed, one failed. Nine known-fail checks passed as expected.
- The failed pin is `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` in `app:pocket3d_hsm`.
- The failure is the path count assertion at `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:144`. Actual counts are `(3158, 3130, 1141)`.
- This platform uses the unmeasured macOS count range documented with #2371. Earlier safety assertions pass.
- Baseline check: remove all PR source changes in motion and app. Run the exact ignored heavy pin. It fails with the same counts.
- Restore the source and run the exact pin again. It fails with the same counts. `git diff --exit-code` passes after restoration.
- This count failure therefore predates the PR source changes. No count range was changed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: RED. 163 of 164 steps passed in 26.1 minutes.
- Motion: 1,046 passed, zero failed, 54 ignored. App: 1,002 passed, zero failed, 18 ignored.
- All 12 motion `equal_steps` pins and all six app `equal_steps` pins pass.
- UI library in quick: 1,278 passed, seven failed, seven ignored. The other selected UI targets pass.
- Explicit UI library rerun from `crates/ui`: the same counts in 37.23 seconds. Neither run has a SIGSEGV.
- All seven UI failures report `No adapter found`. They are the six report capture tests and `headless_run_succeeds` named in the review.
- This machine reports an Apple M3 Max GPU with Metal support. The test process finds no Metal adapter.
- A passing local UI library run with an accessible graphics adapter remains required.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.
- All commands ran locally with sccache disabled. No tests were skipped to obtain a pass.
- No source, test, screenshot, log, evidence file, or process version was committed. The PR stays a draft.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.cnc"` is empty. The default ladder is the same.

## Not exercised

- No pin generates these ladders with the mode on: the 2D Adaptive rest ladder, the Circular vault rings, the 3D Pocket shell and rest-refine ladders, the rotary and multi-axis roughing. They call the same function as the pinned ladders.
- No pin generates a pocket on a part with the mode on. `the_region_law_reads_the_stepdown_of_the_ladder_mode` pins the stepdown that the region law reads, not the region.
- Code that reads `stepdown` as a bound is not changed (the 3-D shell floor below a plane, the first entry height of the contour). With equal steps it reads a bound a little larger than the real step. The decision file records this.

Whichever merges second refreshes, and must keep the mode in the 3-D ladder.

title: perf(sim): share unchanged cut bricks between playback keyframes
body:
## What changed

- The three cut layers of `SdfField` (`cuts`, `cut_ups`, `cut_downs`) hold each brick in an `Arc` (`CutLayer`, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field.rs`).
- A clone of the field copies the keys and the pointers only. It shares the bricks.
- A write goes through `layer_brick_mut` (`Arc::make_mut`). It copies a brick first when a clone still holds that brick.
- `claim_record` and `up_record` read the cell first. They take the writable brick only when the value changes. A move that changes no cell copies no brick.
- `KeyCost` has a new method, `key_bytes_after(prev)`. The keyframe store counts a keyframe by the bricks that the keyframe before it does not share, and by its map entries.
- `Keyframes::offer` and `Keyframes::held_bytes` use that count. The budget, the thinning and the stride law do not change.
- The public API of the sim crate only grows: `SdfField::cut_bytes_after` and `KeyCost::key_bytes_after` (with a default).

## Cause

A playback keyframe was a whole copy of the cut layers (#2181, PR #2192). Two keyframes one stride apart differ only in the bricks that the moves between them changed. The store paid for all bricks in each keyframe.

## Readings

Dense 100 mm face (`precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face`, release, 4268 moves, 68 keyframes, stride 64):

| | Keyframe bytes | Calculation time |
|---|---|---|
| `upstream/main` (old sim sources) | 444 940 288 (424 MiB) | 49.8 s |
| This PR | 65 181 664 (62 MiB) | 30 s to 32 s (three runs) |

The factor is 6.8. The test asserts a factor of 6 at least.
The machine had other builds in progress, so the times are not exact.

Staged 24 mm face at 0.5 mm cells (debug, 28 keyframes): 9 923 808 bytes held. Whole copies cost 45 301 760 bytes. The factor is 4.56. The test asserts a factor of 4 at least.

## Tests

Pins:

- `the_keyframes_share_the_bricks_that_no_move_changed` (`crates/app/tests/stock_play_precalc.rs`). It asserts the factor of 4, the equality of the running count and the audit, and the bit-identical replay at six positions.
- `a_keyframe_costs_what_the_one_before_does_not_share` (`crates/sim/tests/play_keys.rs`). It asserts the count on plain values, before and after a thinning.
- `a_clone_shares_its_cut_bricks_and_a_write_copies_first` (`crates/sim/tests/play_keys.rs`). It asserts that a clone is not written through, and that the cut over shared bricks is the plain cut, bit for bit.
- `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face` (heavy lane, release). It now asserts the factor of 6 on the dense face.

Red before the fix: the first pin failed on unchanged code with `8454144 bytes held; whole copies cost 8454144`.

Mutations (each one red, then green after the restore):

- `offer` counts `value.key_bytes()` (the old line): `a_keyframe_costs_what_the_one_before_does_not_share` is red.
- `held_bytes` sums whole copies (the old line): the same test is red, `(5, 1, 40, 100)` against `(5, 1, 40, 40)`.
- `layer_brick_mut` writes through the shared pointer: `a_clone_shares_its_cut_bricks_and_a_write_copies_first` is red at "a shared brick is copied before the write".
- `claim_record` takes the writable slot before the read: `the_keyframes_share_the_bricks_that_no_move_changed` is red, `16358624 bytes held; whole copies cost 45301760`.
- All of `crates/sim/src` from `upstream/main`: `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face` is red, `444940288 bytes held; whole copies cost 444940288`.

Unchanged and green: `the_precalculated_stock_is_the_live_cut_at_every_position`, `a_live_seek_after_a_cancel_keeps_the_byte_budget`, `the_worker_calculates_first_then_replays_and_the_post_gate_is_unchanged` (the replay is bit-identical, the budget holds, the post gate reads the same).

Gate on the final head: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green, 11 steps, 0 failed (sim lib, `play_keys`, `play_precalc`, `stock_carry_side_exact`, `stock_columns`, `stock_field_cost`, `stock_sdf`; app `stock_field_cost`, `stock_play_precalc`). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Heavy lanes that ran (release, `--ignored`): app `stock_play_precalc` and app `stock_field_cost`. The two are green.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.png"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` plans 217 steps for this diff. Only the two heavy binaries above ran. The other heavy lanes did not run. Run them before this PR is flagged ready.
- The `camcraft-ui` crate was not built. This PR changes no item that the UI crate can see, other than the two additions.
- The gate and the tests ran without sccache and with a target directory outside the worktree. The sccache daemon on this machine executed no compile, and a stuck `cargo check` of the editor tooling held the build lock of the worktree.
- `CostLedger` (the cut region, the full-brick ledger, the dirty set) is still copied whole by each keyframe. The store does not count it, as before.
- The time of one cell write was not measured alone. The dense face calculation as a whole is faster.

## Overlaps

PR #2714 changes other files in `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/` and `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs`. It changes none of the files of this PR.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2194-share-keyframe-bricks.md`.

Effort: max

Changelog: Simulation playback: keyframes share the stock bricks that no move changed, so the calculation before playback uses much less memory (the dense 100 mm face: 62 MiB, before 424 MiB) and keeps a shorter stride on large programs.

Fixes #2194

title: fix(xtask): derive the gate job budget from available CPUs
body:
## What changed

The default gate budget uses `std::thread::available_parallelism()`.
The default has a floor of 2 and a cap of 64.
CPU detection failure uses 2 jobs.
`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` still accepts any positive whole number.
The plan prints the budget and its source, including in `--dry-run`.
Batch and release already share the budget over dynamic lanes.
Builds, isolated tests, UI steps and clippy keep the full budget.
The lane fixtures use an explicit budget of six.
AGENTS.md and the gate skill describe the new default.
The decision record is `docs/decisions/2814-core-budget.md`.

Process change: yes

## Cause

`budget::DEFAULT` fixed the automatic budget at six.
Larger machines left available CPUs idle unless a runner owner set the override.

## Tests

All pins are in `xtask/src/budget_tests.rs`:

- `the_default_budget_uses_the_available_cpus`
- `the_override_reports_its_source`
- `the_default_budget_has_a_floor_and_cap_with_mock_cpus`
- `an_explicit_budget_is_not_limited_by_the_cpu_floor_or_cap`
- `an_invalid_budget_uses_the_cpu_default_and_names_the_bad_input`

The first two pins failed on unchanged code.
The host default was six instead of 32, and the override had no source note.
The deterministic pins cover missing CPUs, zero, one, the bounds, large counts, empty values and invalid overrides.

Mutation checks:

- Restore `upstream/main:xtask/src/budget.rs` with compatible initial pins: red; restore the fix: green.
- Change the CPU fallback to six: red; restore: green.
- Remove the floor: red; restore: green.
- Remove the cap: red; restore: green.
- Clamp explicit overrides: red; restore: green.

Each mutation failed a runtime assertion.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed: 196 unit tests and 22 integration tests.
The gate took 317 seconds, including a cold application build for a catalog test.
`cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

`cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run` passed without `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS`.
It reported 32 available CPUs, 32 jobs and at most 16 lanes.
The queue used 16 lanes with two jobs each.
Alone steps received 32 jobs.

The gate used base `380c29b3c`.
Upstream advanced with #2809 during verification.
That change does not touch these files.
The branch has no refresh merge.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

A full batch or release gate did not run.
Windows and macOS did not run.
The optional memory guard is omitted.
CPU detection failure is covered through injected values.
The final documentation was added after the green gate, as the requested procedure specifies.

## Overlaps

- #2825 touches `xtask/src/exec.rs`: same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
