title: fix(sinker): judge body electrodes against cavity outlines
body:
Stacked on #2714 (merge #2714 first)

## What changed

This fix changes 23 files relative to parent `b95c27b2e`.
It adds `cavity_outline` to Sinker Burn parameters.
The points use coordinates relative to the burn point.
The project file, operation digest and MCP tools carry the outline.
An empty outline keeps the previous extent law.

The size law compares the electrode with inward cavity wall offsets.
It permits the derived diamond finish electrode.
It still refuses an oversized electrode by name.
It also refuses malformed outlines, contradictory dimensions and an incomplete finish.
Command creation checks the outline and its stated dimensions.
Generation repeats the bounds checks.
The existing scalar law keeps the floor and condition checks.

The MCP schema declares an optional array with a `null` default.
The electrode reply supplies an array for a body and `null` for a rectangle.
A `null` params patch clears the outline.
The independent stock verdict still checks the actual burn.

## UI screenshots

These inherited parent renders use the headless `ShellUi` (`1440x960` WGPU).
The before views show upstream `5ed5b7fe2`.
The after views come from parent PR #2714.
The pictured UI files are unchanged in #2836.
The images are stored only on `mkinney/Camcraft` branch `pr-screenshots`, at commit `0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86`:

| View | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tool editor (`DT-20-60` dovetail cutter) | ![Tool editor before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-before.png) | ![Tool editor after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-after.png) |

## Cause

The previous law judged X and Y extents.
An inward offset moves a sharp diamond corner farther than the condition's undersize.

- `malformed_cavity_outlines_are_refused_by_name`

Each mutation failed its pin with the old code or the guard removed.
Each pin passed after restoration:

- `old-generator`: red / green.
- `shape-point-limit`: red / green.
- `region-lattice`: red / green.
- `extentmatch`: red / green.
- `consumed-inset`: red / green.
- `scalar-floor`: red / green.
- `vector`: red / green.
- `containment`: red / green.
- `finish-coverage`: red / green.

- `early-size`: red / green.

Final targeted runs passed 11 app tests and 10 motion tests.
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran 780 steps.
It passed 779 steps and found one failure in the rectangular MCP reply.
The reply now uses `null` for the absent outline.
The failed step passed on rerun.
All three affected app binaries then passed.
The final early-size guard also passed its red/green check.
Clippy passed for all five touched crates with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`.
Formatting checks passed for the three new Rust files.

## Goldens moved

The required comparison with `upstream/main` shows 13 inherited differences.
Each complete file diff was checked.

Parent commit `b95c27b2e` adds these four files:

title: feat(ui): viewport Display menu with four display modes, Look at and graphics switches
body:
## What changed

- The viewport toolbar has a new button, "Display". It opens a menu above the toolbar.
- The menu has three groups:
  - **Display mode** (one choice): "Shaded, with edges", "Shaded", "Wireframe", "Shaded, with hidden edges".
  - **Look at**: "Look at a face". The next click on a face turns the view to face it.
  - **Graphics**: "Grid", "Origin axes", "Perspective view", "Orthographic view".
- Each entry has a tooltip. The active entries show a check mark (radio or check box).
- Each entry is view state. No entry queues a command.
- `draw_list::plan` gives the draw list of each display mode. `View3D::render_with` follows it.
- "Shaded" draws no wire on the model and on the stock.
- "Shaded, with hidden edges" draws the cached model edges a second time behind the faces, in a lighter tone. It builds no new buffer.
- The display mode and the grid switch are saved in the per-user `view.json`, with the gizmo names. An old file without the keys loads the defaults.
- The display mode choice moved out of the Browser pane ("Solids" radios). The Projection radios stay there.
- The wireframe button stays. One press gives wireframe from each mode.

Not in this PR: the quality preset, the ground shadow, the ambient occlusion, and "Look at" for a plane that is not a model face. Issue #2834 has them. #2818 permits this split.

The fourth mode of #2636 ("Wireframe, see-through") is not in this PR. #2636 stays open for it.

## Cause

This is new work that the maintainer asked for in #2818. The viewport had two display modes and no menu for them.

## Screenshots

Before (unchanged `main` at 380c29b3c):

| Browser "View" door with the "Solids" radios | Shaded | Wireframe |

|---|---|
| ![after wireframe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2818/after-wireframe.png) | ![after hidden edges](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/issue-2818/after-shaded-hidden-edges.png) |

The screenshots come from the off-screen harness of the guide images. They are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch. No image is in this branch.

## Tests

Pins (all new, all green on the head):

- `ui::draw_list::tests` (6 tests): the draw list of each display mode, the traced stock, the empty document.
- `egui_app::tests::display_menu` (6 tests):

  - `each_display_mode_entry_sets_the_mode_and_shows_the_check`
  - `the_graphics_entries_set_their_fields`

  - `look_at_on_empty_space_changes_nothing_and_says_so`

- `view_file::the_display_mode_and_the_grid_round_trip_and_an_old_file_loads_the_defaults` (`camcraft-app`).

Red before the change: the pins use new types, so they do not compile on unchanged `main`. The mutation checks below show that each guard is pinned.

Mutation results (the guard was broken, the pin went red, the guard was restored, the pin went green):

| Broken guard | Red test |
|---|---|
| `plan`: "Shaded" draws the model edges | `shaded_draws_faces_and_no_edges` |

None. No `.nc` file, no `.cl` file and no snapshot PNG changed.

This PR adds `Nav::Display` to the same lists and one arm to `act` and `draw`. It touches the same functions on different lines. Whichever merges second refreshes, and #2783 then needs a tooltip for `Nav::Display`.

## What changed
- Added `CornerRelief` (`None`, `Dogbone`, `TBone`), `TBoneDirection` (`LongEdge`, `ShortEdge`, `Horizontal`, `Vertical`), and per-corner `overrides` to `OpParams::Pocket`, `OpParams::Adaptive2D`, and `OpParams::Offset2D`.
- Implemented inside-corner detection (with micro-fillet chord collapse) and relief spur splicing in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/corner_relief.rs` and `corner_relief_spur.rs`, plus corner-blend ban seeding in `pocket_emit.rs`.
- Added operation safety checks in `crates/app/src/operation/corner_relief.rs` for stock bounds, `Exclude` and open far-side regions, `DoNotTouch` keepouts, kept/neighbour steel, and multi-height thin-wall punch-throughs.
- Refused `Adaptive2D::Trochoidal` with active corner relief by name in `crates/app/src/operation/types/sane.rs`, `generate.rs`, and the UI panel.
- Added strictly bounded verification corridors (`CornerReliefZone`) in `crates/sim/src/verify/corner_relief.rs`, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/corner_relief.rs`, and `crates/app/src/operation/corner_relief_sim.rs`.

## Cause
Inside sharp corners of closed 2D pockets and square slots always leave unmachined corner fillets equal to the cutter radius. Adding opt-in bisector (`Dogbone`) or tangent (`TBone`) spurs extends the cutter center to the true corner reach while pre-emission guards and bounded verification zones block wall gouges and punch-throughs.

title: feat(2d): arc turns and their radius on Face, 2D Contour and Slot
body:
## What changed

Face, 2D Contour and Slot have the arc turns option with a corner arc radius. The parameters are `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`, the same as on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset (#1733).

All three kinds can round their corners safely. No kind is left out.

- **2D Contour** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the tool radius, as before.
- **Face** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the semicircle of half the row spacing, as before. A smaller radius gives two quarter arcs with a straight step between them. The step is one radius outside the overrun line, away from the footprint. With a radius, rows spaced wider than the tool diameter turn on arcs too.
- **Slot** gets `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`. Each row-end corner of the serpentine pass turns on one tangent arc. No radius is the tool radius. The new module is `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_turns.rs`.

The parameter door (`sane.rs`) refuses a radius below 0.01 mm on the three kinds. The generators refuse a radius larger than the tool radius, with the text of `corner_arc_radius`. The project file writes the keys only when they are set. The cache digest reads the radius only when the option is on.

The operation pages show the radius rows when the option is on. The Face page names its default "Arc radius = half the row spacing".

MCP: `edit_operation` sets the two fields through `EditOperationParams`. No new command and no new tool are necessary.

The type is `feat`, because the change adds parameters. The task template gave `fix`.

## Cause

The fix for #1733 gave the radius to the three pocket kinds only. Face and 2D Contour had the option without a radius. Slot did not have the option.

## Which corners turn, and why no arc cuts past the wall

- 2D Contour: only a corner that turns toward the air gets an arc. This is the law of `fillet.rs`, and it did not change. A corner that turns toward the part stays sharp, and the notes name it. A convex outside corner is such a corner, so an arc cannot leave material there.
- Face: each point of a turn is on or outside the overrun line, one tool radius from the footprint. The turn reaches one radius past that line at most.
- Slot: the pass is in the cutter-center stadium, which is convex. A fillet is inside the triangle of its corner and its two tangent points, and that triangle is inside the stadium. `fillet_corners` proves each triangle again and keeps a corner sharp if it cannot prove it. An arc leaves corner rest at the round end of the slot. The note states the largest rest.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` (13 tests):

- `face_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short` (review fix)
- `no_face_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_overrun_line`
- `a_face_radius_past_half_the_row_spacing_turns_on_the_semicircle`
- `a_face_radius_rounds_rows_spaced_wider_than_the_tool`
- `the_face_door_refuses_a_radius_no_control_can_cut_and_reads_none_when_off`
- `contour_corners_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `no_contour_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_wall`
- `no_contour_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name`
- `slot_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`

### Review fix: the Face radius bound

`corner_turn` in `blend.rs` gave the semicircle when half the row spacing was less than 0.005 mm past the radius. That semicircle is larger than the radius. Now:

- If half the spacing is not more than the radius (1e-9 mm float margin), the turn is the semicircle, as before. Its radius is not larger than the requested radius.
- If half the spacing is more than the radius by 0.005 mm or less, the turn uses two corner arcs. Their radius is half the spacing minus 0.005 mm, which is less than the requested radius. The straight step stays 0.01 mm.
- If that radius is below 0.01 mm, the turn stays sharp. The status line counts it as the `Tiny` refusal ("row spacing below the 0.020 mm arc resolution").

The images show the Passes tab of the Properties panel, cropped. A temporary test rendered the real egui shell with `Harness::render()`. That test is not in the PR. "Before" is `upstream/main` `5fdbed9bd` with arc turns on. "After" is this PR with arc turns on and a radius set. The header of the panel names the seeded operation, so the crop leaves it out. The images are on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

title: fix(xtask): batch suite steps start the built test executables, not cargo
body:
Stacked on #2788 (merge #2788 first)

Process change: yes

## What changed

- Each batch prebuild step (`debug build: <crate> (--no-run)`) has the flag `--message-format=json-render-diagnostics`.
- The executor keeps the JSON messages of that build. It records the test executables of the crate from them (`xtask/src/artifacts.rs`).
- A suite step of that crate (`--lib`, `--bins`, `--test <name>`) then starts its executable. It does not start cargo (`xtask/src/direct.rs`).
- The executable starts as `cargo test` starts it. The working directory is the package directory. The args are the libtest args after `--`. The variables are the ones that cargo sets: `CARGO`, `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, `CARGO_MANIFEST_PATH`, the `CARGO_PKG_*` set, `CARGO_BIN_EXE_<bin>`, `OUT_DIR`, the `rustc-env` pairs of the build script, and the dynamic library path.
- The gate writes cargo's `Running <target> (<path>)` line into the step log. `read_log`, the notes and `--failed` read the log as before.
- The step names, the step numbers, the log file names and `--dry-run` do not change. `--only` and `--failed` do not change.
- The executable path comes only from the cargo JSON list. The gate does not search `target/`.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_NO_DIRECT=1` makes each step a cargo step again.
- `xtask/src/json.rs` is a small JSON reader. The PR adds no dependency.

These steps stay cargo steps:

- a `--doc` step (a doctest has no executable);
- a step that `--only` or `--failed` selects without its build step;
- a step whose target has no executable in the list;
- each step of the quick tier, the heavy lanes and the release tier.

## Cause

- `Run::execute` started `cargo test -p <crate> --test <binary>` for each suite step. The build step before it had built that binary already.
- Each cargo start costs time, and parallel cargo starts wait for the lock of the build directory. The step log of the pin shows `Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`.

## Tests

Pins (all in `xtask`):

- `direct_tests::batch_suite_steps_run_the_built_test_executables_without_a_cargo_start`. It runs the real executor on a fixture workspace. Red before the fix: `post_suites_lib: the step must start the test executable, not cargo`, and the log has cargo's `Finished` line.
- `direct_tests::a_selected_suite_step_without_its_build_step_starts_cargo_as_before`. It is green before and after the fix. It guards the `--only` path.
- `artifacts_tests::package_takes_only_its_own_test_executables_from_the_json`
- `artifacts_tests::package_gives_the_variables_of_a_cargo_test_process`
- `artifacts_tests::package_refuses_a_build_that_did_not_finish_or_a_package_it_does_not_know`
- `artifacts_tests::only_a_single_crate_debug_build_with_json_records`
- `artifacts_tests::a_debug_target_step_of_a_recorded_package_runs_its_executable`
- `artifacts_tests::the_batch_plan_records_each_crate_and_keeps_its_steps`
- `artifacts_tests::json_reads_cargo_lines_and_refuses_bad_text`
- `artifacts_tests::lib_path_puts_the_build_dirs_first_and_keeps_the_current_value`
- `step_tests::batch_prebuild_leaves_suite_steps_fresh_with_truck_dev_dep` (of #2788) got one line. It sends the JSON output of the build to null.

Mutation results. Each mutation was put in by hand and removed again. The pins were green after each restore.

| Mutation | Pin that went red |
|---|---|
| `plan::debug_build_crate` without the JSON flag (the old args) | `batch_suite_steps_run_the_built_test_executables_without_a_cargo_start`, `only_a_single_crate_debug_build_with_json_records`, `the_batch_plan_records_each_crate_and_keeps_its_steps` |
| `direct::of` does not set the package variables | `batch_suite_steps_run...` (the fixture test read `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` of `xtask`), `a_debug_target_step_of_a_recorded_package_runs_its_executable` |
| `direct::run` starts in the workspace root | `batch_suite_steps_run...` (the fixture test asserts its working directory) |
| `direct::of` accepts an arg that it does not know (`--release`, `--features`) | `a_debug_target_step_of_a_recorded_package_runs_its_executable` |
| `direct::records` accepts a build of two packages | `only_a_single_crate_debug_build_with_json_records` |
| `artifacts::package` takes an artifact that is not a test build | `package_takes_only_its_own_test_executables_from_the_json`, `package_gives_the_variables_of_a_cargo_test_process` |
| `artifacts::package` takes the artifacts of other packages | `package_takes_only_its_own_test_executables_from_the_json` |
| `artifacts::package` accepts a build that failed | `package_refuses_a_build_that_did_not_finish_or_a_package_it_does_not_know` |

Gate on head `68feacb29`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. 1 step (`xtask unit tests`), 184 s. 201 unit tests and 22 integration tests pass.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: no warnings.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run`: 929 steps, the same names as on #2788.

## Wall time

Measured on macOS (16 cores, shared with other agent builds, load about 10), job budget 6, warm build, compile cache off. The selection is 5 build steps and the 205 suite steps of `geometry`, `cl`, `tools`, `post` and `sim`:

`cargo xtask gate batch --only "debug build: geometry" ... --only "sim suites"` (210 of 929 steps, all green in each run).

| Run | Mode | Wall time | Sum of the step times |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | `CAMCRAFT_GATE_NO_DIRECT=1` (one cargo start for each step) | 109 s | 199 s |
| B1 | this PR (direct) | 89 s | 178 s |
| A2 | `CAMCRAFT_GATE_NO_DIRECT=1` | 102 s | 186 s |
| B2 | this PR (direct) | 87 s | 173 s |

- The mean is 105.5 s with cargo and 88 s direct. That is 17 % less wall time for the same steps.
- The wall time is from the creation time of the log directory to the last write of `timings.tsv`.
- The first direct run of the same selection had a cold build. It was green: 210 steps, 9.8 min.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes.

## Not exercised

- A full batch gate (929 steps). Only the 210 steps above ran. The `kernel`, `motion`, `app` and `ui` suites did not run in direct mode.
- Windows and Linux. The issue gives 0.5 s for one cargo start on Windows. The measurement above is macOS only.
- The post-merge runner (`post-merge.yml`).
- A crate with a dynamic library from a build script. The path is set from `linked_paths`, and a unit test pins the list. No real crate of that kind ran.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_NO_DIRECT=1` has no unit test. The A runs above used it.
- The `gate` skill text (`.claude/skills/gate/SKILL.md`) still says that each step calls `cargo test`. The worker session could not edit that file. It needs an update.

## Overlaps

- #2788 (open): `Run::execute` and `Run::step` in `xtask/src/exec.rs`, `plan::debug_build_crate` in `xtask/src/plan.rs`, `run_schedule` and `drain` in `xtask/src/queue.rs`. This PR is stacked on its head `1da2bcca2`. The parent of #2788 (#2779) is merged.
- #2787 (draft, `needs-rework`, `conflicts`): it touches `xtask/src/exec.rs` and `xtask/src/main.rs`. Whichever merges second refreshes.

The decision record is `docs/decisions/1951-gate-direct-test-exe.md`.

Changelog: The batch gate starts each built test executable itself and no longer starts cargo for each suite step (#1951).

Effort: high

Fixes #1951

title: fix(drilling): Back bore (G89) carries the dwell and feeds out at the plunge feed
body:
## What changed

- The drill generator now writes the user's dwell into the `Cycle` record of a Back bore (G89) hole.
- The Back bore chain now feeds out at the plunge feed. This is the same feed as the feed in.
- The Sinumerik post writes `P0` for a G89 hole with zero dwell. This clears a previous positive dwell.
- No golden file changed.

Files:

- `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs`: the two changes above.
- `crates/motion/src/drilling/tests_backbore.rs`: the two pinning tests (new file).
- `crates/motion/src/drilling/mod.rs`: registers the test module.
- `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps`: writes an explicit G89 P word, including zero.
- `crates/post/tests/sinumerik_g89_dwell.rs`: pins the G89 dwell unit and the transition to zero.
- `docs/decisions/1480-backbore-dwell.md`: the decision entry.

## Cause

`drill()` set the dwell of a Back bore hole to 0. The dwell of the user did not reach the cycle record, the simulation or a post.

`drill()` also fed out at the cutting feed. A canned G89 has one F word, and the post takes it from the first cutting move of the hole, which is the plunge. The control fed out at the plunge feed, but the CL chain said the cutting feed. The verifier and the simulation read a different motion than the machine ran.

## Dwell unit for each post

The posts read the dwell in seconds and write their own P unit. The Sinumerik post now writes G89 P at zero too. These tests pin the words:

- Fanuc, Mazak, Doosan: `G89 ... P500` (whole milliseconds). `crates/post/tests/dwell_cycles_modal_p.rs`.
- grblHAL, Tormach, LinuxCNC: `G89 ... P0.5` (seconds). The same file.
- Haas: `G89 ... P500`. `crates/post/tests/haas_dwell_cycles.rs`.
- Mach4: `G89 ... P0.25` (seconds). `crates/post/tests/mach4_post.rs`.
- Sinumerik: `G89 ... P500`, then `G89 ... P0`. `crates/post/tests/sinumerik_g89_dwell.rs`.
  Unit source: [Siemens ISO dialects Function Manual, 07/2021](https://cache.industry.siemens.com/dl/files/254/109801254/att_1077768/v1/ONE_840Dsl_828D_iso_dialects_fct_man_0721_en-US.pdf), table 6-1, printed page 95. Section 6.3.1 describes modal cycle parameters.
- Heidenhain: an explicit chain with one `FUNCTION DWELL TIME` block. `crates/post/tests/heidenhain_cycles.rs`.
- The lathe posts and the posts with no canned cycle refuse the Back bore by name.

## Tests

Pins (`camcraft-motion`, lib):

- `drilling::tests_backbore::back_bore_carries_the_dwell`
- `drilling::tests_backbore::back_bore_feeds_in_and_out_at_the_plunge_feed`

Post pins (`camcraft-post`):

- `sinumerik_g89_dwell_posts_p_in_milliseconds`
- `sinumerik_g89_zero_dwell_clears_previous_p`

Red on unchanged code:

- `back_bore_carries_the_dwell`: `G89 dwells at the bottom: the cycle record carries the user's 1.5 s, got 0`.
- `back_bore_feeds_in_and_out_at_the_plunge_feed`: `left: Some(500.0) right: Some(100.0)`.

Mutations:

- The old feed-out feed (`p.feed`) put back: `back_bore_feeds_in_and_out_at_the_plunge_feed` is red. Restored: green.
- `CycleKind::BackBore` removed from the dwell list: `back_bore_carries_the_dwell` is red. Restored: green.

Gate on final head `766540356cab0fc156ea47466977f9432e0eeae4`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: PASS, 69 steps, 0 failed, 6.1 minutes. 1126 tests passed; 16 were ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS, no warnings.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: PASS, 217 steps, 0 failed, 27.5 minutes. The three checks for known failures in #1950 failed as expected. The gate accepted those expected failures.
- Reached lanes: motion heavy and app heavy. Tested head: `766540356cab0fc156ea47466977f9432e0eeae4`.
- Motion heavy: 56 tests passed. Two known-failure checks for #1950 failed as expected and the gate accepted them.
- App heavy: 42 tests passed. One known-failure check for #1950 failed as expected and the gate accepted it.
- Sinumerik mutations: removing the milliseconds scale made `sinumerik_g89_dwell_posts_p_in_milliseconds` fail (`P1`, expected `P500`). Restoring the scale made it pass. Restoring the old P condition made `sinumerik_g89_zero_dwell_clears_previous_p` fail (the second G89 had no `P0`). Restoring the fix made both tests pass.
- Commands used `RUSTC_WRAPPER=` and `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty. No recorded program has a Back bore that the generator makes.

## Not exercised

- No test posts a generated Back bore with a dwell from the operation to the G-code in one run. The generator pin and the post pins meet at the `Cycle` record.
- The Heidenhain post writes the Back bore as an explicit chain. Its retract line now has the plunge feed for a generated Back bore. The existing Heidenhain test uses a recorded chain and did not change.
- The UI was not started.

## Behaviour that changes for a program with no dwell

A Back bore with no dwell keeps the same F. The Sinumerik G89 block now includes `P0` to clear a previous dwell. Its `.cl` chain changes: the feed out is now the plunge feed. The simulation time of the retract changes with it.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes a file in `crates/motion/src/drilling/`.

Effort: high

Changelog: Back bore (G89) holes now carry the dwell at the bottom, and the toolpath feeds out at the plunge feed, as the canned cycle does. Sinumerik G89 clears the dwell when it changes to zero.

Fixes #1480

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Pocket from the previous operations
body:
## What changed

The rest group of the 2D Pocket has a new mode, "previous operations".
In this mode the rest area is read from the stock that the earlier operations of the same setup leave.
The entered-tool mode of #1489 does not change, and it stays the default.

- `RestParams` has the field `source` (`RestSource::EnteredTool` or `RestSource::PreviousOperations`).
- `machining2d::rest_pocket_previous` plans the rest passes from a column grid.
  `rest_stock_from_columns` builds the `RestStock` of #2031 from that grid, one floor for each cut depth.
  `rest_plan_stock` makes the rest area from it.
- The grid is the one that `rest::prior_state` builds for the 3D Pocket: the setup stock, cut by the cached paths of the earlier operations, each with its tool shape.
- The reading is conservative:
  - A column stands at a cut depth when its top is above that depth. A floor allowance is material.
  - The standing columns grow by one cell diagonal.
  - A column that cannot be read stands. The pocket outside the grid stands.
  - The rest area is the union over all cut depths. A roughing pass that stops above the floor leaves the whole pocket.
- The two modes never use the planner of the other mode. Each planner refuses the other mode by name.
- The mode rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest.source` and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter.
  A file without the key reads as the entered tool.
- The Pocket page has the row "Rest stock from". The previous tool rows hide in the new mode.

Generation refuses by name when the stock cannot be established:

- an earlier operation of the setup has no toolpath;
- an earlier operation of the setup has a stale toolpath;
- an earlier operation of the setup is suppressed and has a cut on record;
- the Pocket is tilted (also refused at the edit).

When no earlier operation cut, the stock is known. The whole pocket is cut and a note says it.

## Cause

The rest generator trusted the entered previous tool.
It could not see the depth that the earlier operation reached (#1490, item 3).

## Tests

Pins, all new:

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_tests.rs` (lib): `each_reading_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `a_floor_cut_at_the_cut_depth_does_not_stand_and_one_above_it_does`, `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_previous.rs`: 6 tests. They compare the rest area with an independent simulation of the earlier operations: a flat tool, a wall allowance, a bull-nose tool, mixed tools with a partial depth and disconnected cuts, an island. The rest path cuts each column that was left and cuts no wall.
- `crates/app/tests/rest_previous_ops.rs`: 7 tests. The real job against an independent simulation; the shallow roughing pass; the four refusals; stale after a changed tool, depth and order; `RegenerateAll`; undo and redo; the project file; MCP with save and reopen.
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` now also covers the mode.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/rest_source_tests.rs`: 2 tests for the new row.

Red before the change: the pins use the new API and do not compile on `upstream/main`. Thus the mutation results below are the proof for each guard.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant | Restored |
|---|---|---|---|
| every cut depth is read (`Guards::depth`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| an unreadable column stands (`Guards::unknown`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| the pocket outside the grid stands (`Guards::outside`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| one cell of growth (`Guards::cell`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| `rest_plan` refuses the new mode | `the_two_rest_modes_never_use_each_others_planner` | red | green |
| `rest_pocket_previous` refuses the entered mode | same | red | green |
| `validate` does not read the previous tool in the new mode | same | red | green |
| job: tilted plane refused | `a_tilted_plane_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit_and_at_generation` | red | green |
| door: tilted plane refused at the edit | same | red | green |
| job: `previous_ops_refusal` is called | `a_stock_that_cannot_be_established_is_refused_by_name` | red | green |
| earlier operation suppressed | same | red | green |
| earlier operation stale | same | red | green |
| earlier operation never generated | same | red | green |
| the Pocket arm routes the mode | `the_rest_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left` | red | green |
| stamp byte 0xD8 | `the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` | red | green |

The first four guards have a switch in the code (`rest_prior::Guards`), and the unit test turns each off. The other eleven were removed by hand.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the head merged with `upstream/main` c4ac3ce6d: green, 357 steps, 0 failed (29.2 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.png"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- A setup whose stock is carried from an earlier setup (#318). The code path is `rest::prior_state`, which the 3D Pocket uses. No test here crosses a setup boundary. The check for stale operations reads the same setup only.
- A WCS yaw. The existing `wcs_yaw::enter` turns the grid. No test here has a yaw.
- The field stock engine (#586, #637). The reader is `Columns`, which reads the two engines. The tests use the column grid.
- Zigzag and Offset rings in the new mode. They use the passes of the entered-tool mode, which has its own tests. The new tests use Waterline.
- The pixel snapshots (release lane). The new row moves the rows of a Pocket page that has rest machining on.
- The app was not started by hand. The UI tests ran the page in the test harness.

## Known limits (recorded in `docs/decisions/2033-rest-previous-ops.md`)

- One rest area for all levels. An upper level can cut air where only a lower level has material.
- The strict reading keeps a band of about 1.5 cells along each wall that an earlier tool rode. The rest pass follows those walls.
- The Adaptive strategy stays refused. The Adaptive strategy of the 2D Pocket is retired, so `rest_adaptive` has no door from this operation.
- The MCP skill text (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`) does not describe the new `source` key. The session could not write that file. That edit is owed.
- The guide pages on the site do not describe the new mode.

## Overlaps

- #2716 changes `generate.rs`, `job.rs` and `params.rs` in other arms (the Contour kind). Different function parts. The PR that merges second refreshes.
- #2714 changes `generate.rs`, `params.rs` and `machining2d/mod.rs` for the Slot Undercut kind. Different lines. The PR that merges second refreshes.
- #2678 changes `generate.rs`, `job.rs` and `machining2d/mod.rs`. Its hunks are not in the rest branch of the Pocket arm. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Changelog: The 2D Pocket's rest machining can read the remaining material from the previous operations of the setup ("Rest stock from: Previous operations"), at every cut depth, in place of an entered previous tool.

title: feat(fidelity): vouch for a mesh of unknown fidelity (VouchModelFidelity)
body:
## What changed

- A new undoable command, `VouchModelFidelity { model, by }`, clears the "fidelity unknown" mark of one model. It also clears the mark of each stock that is copied straight from that model.
- The command is one labelled undo step. The label names the person who vouched. Undo puts each mark back.
- The command refuses by name:
  - a model with a recorded coarse chord (#864);
  - an incomplete model (#1610);
  - a model that is not marked;
  - a name that is not a model;
  - an empty name of the person who vouches.
- A new component, `FidelityVouched { by, rev }`, records who vouched. The record is valid only while the model has the same geometry revision and no fidelity flag.
- The project file keeps the record in the optional key `fidelity_vouched` of the model row. There is no project version step.
- The MCP tool `vouch_model_fidelity { model, by }` runs the same command. `get_job` shows `models[].fidelity_vouched`. A script uses the tool through `cam.call`.
- The model page shows a name field and the button "Vouch for this mesh" below the "Fidelity unknown" line. A vouched model shows who vouched.

## Cause

Since project v59, each mesh of an older project without a recorded chord loads as "fidelity unknown" (#1056). The gate refuses its operations until a re-import. A model whose source file is gone, or whose mesh is exact, had no other path to a post.

## Tests

Pins:

- `crates/app/tests/vouch_fidelity_mcp.rs`
  - `a_vouched_model_posts_and_its_undo_is_refused_again`: the post refuses, the tool vouches, the post writes a file, undo refuses again, redo passes again.
  - `the_tool_refuses_by_name_and_enters_no_history`
- `crates/app/tests/vouch_fidelity.rs`
  - `a_vouched_model_passes_the_gate_and_its_undo_is_refused_again`
  - `a_recorded_coarse_chord_is_never_vouched_away`
  - `every_other_bad_input_is_refused_by_name`
  - `the_record_speaks_only_for_the_facets_it_was_given_for`
  - `the_vouch_rides_the_project_file`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/model_vouch.rs`
  - `model_page_vouches_for_an_unknown_mesh_and_undo_brings_the_row_back`

Red before the change: `a_vouched_model_posts_and_its_undo_is_refused_again` failed on unchanged `upstream/main` (`e048b103c`) at the assert "the tool is listed". The asserts before it passed: the gate and the post refused the model by name.

Mutation results (each guard removed, pins run, guard restored):

| Guard removed | Result | Failing pin |
|---|---|---|
| a recorded coarse chord is refused | red | `a_recorded_coarse_chord_is_never_vouched_away` |
| an incomplete mesh is refused | red | `every_other_bad_input_is_refused_by_name` |
| only stock copies with the unknown mark are cleared | red | `a_recorded_coarse_chord_is_never_vouched_away` |
| a name that is not a model is refused | red | `every_other_bad_input_is_refused_by_name` |
| an empty name of the person is refused | red | `every_other_bad_input_is_refused_by_name` |
| the record is silent for other facets (`rev`) | red | `the_record_speaks_only_for_the_facets_it_was_given_for` |
| the record is silent beside a flag | red | `the_record_speaks_only_for_the_facets_it_was_given_for` |
| the loader refuses a vouch beside a flag | red | `the_vouch_rides_the_project_file` |
| undo puts the mark back | red | `a_vouched_model_passes_the_gate_and_its_undo_is_refused_again` |

All pins are green with each guard restored.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on `beb3a91cb`: 339 steps, 0 failed (the app suites that the diff selects, the `camcraft-ui` lib tests and 16 ui suites). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The gate and clippy ran with an empty `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, because the shared sccache server did not answer compile requests.

## Screenshots

The Properties pane shows the same model before and after the vouch command.
The existing UI test captures both states. The test passes.
A temporary CPU renderer draws the actual egui meshes and textures.
The shell test harness uses a placeholder viewport. These images show the Properties controls.
The images are stored only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch.
No screenshot, renderer, or capture code is part of this PR branch.

Before: the model has unknown fidelity. The name field is empty, so the button is disabled.

![Unknown fidelity in Properties](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/25414055eafe551638580fedf508a0e8aa8fa104/pr-2821/fidelity-unknown.png)

After: the Properties pane records who vouched for the model.

![Vouched fidelity in Properties](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/25414055eafe551638580fedf508a0e8aa8fa104/pr-2821/fidelity-vouched.png)

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

## Not exercised

- The name field was not typed into through the keyboard. The UI pin sets the draft and clicks the button.
- A fixture of unknown fidelity was not vouched in a test. A fixture is a model, so the command accepts it.
- A stock copy whose source model is deleted is not covered. The command takes a model name.
- The screenshots below use the real shell test harness. The app window was not opened by hand.
- The row for `vouch_model_fidelity` in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` is not in this PR. The session could not write to that path. The tool description in `crates/app/src/mcp/vouch_tools.rs` has the facts for the row. A session that can write process files must add the row.

## Overlaps

- #2024 changes `crates/app/src/model_fidelity.rs` and `crates/app/src/mesh_open.rs` (`coarse_source`, `adopt_copies`, `hole_of`, `set`). This PR changes two doc comments in `model_fidelity.rs` and no function there. It touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2792, #2773, #2716, #2678, #2554 and #2149 add rows to the module lists in `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`, `crates/app/src/mcp/mod.rs` or `crates/app/src/commands/mod.rs`. This PR adds one row to each list. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1339-vouch-fidelity.md`.

Changelog: Model page and MCP: a model marked "fidelity unknown" (a project saved before v59) can be vouched for by a named person (`VouchModelFidelity`, `vouch_model_fidelity`), so its operations post again without a re-import; undo puts the mark back.

Effort: high

Fixes #1339

title: fix(motion): keep circular ramp transitions at depth
body:
## What changed

Circular Ramp entries stay at depth between eligible levels of one ring.
The generator uses the existing certified KeepDown link.
Each new ring still enters from clearance.
The final retract stays in place.

The first ramp starts at most 0.1 mm above the remaining material.
A smaller configured gap stays in use.
The remaining material height keeps the rapid above stock over Top Z.
Explicit Retract links and other transition types keep their selected lift planes.
Ramp-to-depth entries keep their lift behavior.

The decision is in `docs/decisions/1807-circular-stay-down.md`.
Effort: high.

## Cause

Circular passed the default Clearance link to every level transition.
The default 2 mm entry gap also made the first ramp travel through excess air.
Readings: the local Circular generator, level-link proof, descent planner, and Approach material-height contract.

## Tests

The two primary pins failed on unchanged upstream code:

- `circular_ramp_stays_down_between_levels_of_one_ring`: 12 upward rapid moves instead of one.
- `circular_first_ramp_starts_just_above_material`: entry began 2 mm above material instead of within 0.1 mm.

The motion suite now passes all six tests.
The pins cover both cut directions and implicit or explicit Ramp transitions.
They also cover smaller entry gaps and alternative link choices.

`circular_stay_down_keeps_stock_entry_safe_and_does_not_gouge` passes four cases.
It tests one or two rings in both directions with stock above Top Z.
Verification accepts each path.
Stock simulation reports zero gouge cells.
`circular_ramp_stay_down_matches_golden` also passes.

The full old-code replacement fails both primary pins.
Seven separate mutations fail their matching assertions:

- Remove the Ramp entry guard.
- Remove the Clearance link guard.
- Remove the Ramp transition guard.
- Remove the ramp-to-depth guard.
- Discard a smaller entry gap.
- Remove the 0.1 mm cap.
- Remove the KeepDown selection.

All pins pass after each restoration.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed 630 steps with zero failures.
The new shared CL fixture made the gate select the broader fixture consumers.
`import_step_guard` passed without a retry.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
The tested branch starts at upstream commit `3970d3d0319e423761c48f9a7e0a6391a14b9403`.

## Goldens moved

Added `crates/app/tests/golden/circular_ramp_stay_down.cl`.
The existing Circular Helix golden has no change.
No `.nc` file changes.

The old generator emits 185 moves for the new fixture.
The fixed generator emits 133 moves.
The comparison changes only the initial air ramps, intermediate clearance rapid pairs, and the move count.
Cut rings, interlevel descent arcs, ring changes, and the final retract stay identical.

## Not exercised

Physical CNC hardware, the PathPilot simulator, and release-only heavy tests did not run.
Later upstream changes were not merged into this branch.

## Overlaps

None at the file checks before the claim.
PR #1713, which blocked the previous attempt, had already merged.

Changelog: Circular Ramp entries stay at depth between levels and start near the remaining material.

Fixes #1807

title: feat(2d): place typed text as single-line engraving strokes (InsertText, MCP insert_text)
body:
First slice of #2679. This PR does not close the issue.

## What changed

- `crates/geometry/src/stroke_text/` is new. It holds our own single-line engraving font and the layout of a typed string.
  - `glyphs.rs` is the glyph table: capital letters, digits, the space and `- _ . : / # + = ( )`. Each glyph is straight strokes on a 4 x 6 grid.
  - `mod.rs` has `strokes()` (polylines in mm) and `sketch()` (a `SketchData` on the layer `text`).
- `crates/app/src/commands/insert_text.rs` is new. `InsertText` is an undoable command. It places the typed text as a `Sketch` on the top face of the stock of a setup, at X, Y and an angle.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/sketch_tools.rs` has the new MCP tool `insert_text`. It calls `InsertText`.
- `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` lists the tool.
- `docs/decisions/2679-engrave-typed-text.md` records the decisions.

The text profile is the same entity as a DXF profile. `move_dxf_profile`, `DeleteEntity`, `get_job` and the project file work on it with no change. The project file format does not change.

## Cause

There was no way to make 2D geometry from typed text. A user had to draw the letters in a CAD program and import a DXF file.

Two facts of `main` set the scope of this slice:

1. The issue says to use a font from `assets/ui/fonts/`. The repository holds no font file. The outlines of the `egui` default fonts need a font parser as a new dependency. A new dependency waits for the maintainer. This PR uses our own stroke font, drawn from scratch. A single-line stroke is also the correct input for the centreline Engrave generator: it gives a solid mark, not a hollow letter.
2. On `main`, an operation on a profile refuses generation by name ("a toolpath from the chains of a DXF profile is not generated yet"). #1869 adds Engrave and Trace on sketch chains, and #1869 depends on #1864 (PR #2716). The toolpath, the verify and the golden CL of #2679 need #1869.

## Refusals by name

- An empty text.
- A character with no glyph. A lower-case letter is refused. It is not changed to a capital, because a silent change puts a wrong mark on a part.
- A cap height outside 0.5 mm to 1000 mm. A letter spacing outside 0 mm to 1000 mm. More than 256 characters.
- A placement that is not finite or is more than 1e6 mm from the stock origin.
- A setup that does not exist. A setup with no stock. A name in use or a reserved name.
- `stroke_text::sketch` fails if a stroke does not chain clean. A text profile cannot hold a rejected chain.

## Tests

Pins (red before the change: the test files did not compile, `unresolved import camcraft_geometry::stroke_text`):

- `crates/geometry/tests/stroke_text.rs`
  - `a_known_string_gives_its_golden_strokes` (golden strokes of `SN-0471`)
  - `each_glyph_chains_with_no_rejection_at_the_extreme_heights`
  - `the_whole_character_set_in_one_string_chains_clean`
  - `the_sketch_is_in_millimetres_on_one_layer_with_the_cap_height_stated`
  - `height_scales_and_letter_spacing_moves_only_the_later_glyphs`
  - `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`
- `crates/geometry/src/stroke_text/mod.rs`: `the_character_set_is_the_glyph_table`, `each_glyph_stays_in_its_box`
- `crates/app/tests/insert_text.rs`
  - `typed_text_lands_as_a_placed_profile_and_undoes`
  - `bad_text_and_bad_places_are_refused_by_name_and_nothing_lands`
  - `a_text_profile_saves_and_loads_with_its_strokes_and_place`
  - `the_mcp_tool_places_text_reports_it_and_takes_an_engrave_operation`

Mutations (each guard removed, the pin run, the guard restored):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `Y` drawn with three stroke ends at one corner | red: `each_glyph_chains_...`, `the_whole_character_set_...` ("3 curve ends meet ... a chain cannot branch") |
| Height check removed in `strokes()` | red: `bad_input_is_refused_by_name` |
| Letter spacing check removed | red: `bad_input_is_refused_by_name` |
| Length check removed | red: `bad_input_is_refused_by_name` |
| Empty-text check removed in `strokes()` | green at first, so the pin was made stricter; then red: `bad_input_is_refused_by_name` (`Ok([])` in place of `Err(Empty)`) |
| No-stock check removed in `InsertText` | red: `bad_text_and_bad_places_...`, `the_mcp_tool_places_text_...` |
| Finite-placement check removed | red: `bad_text_and_bad_places_...` |
| Placement range check removed | red: `bad_text_and_bad_places_...` |
| Reserved-name check removed | red: `bad_text_and_bad_places_...` |

With all guards restored, all pins are green.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green. The change touches the shared crate `camcraft-geometry`, so the quick tier ran as the batch tier.

- Run 1: build, geometry (with `stroke_text`), kernel, cl, tools, post and sim suites: 227 steps ok. The worker tool stopped this run at its time limit in step 228 (`motion suites: lib`). It was not a test failure.
- Run 2 (`--only "motion suites" --only "app suites" --only "ui suites" --only "clippy"`): 709 steps, 0 failed, 53.4 min. `clippy -D warnings` with `--all-targets` on each crate is ok.
- After the gate, one doc comment in `crates/app/src/schema.rs` changed (it names `InsertText` as a writer of `Sketch`). Then `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the suites `insert_text`, `mcp_dxf` and `sketch_project` ran again: all ok.
- The gate ran with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1` and no `RUSTC_WRAPPER`. With sccache, each compile stopped with no progress on this machine.

### Heavy lanes on the reviewed head

Head: `c8734b4492a81a136b66845a2dc0c39626ce407c`.
Heavy diff-selection base: `upstream/main` at `495ef74789b06f9aeaab09a18dd08c9b8ef06a20`.

### Latest quick gate rerun

Head remains `c8734b4492a81a136b66845a2dc0c39626ce407c`.

Command: `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`.

The latest rerun finished with exit 1: 936 steps, 933 passed steps, 3 failed steps, 71.8 minutes.

No source changed. The finding requested gate evidence only, so no new pin or mutation check was needed.
The earlier gate results above describe the original author run. This section records the latest rerun.

### Verification after the follow-up issue

The latest review requests one follow-up issue and a PR body update. #2891 records both missing items.
No source changed. The head remains `c8734b4492a81a136b66845a2dc0c39626ce407c`.

- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: RED, exit 1, 936 steps, 933 passed, 3 failed, 74.3 minutes.
- Base: `upstream/main` at `5fdbed9bd8e7a8bb28e6f162a02ab423842b77e8`. The tests ran on the unmerged PR head.
- The same 11 UI tests failed in `lib`, `egui_app`, and `shell`. The library reports no graphics adapter. All non-UI test suites passed.

- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN, exit 0.

- No new test or mutation applies to this GitHub metadata change. The issue labels and the PR links were checked through `gh`.

## Goldens moved

## Not exercised

- No toolpath, no verify and no posted G-code from a text profile. Generation from profile chains is refused by name on `main` until #1869.
- No UI. There is no dialog and no viewport placement in this PR. The command and the MCP tool are the only doors.
- No script verb `cam.insertText`. Follow-up: #2891 (`MCP: InsertText`).

## Open work for #2679 after this PR

- The Engrave toolpath, verify, post and golden CL on a text profile (needs #1869).
- The UI: type the text, pick the spot, set the height.

title: feat(post): Sodick wire skim passes state their flushing
body:
## What changed

- A wire machine file can state `edm.skim_flushing` (`high` or `low`). It is the flushing of each skim pass.
- `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps` writes its T word (T84 / T85) before each skim's C word.
- The header of the program names the skim flushing word.
- `edm.skim_flushing` needs `edm.flushing`. The machine file parser, `Edm::is_sane`, `Edm::refusal` and the post refuse a file that states only the skim flushing.
- A skim on a machine that states `edm.flushing` and no `edm.skim_flushing` is refused by name. The app writes no file.
- A machine that states no flushing posts its skims as before (#2649).
- The post's machine mirror carries the key only when it is stated.
- The machine editor has a "Skim flushing" choice. It is enabled only while a flushing is stated.
- The MCP `edit_machine` tool takes the key through the same undoable machine patch. No new command is added.
- `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps` writes a note that a stated skim flushing is not programmed.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/2686-sodick-skim-flushing.md`.

## Cause

Since #2649, the Sodick post writes each skim on its own C word. It wrote the flushing word after the threading only. A skim ran on the rough cut's flushing, and the program did not say so. The project had no value for the flushing of a skim.

## Behaviour change

A program with `edm.flushing` stated and skim passes posted before this change. The post refuses it now, until the machine file states `edm.skim_flushing`. The message names the key.

## Tests

Pins (each was red on unchanged code or with its guard removed):

- `crates/post/tests/sodick_skim_flushing.rs` (new, 6 tests):
  - `a_stated_skim_flushing_posts_its_t_word_before_the_skims_c_word`
  - `the_next_sections_rough_cut_selects_the_rough_flushing_again`
  - `a_skim_on_a_machine_that_states_only_the_rough_flushing_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_skim_flushing_without_the_rough_flushing_or_an_unknown_word_is_refused_and_nothing_is_cut`
  - `unstated_flushing_posts_a_skim_as_before` (green before and after: it pins the unchanged output)
  - `the_generic_wire_post_notes_a_stated_skim_flushing_it_does_not_program`
- `crates/app/tests/sodick_wire_passes.rs`:
  - `a_stated_skim_flushing_posts_its_t_word_before_each_skims_c_word` (the new golden, through the app's gate)
  - `a_skim_with_only_the_rough_flushing_stated_is_refused_by_name`
- `crates/post/src/machine/edm_dielectric.rs`:
  - `a_skim_flushing_parses_with_the_rough_flushing_and_is_refused_without_it`
  - `a_parsed_section_with_a_skim_flushing_and_no_flushing_is_not_sane`
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_edit_machine.rs`: `a_wire_tank_and_flushing_edit_is_one_undo_step_and_an_unknown_word_is_refused` (extended).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/machine_wire_edm.rs`: `the_wire_machine_editor_states_the_skim_flushing_only_with_a_flushing`.

Mutation results:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `sodick-wire.cps` and `wire-iso.cps` from `upstream/main` | RED: 5 of 6 in `sodick_skim_flushing`, 2 of 5 in `sodick_wire_passes`. Restored: GREEN |
| `parse_skim_flushing`: the "needs `edm.flushing`" guard removed | RED: `a_skim_flushing_parses_...`, `a_skim_with_only_the_rough_flushing_stated_is_refused_by_name`. Restored: GREEN |
| `Edm::refusal`: the skim flushing rule removed | RED: the `mcp_edit_machine` test. Restored: GREEN |
| `Edm::is_sane`: the skim flushing clause removed | RED: `a_parsed_section_...` at the `is_sane` assert. Restored: GREEN |
| `Edm::fits`: the skim flushing clause removed | RED: `a_parsed_section_...` at the `fits` assert. Restored: GREEN |
| `post::machine::mirror`: the key not written | RED: `a_stated_skim_flushing_posts_its_t_word_before_each_skims_c_word` (the post refuses the skim). Restored: GREEN |
| Machine editor: the enable rule and the reset removed | RED: the UI test. Restored: GREEN |

Gate, on the tree of the pushed head (base `e048b103c`):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 664 steps, 0 failed (all post suites, all app suites, the `camcraft-ui` lib tests).

  - `T85` before `C002` and before `C903`.

## Machine editor captures

These images show the affected tank and flushing controls. A temporary harness renders the actual `dielectric()` function with egui. It uses the real machine types and the accessible-name helper. A CPU renderer draws egui meshes and the font texture. These are section captures, not desktop captures. No capture harness or image is on the PR branch.

After: `51b3940ddb801d9b5fdcc033bbf332c7d2861e4a`. Flushing is high. Skim flushing is low and the control is enabled.

title: fix(wire): add heal_tolerance for bounded 2D swallowtail offsets
body:
## What changed

- Added `heal_tolerance: f64` to `WireRuled` in `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled.rs`, distinct from twist `tolerance`.
- Validated `heal_tolerance` (`is_finite() && >= 0.0`) at the `wire_contour_ruled` door.
- Added `UncutRest` and `cover_healed` in `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/laws.rs` using `reach = k + heal_tolerance.max(COVER_TOL)`.
- Kept `laws::cover` and `laws::cover_run` unchanged for 2-axis, open, and burnout cuts.
- Updated both `ruled.rs` (uniform widening) and `ruled_widen.rs` (per-ruling widening) to read `cover_healed` on both planes and track the worst rest.
- Enforced strict `laws::kerf` (`PATH_TOL`) on both lower moves and upper ring moves inside `ruled::emit`.
- Added an uncut-rest note to `Toolpath::notes` when `COVER_TOL < d - k <= heal_tolerance`.
- Preserved existing `heal_tolerance == 0.0` refusals byte for byte.
- Set `heal_tolerance: 0.0` in existing `WireRuled` callers and tests (`operation/wire_ruled.rs`, `wire_4axis.rs`, `ruled_tests.rs`, `wire_fans.rs`).
- Added `ruled_heal_tests.rs` and `docs/decisions/2693-wire-heal-tolerance.md`.

## Cause

`Region::offset_sharp` already trims local inside-corner swallowtails and bridges shallow slots in 2D.
However, `laws::cover` refused every point past `COVER_TOL` (`0.002 mm`) because `WireRuled` had no explicit healing bound.

## Tests

- Pinning tests in `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled_heal_tests.rs`:
  - `tight_inside_corners_heal_within_heal_tolerance` (failed before fix with `0.0683 mm` cover refusal, passes after fix for `PerRuling` and `Uniform`).

title: fix(sim): simulate cylinder stock along X or Y
body:
## What changed

The column simulation cuts cylinder stock along X or Y, in either direction.
It uses analytic circle sections for the top and the rounded underside.
Removed volume stops at the real underside.
Carried stock uses the same underside.
The viewport draws the laid stock through its existing placed mesh.
The grid builder moves to a separate module to keep the simulation facade near 400 lines.
The decision is in docs/decisions/2758-laid-cylinder-sim.md.

## Cause

The grid builder only represented upright cylinders.
The frame law refused a horizontal cylinder before simulation.
A constant initial top and floor cannot measure the material in a laid cylinder.

## Tests

- laid_cylinders_cut_only_their_real_material_along_x_and_y
- laid_cylinder_refuses_invalid_dimensions_by_name
- laid_cylinder_padding_and_translation_keep_exact_material_sections

- the_eye_draws_the_laid_bars_rotated_stock

The application pin failed on unchanged upstream/main e048b103c with the named laid-cylinder refusal.
The pin passes with the fix.
Eight mutations failed by assertion and passed after restoration.
They cover the frame, grid, removal measurement, carry floor, translation, dimensions, end bound and radial bound.
The first four mutations restore the original files from upstream/main.
The translation mutation removes only the new metadata shifts, because the old file lacks the new struct field.
The new analytic module has no old file. Its three guard mutations remove one guard at a time.

Add the exact 2D nesting kernel to `camcraft_geometry::nesting`.
Preserve the existing raster API.
Compute NFPs and IFPs on the `geo2d::SCALE` grid.
Place parts deterministically with bottom-left-fill.

title: fix(2d): drop near-zero loops from the pocket region on a part
body:
## What changed

- `crates/app/src/operation/area.rs` (`minus_standing`): the result "enclosed area minus standing part material" loses each loop whose absolute area is below `ISLAND_AREA_MIN` (1e-4 mm2).
- `crates/geometry/src/geo2d/slivers.rs`: new method `Region::without_slivers(min_area)`. It filters loops. It does not change a kept loop. A measure that is not positive and finite removes nothing.
- `crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs`: one line, `mod slivers;`.
- `crates/geometry/tests/region_slivers.rs`: two new tests for the method.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/frame_cost_probe.rs`: new pin `area_preview_of_the_default_containment_is_filled`. The helper `adaptive_preview` keeps its behaviour and calls the new `adaptive_preview_with(h, patch, containment)`. The pin selects the welded face with the most strips itself (the concave outer wall of fig8).
- `docs/decisions/2766-preview-sliver-loops.md`: the decision entry.

## Cause

The pocket family on a part cuts the enclosed area minus the part material that stands in it. The enclosed area and the part section share a wall. The two tessellations of that wall disagree by about 1 um. The difference then has 3-point loops of 5e-9 to 1.5e-7 mm2. A clockwise loop of that kind stands outside each boundary. `Region::triangles` refuses the whole region with "hole outside any boundary". Thus `boundary_viz::preview_fill` gave `None` for the biggest fig8 patch with the default Containment.

`selection_region` gives the same region to generation. Thus the slivers also reached generation. This fix removes them there too.

## Screenshots

Both captures use the same fig8 concave outer-wall patch with default Containment and the Boundary group open.
The before capture disables the sliver filter in `minus_standing` to reproduce the missing fill.
The after capture uses the restored PR head.
The images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

| Before: sliver filter disabled | After: sliver filter restored |
| --- | --- |
| ![Fig8 default Containment before the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b7993ca26e8fa68ea8ac24238617e5c901dd35c5/2796/before.png) | ![Fig8 default Containment after the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b7993ca26e8fa68ea8ac24238617e5c901dd35c5/2796/after.png) |

## Tests

Pins:

- `egui_app::tests::frame_cost_probe::area_preview_of_the_default_containment_is_filled` (camcraft-ui lib). It asserts that the preview has a fill, that the region has no loop below 1e-4 mm2, and that the fill area is equal to the region area.
- `without_slivers_drops_near_zero_loops_and_keeps_the_real_ones` and `without_slivers_changes_nothing_for_a_clean_region_or_a_bad_measure` (camcraft-geometry, `region_slivers`).

Red before the fix: yes. On `upstream/main` 971c23faa the UI pin failed at "the area preview is filled".

Mutations:

- Old `area.rs` from `upstream/main`: the UI pin is red. With the fix again: green. The same check on the final tree (the old line in `minus_standing`): red, then green.
- `without_slivers` made a no-op: `without_slivers_drops_near_zero_loops_and_keeps_the_real_ones` is red (4 loops, not 2). With the method again: green.

Author gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed on head `99a91308f`. The quick tier fell back to batch because geometry changed: 934 steps, 0 failed, 57.5 minutes. An earlier run on head 37d295cf0 was also green (922 steps). The last step is `cargo clippy ... --all-targets -- -D warnings` for geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app and ui. It is clean.

The gate ran with `RUSTC_WRAPPER` empty, because the shared sccache server on this machine did not answer.

The [latest review](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2796#issuecomment-7022512995) tested head `99a91308f54dc67573aebb28e832b2d159fbc061`.

title: fix(xtask): the batch gate runs its suites in parallel lanes
body:
Stacked on #2779 (merge #2779 first)

Process change: yes

## What changed

- `cargo xtask gate batch` builds each crate alone first. There is one `debug build: <crate> (--no-run)` step for each crate.
- The batch tier then runs its suite steps in the parallel lanes that the release tier uses (`xtask/src/queue.rs`).
- A quick gate that falls back to the batch plan uses the lanes too.
- The batch queue takes its order from the newest `timings.tsv` of a `batch-*` or `release-*` run. The release queue reads `release-*` runs only, as before.
- The `heavy` tier of #2779 and a quick plan stay one step at a time.
- `AGENTS.md` (batch row of the tier table) and the `gate` skill describe the new batch tier.

The gate keeps its guarantees. Each step runs and has its own log. A red step fails the gate. A failed build stops the run. The checkout is read before each step (VOID). The builds, the `ISOLATED` targets, each ui step and clippy run alone with the whole job budget.

## Cause

- `Run::plan` used the lane queue only when the label was `release`. The batch tier ran each step after the other.
- `plan::batch` had one `--no-run` build for all the crates. `crates/kernel` has a dev-dependency on itself with the `truck` feature. The one build gave the shared dependencies the features of all the crates. A later step with one `-p <crate>` resolved a smaller feature set, and cargo compiled that crate again.

## Tests

Pins (all in `xtask`, red before the fix):

- `step_tests::batch_prebuilds_each_crate_without_mixing_feature_sets`
- `step_tests::batch_prebuild_leaves_suite_steps_fresh_with_truck_dev_dep`
- `lanes_tests::batch_executor_overlaps_lanes_runs_isolated_alone_and_writes_timings`
- `lanes_tests::batch_history_reads_newest_batch_or_falls_back_to_release`
- `tests::batch_skips_slow_binaries_and_release_runs_everything` (updated: it pins the first batch step)

Mutation results:

| Mutation | Pin | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `xtask/src/plan.rs` from #2779 (one build for all the crates) | the two `batch_prebuild*` tests and `batch_skips_slow_binaries_and_release_runs_everything` | red; green after the restore |
| `Run::new`: `lanes` on for `release` only | `batch_executor_overlaps_lanes_runs_isolated_alone_and_writes_timings` | red; green after the restore |
| `lanes::history_for`: `batch` reads `release-*` only | `batch_history_reads_newest_batch_or_falls_back_to_release` | red; green after the restore |

Gate on head `1da2bcca2`:

- `cargo test -p xtask`: 213 tests pass (191 unit, 22 integration).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (1 step, `xtask unit tests`).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: no warnings.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run`: 929 steps. 9 builds run alone, 871 steps are in the queue, 49 steps run alone.

## Wall time

One real `cargo xtask gate batch` run on head `1da2bcca2`: green, 929 steps, 0 failed.

| Reading | Value |
|---|---|
| Machine | 8 cores, shared with other agent builds. The load average was 16 to 31 during the run. |
| Job budget | 6 (the default): 3 lanes x `-j 2` |
| Wall time | 104.5 min |
| Sum of the step times (`summed lane wall time`) | 14993 s = 249.9 min |
| Ratio | 2.4 |
| Builds and clippy (alone) | 716 s. 8 of the 9 crate builds were warm from a stopped run. |
| Longest step | `motion suites: lib`, 2472 s. The issue gives 287 s for it on the post-merge runner. |

- This is not a clean benchmark. The other builds on the machine made each step about 8 times slower than on the runner.
- There is no "before" run on this machine. The sum of the step times is an estimate of a run with one step at a time. It is not a measurement.
- The step logs show that the crate builds do their work. Only `09-debug_build_ui` and `929-clippy` have a `Compiling` line. No suite step compiled a crate.
- The previous worker measured 45.2 min for the same code with a cold `target/` and a job budget of 6 (comment on #2727). The sum of the step times was 5640 s = 94 min there.
- A run on the 16-core machine of the issue, before and after, is not done.

The compile cache was off for this run (`env -u RUSTC_WRAPPER CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`). The sccache server of the machine did not answer. `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1` alone does not help when the environment already sets `RUSTC_WRAPPER`: `exec::cache_env` only declines to add the wrapper.

The 8-core run above shared its machine with other agent builds (load 16-31), so its wall time is not representative.

title: fix(ui): add Delete to model and tool browser menus
body:
## What changed

Models and tools now show Delete in the browser context menu.
The action deletes the item that the user right-clicked.
It uses the existing undoable commands.
Missing or invalid tool targets close the menu.

## Cause

The model menu offered fixture commands but omitted Delete.
Tool rows did not create a context menu target.

## Tests

- `model_context_delete_uses_clicked_model_and_supports_undo_redo`
- `tool_context_delete_uses_clicked_tool_and_supports_undo_redo`
- `tool_context_delete_preserves_existing_missing_tool_block_and_undo`
- `tool_context_delete_hides_missing_or_wrong_kind_targets`

The first three pins failed on unchanged code because the menu did not add Delete.
All four pins pass with the fix.
The historical model menu made its pin fail again.
That mutation retained only empty Tool match arms to compile with the new enum variant.
The historical browser routing made the tool pin fail again.
Removing the tool target guard made the stale-target pin fail.
Each restored fix passed all four pins.

Three existing menu-list assertions now include Delete.
The final quick gate passed all 17 steps.
The UI lib suite passed 1,263 tests and ignored 7 existing tests.
All 15 selected integration suites passed.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

## Goldens moved

None. The diff for `.nc` and `.cl` files is empty.

## Not exercised

Manual desktop interaction and release-only pixel snapshots were not exercised.
The existing tool command permits deletion of a referenced tool.
The operation then shows BLOCKED and names the missing tool.
A pin checks that behavior and its undo.
This PR adds no new tool-reference refusal policy.

## Overlaps

PRs #2773, #2764, #2737, #2678, #2662, and #2149 touch `state.rs`.
PRs #2773, #2764, #2763, #2678, #2554, and #2149 touch `egui_app/tests.rs`.
Each touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
None changes `TreeMenuTarget` or the new test registration location.

Effort: medium

Changelog: Add undoable Delete actions to model and tool context menus in the browser.

## Review screenshots

These screenshots use the offscreen UI render harness.
The before views use the PR parent menu behavior.
The after views use the reviewed head, `3962e985b04f9be2daabce78f8e60d1a3888170e`.
The tool had no context menu before this change.

title: fix(post): a flipped Z refusal names the exact reason
body:
## What changed

- A flipped WCS Z does not post. That does not change.
- The refusal now names the exact reason. The issue permits this result: "or the refusal names the exact reason and the decision is recorded".
- The post engine (`post::wcs_flip::apply`) and the verification gate (`app::setup_wcs_flip::setup_problem`) read the reason from one constant, `post::wcs_flip::Z_REASON`.
- The post engine adds a second clause only for a section that has a canned cycle.
- `docs/decisions/2474-wcs-flip-z-refusal.md` records the decision and answers the two open questions of the issue.

The new text of the post engine:

`operation Probe: the WCS has its Z axis flipped; posting a flipped Z is not supported yet - on a control that reads Z reversed, the tool-length word depends on how the tool lengths were measured (a preset length needs G44, a length touched off on that control needs G43), the project does not state which, and the wrong word moves the tool by twice its length; the section also has a canned cycle, whose R plane a mirrored Z puts on the far side of the hole bottom - clear Flip Z on the WCS page`

## Cause

- The old text gave a general reason: "tool-length compensation (G43) and the canned cycles' retract assume the controller's +Z leaves the work".
- The exact reason is this. The tool is on the physical "up" side of its tip. On a control that reads Z reversed, "up" is the control's -Z.
- A register with a preset length then needs G44. A register with a length touched off on that control needs G43.
- The project states only "Z is flipped". It does not state how the tool lengths were measured.
- The wrong word moves the tool by twice its length. The post cannot select the word, so it refuses.

## The maintainer decides

- This PR does not carry a flipped Z into the program. It closes the issue by the second "Done means" clause.
- A carry needs one new statement from the user: how the tool lengths of the flipped setup are measured. The decision file lists what that work includes.
- If the maintainer wants the carry, the issue stays open or a new issue has that work. This PR files no new issue.

## Tests

Pins:

- `a_flipped_z_refuses_by_name` (`crates/post/tests/wcs_flip.rs`, extended).
- `a_flipped_z_without_a_cycle_names_the_tool_length_word_only` (`crates/post/tests/wcs_flip.rs`, new).
- `a_flipped_z_refuses_the_post_by_name` (`crates/app/tests/wcs_flip_post.rs`, extended).

Red before the fix:

- The two post pins failed on unchanged code. The failure showed the old text.
- The app pin failed with the old `setup_wcs_flip.rs`. The failure showed the old text.

Mutations:

- Old `crates/post/src/post/wcs_flip.rs`: the two post pins are red. Restored: green.
- Old `crates/app/src/setup_wcs_flip.rs`: the app pin is red. Restored: green.
- The cycle clause printed for each section (`if true`): `a_flipped_z_without_a_cycle_names_the_tool_length_word_only` is red. Restored: green.

Gate:

title: feat(ui): stock axis choice on the Stock page (along Z, X, Y or custom)
body:
## What changed

- The Stock page has a "Stock axis" choice: Along Z (default), Along X, Along Y and Custom. Custom shows three angles in degrees: turn about Z (yaw), tilt about Y (pitch), tilt about X (roll). The choice applies to a box and to a cylinder. The old "Rotation (yaw deg)" row is replaced.
- The turn is stored in the stock's existing `Location.rot`. There is no new shape field and no project-file version step.
- Apply sends the whole turn through the undoable `SetStock` (new UI queue entry `CommandKind::SetStockPose`; the old `CommandKind::SetStock { yaw_deg }` stays for its callers). Undo restores the old turn.
- The page reads a stored turn back. A preset turn shows its preset. Any other turn shows Custom with its angles (`camcraft_geometry::geometry::stock_axis`).
- Before any simulation, the page shows a plain note when the simulation cannot cut the drafted stock: a cylinder laid along X or Y, or a stock tilted off the axes. The note asks the simulation's own law (`stock_follow::sim_frame`). The refusals `OBLIQUE_STOCK` and `LAID_CYLINDER` do not change. A box laid along X or Y is a square turn, so the simulation cuts it and no note shows.
- MCP `set_stock` takes an optional `axis` ("z", "x", "y") or `angles_deg` ({yaw, pitch, roll}), not both. It calls the same `SetStock` and returns `{ stock, axis, angles_deg }`. The camcraft-mcp skill row is updated.
- `sketch.rs`: the DXF profile face ignored the stock's turn. Now an upright stock keeps its top face, a stock laid square is read as the same solid unturned, and a laid cylinder or a tilted stock is refused by name (`sketch::NO_TOP_FACE`). `ImportDxf` shows that refusal.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2576-stock-axis.md`.
- Follow-up: #2758 (stock simulation: cut a cylinder or box stock that lies along X or Y).

Process change: yes

## Readings

- X preset = a quarter turn about Y (stock Z goes to world +X). Y preset = a minus quarter turn about X (stock Z goes to world +Y).
- A laid 50 x 40 x 20 box at (3, 4, 5): the profile face is at the highest Z of the turned box, and its normal is world +Z (pinned).

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/stock_axis.rs`:
  - `set_stock_lays_a_cylinder_along_x_and_undo_restores_the_old_turn`
  - `a_turned_stock_survives_the_project_file`
  - `mcp_set_stock_takes_an_axis_and_undo_walks_it_back`
  - `a_profile_lies_on_a_laid_box_and_a_laid_cylinder_is_refused`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/stock_axis.rs`:
  - `the_stock_page_offers_the_stock_axis_and_custom_angles`
  - `apply_lays_the_stock_along_x_and_undo_stands_it_up_again`
  - `a_custom_turn_reads_back_with_its_angles`
  - `a_laid_cylinder_shows_the_simulation_note_and_a_laid_box_does_not`
- `layout_page_stock` now has the "Stock axis" anchor.
- `camcraft-geometry` unit tests: `each_preset_carries_the_stock_axis_onto_its_world_axis`, `custom_angles_read_back_and_a_bad_angle_is_refused`.
- The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui` goes up by 4. No snapshot PNG changes.

## Gate

The gate is INCOMPLETE and is owed.

- Command: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on head d067defa4. The quick gate fell back to batch, because the change touches `camcraft-geometry`.
- The coordinator stopped the gate at step 553 of about 900, to free disk space for an other gate. Steps 1 to 552 finished.
