title: feat(sim): step the simulation to the next or the previous operation
body: ## What changed The simulation transport bar has two new buttons, **Previous op** and **Next op**, between Stop and the slider. Page Up and Page Down do the same steps. - **Next op** moves the playhead to the start of the next operation in program order, and pauses the playback. - **Previous op** moves to the start of the current operation. A second press moves to the start of the one before it. - The readout already names the current operation (`Contour1 · RAPID · ...`). After a step it names the new operation. - **Next** is disabled in the last operation. **Previous** is disabled at the start of the first operation. Both are disabled while the stock removal is calculated, as the slider is (#2611). - The tips (and the AccessKit descriptions) say what each step does, name the target operation and name the key. - A step across a setup boundary, a tool change or a WCS change is the same step. An operation with no toolpath is not on the timeline, so it is no stop. - The user guide (`guide/operations` "Checking") describes the two steps. The lookup is on `sim::Script` in `camcraft-sim` (`crates/sim/src/sim_steps.rs`: `op_starts`, `next_op_start`, `prev_op_start`, `op_starting_at`), so the stand-alone simulator (#2587) can use the same steps. The UI part is `crates/ui/src/egui_app/sim_steps.rs`; `shell.rs` gets one call. An operation starts at its first segment on the timeline (the connector rapid, when there is one). At that position all moves of the earlier operations are complete. A step is a scrub to that time, so the stock follows the playhead as for a scrub. Decision record: `docs/decisions/2608-sim-op-step.md`. ## Screenshots Headless render at 2x, dark theme, two operations, playhead at 1.0 s. Before (`main`): After (this PR): ## Pinning tests - `crates/sim/tests/sim_op_steps.rs` (8 tests): the value of each start from the segments (`cum[k]` of the last segment of the operation before); the kept `OpStarts` answer as the `Script` lookups; the starts in program order; next from inside operation 1 gives the start of operation 2; previous goes to the current start, then to the one before; no step past the first or the last operation; an operation with no moves is no stop; a non-finite playhead. - `crates/app/tests/sim_op_step_stock.rs` (2 tests): "next" from inside operation 1 (the next operation has another tool) gives the stock after every move of operation 1, the same picture as playback move by move; an operation with no toolpath is no stop, and the stock holds before it as in plain playback (#2280). - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/sim_op_steps.rs` (7 tests): a still frame walks no segment (the kept starts are the same `Arc`), and a document change walks the new timeline; click and keys move the playhead and pause; enabled state at the first and the last operation and while held; the tips and the AccessKit description; the shell transport has the steps and the readout names the operation. ## Readings - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 13 steps, 12 green. The red step is `ui suites: lib`, with four frame-cost tests that fail the same way on clean `main` at 6df70dfc5 ("the area preview is filled"). I filed #2762 for them. Each other `ui --lib` test passes. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. ## Not exercised - No windowed run. The screenshots are headless. - The steps do not select the operation in the browser. The decision record gives the reason. - No run on Linux or macOS. MCP: no new command. The playhead is view state, not a document command. ## Heavy lanes `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on the final head 7cdb8b8d9 (#2568). The change in `crates/sim` reaches each heavy target of `motion` and `app`. - Lanes that ran: `motion heavy` (34 steps, each target) and `app heavy` (199 steps, each target), after one release build. 234 steps in total. Wall time 40.3 min, on Windows x86_64. - Result: 233 steps ok, 1 failed. - The failed step is `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`, test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`. It gets the triple (3158, 3130, 1141), the Windows triple of the bore. This PR does not cause it: the branch base does not have the Windows pin of upstream commit 01e74d74c ("pin Windows x86_64 bore counts for the solidcore mesh"). The same test with the same triple is red on `main` at acd5b02d3 on this machine. The merge of `main` at the cut brings the pin. This PR changes no adaptive or pocket code. - The known-fail steps are red as expected: #1950 (2 steps in `motion heavy`, 1 in `app heavy`), #2845 and #2849. - The earlier run on 235201581: 217 steps, all ok. Changelog: The simulation has Previous op and Next op steps (Page Up / Page Down) that pause at the start of an operation with the stock that the earlier operations leave (#2608) Fixes #2608 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(2d): Slot Undercut for T-slot, keyseat, dovetail and lollipop cutters
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the Slot Undercut operation and the cutters for it.

- **Four cutter kinds** in `camcraft-tools`: `t_slot`, `keyseat`, `dovetail`, `lollipop`. They use the existing tool fields. `diameter` is the head. `flute_len` is the head height. `shank_d` and `shank_len` are the neck. `tip_angle` is the dovetail flank angle. The kind words are additive, so `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change. The starter catalog has one cutter of each kind.
- **One generator** in `camcraft-motion` (`machining2d::undercut`). It cuts a straight slot or a circular slot (DXF-style bulge). It changes Z at one XY station only, outside the wall. It feeds in sideways, cuts the centre pass and the radial stepover passes at one depth, feeds out the same way, then lifts. The pass offset comes from the widest point of the cutter profile, not from the tip.
- **One verify law** in `camcraft-sim` (`Mode::Undercut`, `verify/undercut.rs`). A move that changes Z while material is in or over the head is `Warning::UndercutLift`. It blocks the post. A neck or holder band with material above its bottom is a `ShankHit`. The operation layer reads the two again against the stock that the earlier operations left (`acquit_undercut_by_prior`). A neck slot that an earlier Slot operation cut is then air.
- **The true profile in the solid law.** The solid law judges a dovetail as a frustum and a lollipop as a full ball (`Prof::Dove`, `Prof::Ball`). The head top gets the same allowance as the tip, so a head that stands under its roof is contact and not a gouge.
- **The true profile in the field stock simulation** (`Stock::simulate_undercut`, `Stock::with_partial_undercut`, `SdfTool::Dovetail`). The head and the neck are two convex solids. The field keeps their union. Both the stock view and Simulate playback cut the head and neck with it. Notice `cut_twin_work::twin_tool` maps `SdfTool::Dovetail` to `"dovetail"`.
- **The column engines cut nothing for an undercut.** A column has one top for each (x, y). It cannot hold air below material.
- **App**: `OpParams::SlotUndercut` (kind tag 44, appended), the project file mirror (keeping `0.0` `bulge` and `neck_slot` keys in JSON), the stamp digest, heights, the part solid law for a part source, and the kept-parts law for both stock and part sources.
- **MCP**: `add_operation` with kind `Slot Undercut` (key `slot_undercut`) and `add_tool` with the new kind words. `verify` reports the new finding kind `undercut_lift`. `list_operation_types` and `edit_operation` include `bulge` and `neck_slot` when they equal `0.0`.
- **UI**: the four undercut kinds in the tool editor (`tool_undercut_row.rs` seeds valid defaults, `Flank angle (deg)` / `flank angle °` edits `ToolKind::Dovetail`, and `Corner radius` stays hidden for undercut kinds), the Slot Undercut page (`undercut_page.rs`), and five original icons (SVG masters rendered with `cargo xtask icons`).
- **Docs**: a Slot Undercut section in the 2D operations guide, and `docs/decisions/1444-slot-undercut.md`.

## UI screenshots

Before/after renders from the headless `ShellUi` (`1440x960` WGPU) on `upstream/main` (`5ed5b7fe2`) and this PR branch (images stored on `mkinney/Camcraft` `pr-screenshots` commit `0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86`):

| View | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tool editor (`DT-20-60` dovetail cutter) | ![Tool editor before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-before.png) | ![Tool editor after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-after.png) |
| Slot Undercut page (`TSlot` in milling setup) | ![Slot Undercut before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-before.png) | ![Slot Undercut after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-after.png) |

## Cause

There was no cutter kind with a head wider than its neck, and no operation for one. The laws for a plain contour are wrong below a roof. The column model reads a pass as a cleared kerf, so a lift through the roof passes as a retract in its own kerf.

## Tests

New pins cover the new behaviour. Each review fix below also has a direct test and mutation check.

- `camcraft-tools --lib` (`107 passed; 0 failed`): `undercut::tests` checks sane cutters, refusals by name, the profile contact point, and the drawn outline.
- `camcraft-motion --lib` (`459 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored`): `machining2d::undercut::tests` pins single-station Z moves, entry slot refusals, concentric arc slots, profile contact offsets, and input refusals.
- `camcraft-sim --test undercut_laws` (`14 passed; 0 failed`): pins `UndercutLift`, `ShankHit`, `acquit_undercut_by_prior`, `Prof::Dove`, `Prof::Ball`, `Atom::cap`, and `Stock::simulate_undercut`.

title: feat(import): cadmpeg runner with version check and temp-dir sandbox
body:
## What changed

- `crates/app/src/geometry/import/native.rs` is new. It holds the shared qualified-extension table. The table is empty. Each native CAD extension that is not in the table is refused by name. This includes IGES and `.prt`.
- `crates/app/src/geometry/import/cadmpeg/` is new. It runs the external `cadmpeg` program and gives the STEP text to the STEP importer.
  - It uses the stated path first. If no path is stated, it searches `PATH`.
  - It requires version `0.6.12` or newer.
  - It runs `cadmpeg check --json <input>`.
  - It runs `cadmpeg convert <input> -o <out> --to step --reject-lossy=export`. It never gives `--allow-errors`.
  - The file path is one argument of the child process. No shell runs.
  - Each run uses a private folder below the temp folder. A `Drop` guard removes the folder.
  - A time limit stops the child. A 16 MiB limit applies to the output that the child prints. `MAX_FILE_BYTES` applies to the STEP file.
- `ImportModel::checked_budget` uses the table. The hardcoded `"iges" | "igs"` arm is removed.
- `ViewPrefs` has the new optional field `cadmpeg_path` (`cadmpegPath` in `camcraft-prefs/1`). The key is written only when it is set. Older files load unchanged.
- The UI keeps a stated `cadmpegPath` when it saves the preferences. No UI control sets the path. That is the work of #1876.
- The module `cadmpeg` is compiled only when the target is not `wasm32`.

No shipped import reaches the runner now, because the table is empty. #1875 adds the formats.

## Cause

This is new work for #1572. It is not a defect fix.

## Deviation from the issue

The issue asks for a `cadmpeg formats --json` probe. cadmpeg 0.6.12 does not have this option. `formats` prints a text table only. The first worker on this issue reported this.

This PR does not parse that table. The exit status of `check` and of `convert` is the capability test. A build that cannot read the format or cannot write STEP fails one of the two commands, and the import is refused with the last error line of cadmpeg. `docs/decisions/1873-cadmpeg-runner.md` records this decision and four others. The maintainer can reject it.

## Tests

New suite `crates/app/tests/cadmpeg_import.rs` (13 tests). It uses the stand-in program `testdata/stubs/cadmpeg_stub.sh`. The stub tests are `#[cfg(unix)]`.

- `unqualified_native_extensions_are_refused_by_name`
- `a_qualified_extension_routes_to_the_converter`
- `stub::a_converted_part_imports_through_the_step_importer`
- `stub::the_program_is_found_on_the_search_path_when_no_path_is_set`
- `stub::a_missing_program_is_refused_naming_cadmpeg_and_the_extension`
- `stub::an_old_version_is_refused_by_number`
- `stub::a_failed_check_is_refused_and_nothing_is_converted`
- `stub::a_blocking_finding_is_refused_even_with_exit_status_zero`
- `stub::a_hung_program_is_stopped_at_the_time_limit_and_its_folder_removed`
- `stub::a_failed_or_empty_conversion_is_refused`
- `stub::an_oversized_step_is_refused`
- `stub::output_past_the_capture_limit_stops_the_program`
- `stub::garbage_output_is_refused_by_the_step_importer`

Other pins:

- `view_prefs`: `cadmpeg_path_survives_a_restart_and_old_preferences_still_load`. The test `offline_only_survives_and_the_file_stores_zero_keys` has the new key in its key list.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `prefs_door::a_pick_keeps_the_stated_cadmpeg_path`.

Red before the change: the pins did not compile on `upstream/main` (`import::native`, `import::cadmpeg` and `ViewPrefs::cadmpeg_path` did not exist).

Mutation results. Each guard was removed, the pin was red, the guard was restored, the pin was green.

| Guard removed | Red test |
|---|---|
| `from_json` reads `cadmpegPath` | `cadmpeg_path_survives_...`, `offline_only_survives_...` |
| blank path filter in `from_json` | `cadmpeg_path_survives_...` |
| unqualified refusal in `checked_budget` | `unqualified_native_extensions_are_refused_by_name` |
| stated path must be a program file | `a_missing_program_is_refused_...` |
| minimum version | `an_old_version_is_refused_by_number` |
| `check` exit status | `a_failed_check_is_refused_...` |
| blocking findings count | `a_blocking_finding_is_refused_...` |
| report that is not JSON | `a_blocking_finding_is_refused_...` |
| time limit | `a_hung_program_is_stopped_...` |
| stop of the child at a limit | `a_hung_program_is_stopped_...` (process id check) |
| capture limit | the capture-limit test |
| STEP size limit (loop and final check) | `an_oversized_step_is_refused` |
| `convert` exit status | `a_failed_or_empty_conversion_is_refused` |
| empty output | `a_failed_or_empty_conversion_is_refused` |
| folder removal in `Drop` | 9 stub tests (folder count) |
| UI save keeps the path | `a_pick_keeps_the_stated_cadmpeg_path` |

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 44 steps, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- No real cadmpeg ran. It is not installed here. The command line comes from the public help text and README of cadmpeg 0.6.12.
- No real `check --json` report was read. The runner trusts the exit status and also scans each `findings` list for severity `error` or `blocking`.
- Windows and macOS did not run. The stub tests are Unix only.
- The `wasm32` build did not run. The target is not installed here.
- The path from `ImportModel::within` to the runner is not reached while the table is empty. The tests call `cadmpeg::load_open_within` and `native::route_in` directly.
- Only the direct child is stopped at a limit. A grandchild process is not stopped (decision 3).

## Overlaps

No open PR changes the same function.

- #2664 adds one line to the module list of `crates/app/src/geometry/import/mod.rs`. It touches the same file, different lines; whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2665 appends code to the end of `crates/app/src/prefs.rs`. It touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.

## Notes

- The MCP tool and the script verb do not change. #1877 owns them. This PR adds no command.
- The stub is committed with mode `100755`. The tests link to it, so no test writes a program file.

Changelog: An import can convert a native CAD file to STEP through the optional `cadmpeg` program (version check, private temp folder, time and size limits); no format is enabled yet, and each native extension is refused by name.

Effort: max

Fixes #1873

title: fix(motion): cut shallow blind pocket floors
body:
Takeover: the coordinator session of NeoTech refreshed this PR by the maintainer's order; the author is mkinney.

## State

PR #2149 is on `main`. This branch has merged `main` (`ee91ac3e5`), and `main` is an ancestor of the head `e047966c2`. The PR now changes only its own files:

- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/entry.rs`
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/floor_levels.rs`
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/mod.rs`
- `crates/motion/tests/blind_floor.rs`
- `docs/decisions/2088-shallow-floor-levels.md`

The PR changes no process file.

## What changed

3D Pocket now cuts a 3 mm blind hole at its floor with a 4 mm stepdown. The level planner adds flat upward floors, plus `stock_to_leave`, inside the first depth interval. The added levels obey the same material, entry, shell, mask and protected-area checks as the regular levels. The planner refuses excessive floor levels by name.

## Cause

The regular depth ladder used the levels -4, -8, -12 and -15 for the test hole. It missed the floor at -3. The material checks correctly refused every lower level, because solid material stood above it. The operation then refused with "nothing to cut".

## Where the floor levels apply

- The 3D Pocket sites get the discovered floor levels:
  - plain and offset-shell (`run_plain_with`, with the open-side and avoid variants);
  - the coarse and rest legs (`run_rest_with`);
  - trochoidal (`pocket3d_trochoidal`, through the two functions above);
  - the multi-axis rough, which follows the path of `pocket3d`.
- The rotary air-split ladder (`pocket3d_air_split`, called only by the rotary wrap) keeps the plain level law (commit `7caff3125`). In the wrap, a flat face is the turned skin of the bar, not a blind floor. A height window whose only open level is the wrap top is air and must be refused. Without this split, `rotary_offset::the_height_window_names_the_stations_and_refuses_an_empty_one` got a toolpath in an air window.

## Tests

The six tests of `crates/motion/tests/blind_floor.rs`:

- `a_blind_hole_shallower_than_one_stepdown_is_cut_at_its_floor`: the 3 mm hole at stepdown 4 is cut at one level, Z -3, for `pocket3d` and `pocket3d_offset`. No gouge, and the verify is silent.
- `a_shallow_floor_keeps_stock_allowance_and_the_top_stock_level`: with `stock_to_leave` 0.5 the level is at -2.5 and no move is below it. With stock over Top Z, the Top Z stock level stays.
- `excessive_shallow_floor_levels_are_refused_by_name`: `MAX_PASSES` added flat heights give the named refusal.
- `the_rotary_air_split_ladder_keeps_the_plain_level_law`: on the same hole, `pocket3d` cuts and `pocket3d_air_split` refuses with `GenError::Empty`.
- `a_blind_pocket_never_enters_solid_under_any_ladder`: the matrix keeps its no-gouge, no-move-under-the-floor and silent-verify asserts. It now cuts all 1152 cases. The 64 removed "nothing to cut" refusals were the cases with hole depth 3 mm, stepdown 4 mm and Bottom Z under the hole: an open blind hole that must be cut.
- `the_islands_law_shadows_a_blind_floor_all_the_way_down`: the existing islands-law test. It did not change.

Mutation checks (each one reverted after the run):

- All floor-level calls back to `cut_levels_under`: 5 of 6 `blind_floor` tests fail.
- `+ p.stock_to_leave` removed in `floor_levels.rs`: `a_shallow_floor_keeps_stock_allowance_and_the_top_stock_level` fails.
- `pocket3d_air_split` back to the floor levels: the rotary pin fails, and `rotary_offset.rs:328` fails.

## Gates (Windows x86_64, head `e047966c2`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=18`)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 38 steps, 0 failed.
- Rotary and multi-axis suites, debug, 0 failed:
  - motion: `multiaxis`, `multiaxis_avoid`, `multiaxis_rough`, `rotary`, `rotary_adaptive`, `rotary_dflat`, `rotary_links`, `rotary_offset`, `avoid_pocket`.
  - app: `blind_floor`, `center_cut_multiaxis`, `mcp_rotary_stack`, `rotary_face_selection`, `rotary_feed_cap`, `rotary_field_parity`, `rotary_letter`, `rotary_subplate`, `rotary_subplate_standing`, `rotary_verify`, `setup_align_multiaxis`.
  - sim: `verify_avoid`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 2 steps, 0 failed.
- Selected heavy steps: 17 of 18 pass. They include `golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens`, the pocket3d steps and the rotary and multi-axis steps.
- The red heavy step is `app pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`. It fails with the same triple `(3158, 3130, 1141)` on unmodified `main` `ee91ac3e5`. This PR adds no level there (Z 15, 10, 5, 0). Refs #3050

No golden changed.

## Not exercised

The other heavy steps that the diff reaches, the release gate and physical machining were not run. Floor discovery covers only exactly flat upward faces in the first depth interval.

Effort: high
Changelog: Cut shallow flat blind floors in 3D Pocket when the stepdown exceeds the hole depth.
Fixes #2088

- Recorded the design choices in `docs/decisions/1198-bar-snap-and-value.md`.

## Viewport bar screenshots

These images show the viewport pane at `2x` scale with the seeded `Block` selected. The headless GPU and egui shell render the 3D scene, the handles, the bottom bar, and the legend.

title: feat(post): add Hurco WinMax (NC) ISNC post and Hurco VM10i machine
body:
Replaces #2640 with the same Hurco commit (`4cd8bdae2`, cherry-picked unchanged) on a branch straight off `main`. #2640 was stacked on the Grbl post draft #2506, so it could not merge before #2506; this one does not need it.

## Latest review fixes

Head: `ed04216dc468f9880dea0651c813b5762c401488`.

- Finding 1: Cancel active cycles before travel. Seat each hole at the section hop before descent to R. Refuse missing hops.
- The `cycle_hop` suite includes Hurco. It checks back-to-back cycles and cycles after probing, feeds, and arcs.
- Finding 3: Set the vendor to `Camcraft`. `hurco_post_vendor_is_camcraft` pins the value.
- All 30 focused tests passed. Cycle seating, feed tracking, arc tracking, and vendor mutations failed their pins. Restored fixes passed.
- Update the synthesized Hurco golden for safe hops. Conformance passed all 7 tests.
- Clippy for `camcraft-post` and `camcraft-app`, all targets with warnings denied: passed.
- Quick gate ran 648 steps. After the golden update, only `continuous_4axis_part` remains red: `/version: 71 != 70`.
- Finding 2 remains open. No simulator access, load results, or path comparisons are available. Issue #2573 remains incomplete.

Re-checked on this branch: `camcraft-post --test script_hurco_winmax` 11 passed; `camcraft-app --test hurco_winmax_post` 7, `post_spindle_rule_all` 2, `conformance` 5 passed.

---

## What changed

- Add clean-room built-in post `Hurco WinMax (NC)` in `assets/posts/hurco-winmax.cps`.
- Add clean-room 3-axis VMC definition `Hurco VM10i` in `assets/machines/hurco-vm10i.mch`.
- Register both entries in `BUILTINS`, `MACHINES`, and `embedded()` inside `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`.
- Emit Hurco WinMax ISNC blocks (`G20`/`G21` unit block, `O0001`..`O9999`, `G90 G17 G94 G54..G59 G40 G49 G80`, `G54.1 P1`..`P93`, decimal-second `P` dwell on `G04`/`G82`/`G89`, `G84.2`/`G84.3` rigid tapping and `G84` floating tapping, `G68`/`G69` rotation, `G31` probing with `G10 L2`, no `G91.1`).
- Record design decisions in `docs/decisions/2573-hurco-winmax-post.md`.

## Cause

No built-in post processor or machine definition existed for Hurco WinMax 3-axis NC/ISO (ISNC) mills.

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `crates/post/tests/hurco_winmax_post.rs` (8/8 pass; red before fix `0/7`: `hurco-winmax.cps` missing): multi-op contour/arc/drill/peck/tap across two tools and two offsets, `G20`/`G21` and `EndUnits`, decimal-second `P` dwell, `G84.2`/`G84.3`/`G84`, `G54`..`G59` and `G54.1 P1`..`P93`, `G28`/`G53` safe retract, `O0001`..`O9999` bounds, `G41`/`G42` compensation, `G68`/`G69` rotation, `G31` probing, smoothing note, named refusals, and a strict documented WinMax ISNC word-set allowlist check over posted programs and all 21 `.nc` goldens.
  - `crates/app/tests/hurco_winmax_post.rs` (2/2 pass; red before fix `0/2`: missing registry entries): checks `BUILTINS`/`MACHINES` registration, `post_serves`, VM10i parse, full ECS contour/pocket/drill/peck/rigid-tap workflow across two tools and `G54`/`G55`, plus `G54.1 P1`.
  - Cross-post suites updated and green: `conformance` (7/7), `machine` (33/33), `machine_library` (11/11), `post_spindle_rule_all` (5/5), `bore_cycle` (9/9), `comp_plane` (3/3), `decimal_point_fanuc_family` (3/3), `declared_options` (3/3), `end_units` (3/3), `first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family` (9/9), `radius_arcs` (7/7), `script_hurco_winmax` (11/11).
- Mutations (each verified RED when reverted/weakened, GREEN when restored):
  - `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` reverted to `HEAD`: `0/1` (`hurco_winmax_post_and_vm10i_are_registered_and_serve_mill` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `oWord()` `1..=9999` check removed: `0/1` (`extended_work_offsets_and_safe_retract_and_o_word` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `workOffsetMax` raised and `> 99` guard removed: `0/1` (`extended_work_offsets_and_safe_retract_and_o_word` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `G53` missing `safeRetractZ` check removed: `0/1` (`extended_work_offsets_and_safe_retract_and_o_word` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `rigidTapping === false` check removed: `0/1` (`tapping_modes_and_rigid_tapping_guard` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - Cycle illegal dwell `rawDwell > 0` check removed: `0/1` (`cycles_refuse_illegal_dwell_and_tilt_and_zero_spindle` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `tiltOk()` 3-axis guard bypassed: `0/1` (`cycles_refuse_illegal_dwell_and_tilt_and_zero_spindle` fails), restored `1/1`.
- Gate & lint:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 643 step(s), 0 failed (57.0 min).
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: 0 warnings, exit 0.

## Goldens moved

- Added 14 new `conformance` goldens under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/hurco-winmax/*.nc` (13 ops) and `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_hurco-winmax.nc`.
- Added 11 new `script_hurco_winmax` recorded goldens under `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/hurco-winmax/` (7 `.nc`, 4 `.refusal`).
- No existing `.nc` or `.cl` goldens changed.

## Not exercised

Latest review finding 2 remains open. The required simulator load results and path comparisons are not available. Issue #2573 remains incomplete.

Programs were not verified on the community owner's WinMax `09.01.393.30` simulator or on a physical Hurco control. Behaviour follows published Hurco WinMax Mill NC documentation (`704-0116-101`, `support.hurco.com`) and public Hurco VM10i specifications.

## Overlaps

This PR branches from `main`. It touches these functions and tables:
- `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` (`BUILTINS`, `MACHINES`, `embedded`)
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` (`POSTS`, `EXTENSIONS`)
- `crates/app/tests/machine.rs` (`every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks_its_declaration`)
- `crates/app/tests/post_spindle_rule_all.rs` (`POSTS`)
- `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs` (`NO_DWELL`)
- `crates/post/tests/comp_plane.rs` (`POSTS`)
- `crates/post/tests/decimal_point_fanuc_family.rs` (`MILL_POSTS`)
- `crates/post/tests/declared_options.rs` (`shipped_milling_posts_declare_valid_option_schemas`)
- `crates/post/tests/end_units.rs` (`writing_mill_posts_emit_end_unit_word_before_program_end`)
- `crates/post/tests/first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family.rs` (`POSTS`)
- `crates/post/tests/radius_arcs.rs` (`RADIUS_POSTS`)

Open PRs `#2515` and `#2310` also touch `posting_files.rs` / `conformance.rs` / `machine.rs` and were already conflicting with `main` at Step 2.

Refs #2573

title: ci(release): run the site tests in the site job
body:
## What changed

PR #1825 added `site/tests/test_operation_reference.py`. It pins the 44 operation pictures against the `OpType` enum. Nothing ran it. The four other site tests that build the site with Zola had the same problem.

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`, job `site`: a new step `Site tests`, after `Install pinned Zola` and before `Version the site is built from`. It runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s site/tests -v` with `ZOLA: /tmp/zola` (the pinned v0.23.6 that the job already installs and checks).
  - It runs the full site suite, not only the operation reference file. This is the command that `site/README.md` already gives, and all 61 tests pass. Thus the guide navigation, image, icon and troubleshooting tests also get a run. Dropped option: one file only (`test_operation_reference.py`), which leaves the other Zola tests with no run.
  - It runs before `version.toml` exists, on the same tree as a local run.
  - No `continue-on-error`: a red site test fails the `site` job, and thus `pages` does not deploy.
- `site/README.md`: one paragraph says that the release runs the same command, and how the tests find Zola.
- No trigger, permission, runner or other job changes. `python3` is on `ubuntu-latest`.

## Tests

Pinned by `the_site_job_runs_the_site_tests_with_its_pinned_zola` (new file `xtask/tests/release_site_tests.rs`, in the same form as `xtask/tests/post_merge_concurrency.rs`). It reads the `site` job and asserts:
- the `Site tests` step comes after `Install pinned Zola`;
- it runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s site/tests -v`;
- it sets `ZOLA: /tmp/zola`;
- it has no `continue-on-error`.

Without the workflow step, the test fails with `the site job runs the site tests (#1832)`.

Readings (Linux, the pinned Zola v0.23.6, sha256 checked):
- `ZOLA=<pinned zola> python3 -m unittest discover -s site/tests`: 61 tests, OK, 11 s.
- With one picture line removed from `operations-2d.md` (`operation-paths.svg#Slot`): the suite fails, with `Slot needs its toolpath picture` among the failures. The file was restored.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): `xtask unit tests` ok (the new test ran and passed).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The workflow YAML parses (`yaml.safe_load`); the site steps start `Install pinned Zola`, `Site tests`, `Version the site is built from`.

## Not exercised

- No real `release.yml` run. The next cut (or a `workflow_dispatch` run) is the full check.
- `actionlint` is not installed on this machine.

## Notes

- The issue says that the Zola part of the test is "skippable when the binary is absent, as today". It is not: without Zola, the five Zola tests error (`FileNotFoundError`), they do not skip. This PR does not change that, because the job always has Zola. The README now says so.
- A `.github/` change from a fork: read, not built. It waits for the maintainer (`needs-maintainer`).
- `xtask/` is a process file (the new test). The PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`. A fork needs no action.
- Branch base: `upstream/main`. No context scout ran; this session did its own searches.

Process change: yes
Changelog: none
Effort: low

Fixes #1832

title: fix(ci): post-merge report job runs when the gate fails
body:
## What changed

The `report` job of `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` has `needs: gate` and an `if` with no status check function. GitHub then adds an implicit `success()`. When the gate fails, the job is skipped before GitHub reads the expression. Thus a red `main` opened no rolling issue (run 43535610115, as #1611 says).

- `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`: the `if` of the `report` job now starts with `always() &&`. The other terms do not change:
  - `needs.gate.result == 'success' || needs.gate.result == 'failure'`: a cancelled or a skipped gate still reports nothing.
  - `needs.gate.outputs.skipped != 'true'`: a run that yields to a cut still reports nothing.
  - The ref terms: a dispatch of a non-main ref still reports nothing.
- A comment on the job says why `always()` is necessary.
- No trigger, permission, runner label or step changes.

The red path after the gate already works: the gate job uploads `gate-output.txt` with `if: always()`, and `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh` reads `STATUS=failure` and the FAIL rows.

## Tests

Pinned by `a_failed_gate_still_runs_the_report_job` (new file `xtask/tests/post_merge_report.rs`, in the same form as `xtask/tests/post_merge_concurrency.rs`). It reads the workflow and asserts:
- the `if` of the `report` job starts with `${{ always() && `;
- the `success` / `failure` term and the `skipped` term are still there.

Without the workflow change, the test fails with: `the report job's if starts with always(): ${{ (needs.gate.result == ...`.

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, Linux): `xtask unit tests` ok (the new test ran and passed).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The workflow YAML parses (`yaml.safe_load`), and the `if` value is as above.

## Not exercised

- No real post-merge run. A red run on the self-hosted runner (`camcraft-post-merge`) is the full check: `report` runs and opens or comments on `main is red (post-merge gate)`, and the next green run closes it.
- `actionlint` is not installed on this machine, and did not run.

## Notes

- A `.github/` change from a fork: read, not built. It waits for the maintainer (`needs-maintainer`).
- `xtask/` is a process file (the new test). The PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`. A fork needs no action.
- Branch base: `upstream/main` `e7f5f4315`. No context scout ran; this session did its own searches.

Process change: yes
Changelog: none
Effort: low

Fixes #1611

title: feat(machine): a machine file names its post, and the Setup page offers it
body:
**What changed**

- A `.mch` file can state `controller.post`, the name of a built-in post. `Machine.post`
  holds it. A file without the key reads as before.
- The reader refuses a value that is not a non-empty string, at `controller.post`
  (`post::machine::post_name`).
- The validator also refuses a name that is not a built-in post, and a post that does not
  serve the machine's kind. The post crate gets the registry as a closure, as the holder
  lookup does (#828), so there is no new crate edge.
- `posting::post_offer` returns `Option<PostOffer>`. It offers the machine's named post
  (`OfferWhy::Machine`) when that post is in the registry, serves the mount, and is not
  the setup's post. Otherwise it gives the kind offer as before (`OfferWhy::Kind`). A
  `.cps` file post is never offered over.
- The Setup page's banner tells which offer it is: "the machine names grblHAL as its post;
  switch to it?" or the kind text as before. The button queues `SelectPostNamed`, so it
  rides undo.
- A mount never changes the post by itself (#343, #388).
- The MCP tools say the same, after the QA finding on #2374. `post_offer_for` asks for any
  setup (`posting_offer.rs`). `load_machine` replies with `post_offer` for the setup that it
  mounted to, and `get_job` gives `post_offer` for each setup: the post, why, and the
  `set_setup_post` call that takes it. `null` means no offer.
- The description of the `post` tool lists every name in `BUILTINS`. The hand-written list
  did not have "Tormach PathPilot", grblHAL, TinyG or the Carvera posts.
- 32 shipped machine files state their post, where `MACHINES`, a machine's issue or its
  post writes the pairing: the PathPilot mills, routers, lathes and plasma table, grblHAL
  and the Sienci AltMills, TinyG, the Makera machines, the Doosan DNM 5700s and the Haas
  machines. The generic machines, the Sodick ALC400G, the Mach3-era Tormach mills and the
  sinker template state none.
- The Machines pane's file editor gives a user's own machine its post. General has a Post
  row, a dropdown (`Field.choices`) of the built-in posts that serve the file's kind, plus
  "(none)", which takes the key out. A stated name off the list stays in view with its
  refusal. Only built-in posts are offered: a `.cps` file has no stable name for a machine
  file to state.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2374-machine-names-its-post.md`.

**Screenshots**

Taken by hand in the Windows release build. "Before" is a build of `main` from before this
branch; "after" is this PR's head `b6bc94239`. Same document, setup and window in each pair.
The path line under "Editing ..." is masked: it showed a local user folder.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Setup page, Post: a setup on the shipped Tormach 770MX with the Fanuc post | ![Setup Post before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/c15c4c720e0f6a3c4265d3c998afeb3ad0904e46/2554/setup-banner-before.png) | ![Setup Post after: the machine names Tormach PathPilot as its post; switch to it?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/c15c4c720e0f6a3c4265d3c998afeb3ad0904e46/2554/setup-banner-after.png) |
| Machines pane, file editor, General: a user's own grblHAL machine | ![Machines editor before: no Post row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/c15c4c720e0f6a3c4265d3c998afeb3ad0904e46/2554/machine-editor-before.png) | ![Machines editor after: a Post row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/c15c4c720e0f6a3c4265d3c998afeb3ad0904e46/2554/machine-editor-after.png) |

The Post dropdown open, after: "(none)" and the built-in posts that serve a mill.

![Machines editor after: the Post dropdown open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/c15c4c720e0f6a3c4265d3c998afeb3ad0904e46/2554/machine-editor-after-open.png)

**Readings**

Branched from `main` at `6349a542e`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 346 steps, 0 failed, on `2d26ef2a3`.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --base upstream/main`: 837 steps, 836 ok, 61.9 min. The one red step was
  `clippy -D warnings` (`bool::then` with a closure in `posting_offer.rs`), fixed in
  `a9205467b`; that step reran green with `--failed`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the head `b6bc94239`, clean tree: green,
  346 steps, 0 failed, 10.0 min.
- By hand, the release build: a setup on the grblHAL machine is offered the grblHAL post
  and the switch rides undo; a user's own machine picks its post from the editor's dropdown,
  writes it, and the Setup page then offers it.

**Pinning tests**

- `crates/app/tests/machine_library.rs`:
  `a_machine_that_names_its_post_is_offered_it_and_the_choice_rides_undo`,
  `the_named_post_must_be_a_built_in_post_that_serves_the_machine`,
  `the_editor_offers_the_built_in_posts_that_serve_the_machine`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/machine_named_post.rs`:
  `the_grblhal_machine_offers_its_own_post_and_the_switch_rides_undo`,
  `a_users_own_machine_picks_its_post_from_the_editors_dropdown`
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_machine_post.rs`:
  `mounting_the_770mx_offers_pathpilot_and_the_agent_takes_it_as_one_undo_step`,
  `the_offer_follows_the_setup_the_machine_went_to_not_the_active_one`,
  `a_machine_that_names_no_post_and_serves_the_current_one_offers_nothing`,
  `the_post_tool_lists_every_registry_post`
- `crates/post/src/machine/post_name.rs`: five unit tests for the reader and the rule.
- Not changed and still green: the lathe-over-mill-post offer test in
  `ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`, `plasma_post.rs` (only moved to `offer.post`) and
  `sinker_burn.rs`.

**Not exercised**

- By hand: a `.cps` file post on the setup is not offered over. The tests pin it.
- An older reader on a new file. `Machine` is `#[serde(default)]`, so an older reader drops
  the key and loses only the offer, never a posted line. Thus no `PROJECT_VERSION` bump.
- The pairing for machines with no written pairing. They state no post, and the kind offer
  does not change for them.
- An MCP agent on a document without setups. The `set_setup_post` refusal names
  `select_post`, which is not an MCP tool; the offer's hint says `add_setup`, then
  `set_setup_post`. The refusal text did not change here.

Changelog: A machine file can name the post that writes its programs; the Setup page and the MCP `load_machine` and `get_job` replies offer that post, the Machines editor picks it from a dropdown, the `post` tool lists every built-in post, and the shipped grblHAL, PathPilot, TinyG, Makera, Doosan and Haas machines name theirs (#2374)

title: feat(post): Mach3 Mill post for 3-axis mills
body:
## What changed

A post script for Mach3 Mill (3-axis).

- `assets/posts/mach3.cps` (new). Derived from our `grblhal.cps`. Mach3 differences:
  - Tool change: Z goes up, then `T<n> M6` on its own line, then `G43 H<n>`. Mach3 runs the user's M6Start / M6End macros at M6; the post cannot know what they do, so it lifts Z first.
  - Canned cycles G73, G81, G82, G83, G85, G86, G89 with G98. P on G82, G86 and G89. A G83 dwell is refused by name (G83 has no P word).
  - Option `dwellInMilliseconds` (off by default): P in milliseconds, for a Mach3 with "G04 Dwell param in ms" on in General Config. Off writes seconds.
  - G91.1 in the header, so arc centres never depend on Mach3's IJ-mode setting.
  - G41/G42 control compensation, G84 tapping and probing are refused by name.
- `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`: the post "Mach3" after Mach4, and its embedded copy.
- No new machine. A Mach3 user picks an existing 3-axis machine, for example "VMC 3-axis".

## Readings

- `drill_peck.nc`: `T4 M6`, `G43 H4`, then `G98`, `G73 X20 Y10 Z-24 R0 Q18 F60`, `G80`.
- Header: `G21 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G49 G80`.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/post/tests/script_mach3.rs` (new): `post_suite!("mach3.cps")` with its recorded goldens.
- `mach3` added to the shared post tables: `conformance` (with refused cases and the synth stream), `post_spindle_rule_all`, `end_units`, `declared_options`, `comment_escape`, `comp`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `after_op`, `fanuc_post`, `bore_cycle` (`SECONDS`: G86 with P in seconds) and `dwell_cycles_modal_p` (P0.5 / P0.75).
- App goldens: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/mach3/*` and `synth_mach3.nc`, written with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`.

## Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick`: 623 steps, 1 failed. The failure is `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a` (Tormach golden line count 3246 != 3245). This PR does not touch the Tormach post. It is the known red main in #2483.

- No reading on a real Mach3 control and no air cut.
- That Mach3 accepts G91.1 and P on G86 is from the "Using Mach3Mill" word list only, not tested on a control.
- The `dwellInMilliseconds` option is checked in the goldens only with its default (off).

## Decision

`docs/decisions/2482-mach3-post.md`.

title: feat(post): Grbl 1.1 post for 3-axis mills
body:
## What changed

A post script for Grbl 1.1 3-axis mills, and a machine for it.

- `assets/posts/grbl.cps` (new). Derived from our `grblhal.cps`. Grbl 1.1 has no canned cycles, no cutter radius compensation and no tool table, so:
  - Drill cycles post as G0/G1/G4 moves. The engine already sends the expanded hole moves, and the script passes them through (as `tinyg.cps` does). A dwell (P > 0) is a G4 at the hole bottom.
  - BORE and TAP are refused by name. An expanded bore needs a spindle stop before the rapid retract; a tap needs a synchronised spindle.
  - A tool change is a retract, a comment `(TOOL CHANGE - LOAD T<n> - SET Z ZERO - RESUME)` and `M0`. The first tool gets `(LOAD T<n> AND SET Z ZERO BEFORE THE START)`. No M6, no G43/G49.
  - G41/G42 control compensation is refused, as on TinyG.
  - A line is at most 79 characters (the Grbl 1.1 line buffer is 80 bytes with the terminator). A comment is cut to fit. A motion line that does not fit refuses the program.
- `assets/machines/grbl-3axis.mch` (new): a copy of `grblhal-3axis.mch`, model "Grbl 3-axis".
- `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`: the post "Grbl 1.1" after TinyG, the machine "Grbl 3-axis", and their embedded copies.

## Readings

- `drill_peck.nc`: `(LOAD T4 AND SET Z ZERO BEFORE THE START)`, then G0/G1 pecks to Z-24 and a G0 retract. No G8x word.
- Longest line over all Grbl NC goldens: 43 characters.
- Refusal goldens (`crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/grbl/*.refusal`): rotary, C-axis live tool, probe and thread hand are refused by name.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/post/tests/script_grbl.rs` (new): `post_suite!("grbl.cps")` with its recorded goldens.
- `crates/post/tests/grbl_dialect.rs` (new): every line of every Grbl golden is at most 79 characters and has none of G73, G81-G89, G98, G99, G41, G42, G43, M6, O or H words.
- `grbl` added to the shared post tables: `conformance`, `post_spindle_rule_all`, `machine`, `first_traverse_clearance`, `end_units`, `declared_options`, `expanded_bore_refusal` (new test `grbl_refuses_expanded_bore`), post and app `bore_cycle`, `comment_escape`, `comp`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `program_units`, `after_op`, `fanuc_post`.
- `first_traverse_clearance.rs`: new helper `is_tool_change` reads M6 or the two Grbl tool comments as a tool change.
- App goldens: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/grbl/*` and `synth_grbl.nc`, written with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`.

## Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick` with the worktree's own target dir: 624 steps, 1 failed. The failure is `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a` (Tormach golden line count 3246 != 3245). This PR does not touch the Tormach post. It is the known red main in #2483 (caused by #2386).

## Not exercised

- No reading on a real Grbl 1.1 control and no air cut.
- Grbl 1.1 receives G-code from a sender program. The sender's own limits are not checked.

## Decision

`docs/decisions/2481-grbl-post.md`.

Changelog: New post "Grbl 1.1" and machine "Grbl 3-axis": drill cycles as plain moves, tool change as M0, bore, tap and G41/G42 refused, lines of 79 characters or less.

Fixes #2481

title: feat(boundaries)!: add "Do not touch" face/edge protection on 2D Offset and 3D Pocket
body:
## What changed

PR #2704 merged the earlier head of this PR (`39e6c84e8`). Thus the Do not touch protection is on `main` now, with the project format at v73.

This PR now holds only the changes that are not on `main`:

- `crates/app/tests/continuous_4axis_part.rs`: the test `the_continuous_4axis_part_posts_its_wrapped_program` compares the saved project directly with the committed example. Main migrates the example through the reader first. That migration hides a stale committed example.
- `docs/decisions/2055-do-not-touch.md`: the decision entry for that comparison.

`git diff upstream/main` shows these two files only. No source file, fixture, NC golden, CL golden or PNG changes.

## Conflict refresh

Head: `51a8d34581b425b5dc057e8f3607841c7bbdd2a1`. It merges upstream main at `744c0847b04d54cfc6e3e8b24a21520c40b6bcef`.

The four conflicts take main's side:

- `crates/app/tests/do_not_touch.rs`: main moved the persistence block into `do_not_touch_project.rs`. The test `protected_project_roundtrips_and_refuses_a_future_version` holds each check of the removed block. It also adds the `v72_reader_area` checks and an MCP refusal. The literal `73` assertion is dropped. `v72_reader_area(&raw) == Err(PROJECT_VERSION)` proves the same barrier.
- `crates/app/src/project/apply.rs`: a comment. Main's text contains the text of this branch.
- `crates/app/tests/model_link.rs`: main's v72 barrier assertion.
- `crates/app/tests/sketch_project.rs`: main's v71 assertion. Only the message differs.

## Validation

All results are for head `51a8d3458`, against base `744c0847b`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. 1 step, 0 failed (`app continuous_4axis_part`).
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN. 2 steps, 0 failed. Reached lane: `app heavy: continuous_4axis_part`. This suite has no ignored test, so the lane ran 0 tests (10 filtered out). The diff reaches no motion or sim heavy lane, because the sim and motion sources are equal to `main` now.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.
- App suites that the conflicts touched, in debug:
  - `continuous_4axis_part`: 10 passed.
  - `do_not_touch`: 3 passed.
  - `do_not_touch_project`: 3 passed.
  - `model_link`: 9 passed.
  - `sketch_project`: 14 passed.
- Mutation: example version changed from 73 to 72. `the_continuous_4axis_part_posts_its_wrapped_program` fails with `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj is stale; regenerate with WRITE_GOLDEN=1: /version: 73 != 72`. Restored: 10 passed.

Main moved to `3970d3d03` after the gates. `git merge-tree` shows that this head merges with it without conflicts.

## UI review evidence

The UI change is on `main` through #2704. The images stay on the images-only branch of the fork.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: parent Boundary UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/37652ad68277c01babd8fb2996b41ed38e4cc7bd/2149/before.png) | ![After: protected rows, clearance, and viewport marks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/37652ad68277c01babd8fb2996b41ed38e4cc7bd/2149/after.png) |

## Not exercised

The full release gate, the pixel snapshots and the interactive GUI were not run. The sim, motion and UI suites were not run again, because their sources are equal to `main`.

Process change: yes
Changelog: none (the protection row shipped with #2704; this PR changes a test and a decision entry).
Fixes #2055
